Title: INTEGRATED SMART INDUSTRY 4.0-BASED DECISION SUPPORT FOR OPTIMIZING TACTICAL-OPERATIONAL DECISIONS: CASE STUDY
Authors: Bagheri H.; Ghavareshki M.H.K.; Abbasi M.; Fazlollahtabar H.
Abstract: The paper considers a model for an intelligent sales-distribution network that makes decisions related to marketing, inventory control, and pricing in the entire network. Considering the importance of staying in the competitive world, using machine learning tools is of great importance. A decision support system has been used to forecast the demand. Actual sales data is inserted into the decision support system, and then, using available evidence and past performance, a decision is made to estimate the demand. Then, an intelligent algorithm for solving the mathematical model is raised, which performs the model real-time using the data received from the decision support system and provides updated results. Sensitivity analysis was performed for validation. According to the obtained results, intelligent has a great impact on the objective function values and the use of real data helps in the network performance leading to cost reduction and lost sales. Two innovations used have not been investigated simultaneously in any of the previous studies. © (2025), (American Institute of Mathematical Sciences). All rights reserved.

Title: A decision support system to evaluate the quality and warranty policies for remanufactured products
Authors: Kuik S.; Ban J.; Diong L.; Qi X.
Abstract: Purpose: This paper proposes optimisation models to evaluate and examine the selling of extended warranty policies in terms of improved profits in producing/marketing remanufactured products. These models are numerically solved using a quadratic programming solution approach and implemented in the decision support system (DSS). Design/methodology/approach: The purpose of this paper is to develop the optimisation models for a DSS and evaluate different warranty policies for buyers. Findings: This study has demonstrated the flexibility and usefulness of a model-driven DSS for the quality and warranty management, which is applied to examine and evaluate different configurations (i.e. component reuse, rebuild and recycle) for remanufactured products and propose the selling of extended warranty policies for buyers. Research limitations/implications: The developed model-driven DSS can assist manufacturers to select and increase the number of components, e.g. to be reused, rebuilt, and recycled for producing a remanufactured product and propose suitable warranty policies for buyers. However, this study focusses only on the evaluation of warranty policies for specific remanufactured products in a DSS, i.e. types of air compressors for production operations in manufacturing industry. Originality/value: This study developed optimisation models to be used in a DSS for proposing the selling of extended warranty of a remanufactured product to improve customer satisfaction and maximise the gained profits for manufacturers. © 2022, Emerald Publishing Limited.

Os modelos são resolvidos numericamente utilizando uma abordagem de programação quadrática e implementados em um sistema de suporte à decisão (DSS). O objetivo é desenvolver modelos de otimização para um DSS e avaliar diferentes políticas de garantia para os compradores. O estudo demonstrou a flexibilidade e utilidade de um DSS orientado a modelos para a gestão de qualidade e garantia, aplicado para examinar e avaliar diferentes configurações (ou seja, reutilização de componentes, reconstrução e reciclagem) de produtos remanufaturados e propor a venda de políticas de garantia estendida para os compradores. O DSS desenvolvido pode ajudar os fabricantes a selecionar e aumentar o número de componentes a serem reutilizados, reconstruídos e reciclados para a produção de um produto remanufaturado e propor políticas de garantia adequadas para os compradores. Title: Performance evaluation for competency of bank telemarketing prediction using data mining techniques
Authors: Rashid Farooqi M.; Iqbal N.
Abstract: In today's market there is cut throat competition in the banks and struggling hard to gain competitive advantage over each other. The banking industry has undergone tremendous changes in the way business conducted. They realizes the needs and techniques of data mining which is helpful tool to gather, store, capture data and convert into knowledge. The application of data mining enhances the performance of telemarketing process in banking industry. It also provide an insight how these techniques effectively used in banking industry to make the decision making process easier and productive. This work describes a data mining approach to extract valuable knowledge and information from a bank telemarketing campaign data. At this time, the potential of five data mining methods was explored for forecasting of term deposit subscription. The presentation of these techniques was evaluated on fourteen different classifier parameters. The overall better performance achieved by J48 decision tree which reported 91.2% correctly classified with sensitivity, specificity and lowest error rate of 53.8, 95.9 and 8.8 % respectively. © BEIESP.
Keywords: Bank telemarketing; Classification; Data mining; Decision support; Direct marketing

rationale: The abstract discusses the use of data mining techniques to improve the telemarketing process in the banking industry, emphasizing the gathering and processing of data to extract valuable knowledge. This aligns with the Mechanical AI category, which focuses on data collection and automated processes. Although there are elements of decision-making and performance evaluation, the primary focus remains on data mining as a tool for data collection and analysis.
resumo: No mercado atual, a competição entre os bancos é intensa, e eles lutam para obter vantagem competitiva. A indústria bancária passou por mudanças significativas na forma como os negócios são conduzidos, reconhecendo a importância da mineração de dados como uma ferramenta útil para coletar, armazenar e transformar dados em conhecimento. A aplicação da mineração de dados melhora o desempenho do processo de telemarketing no setor bancário e oferece insights sobre como essas técnicas podem facilitar e tornar mais produtivo o processo de tomada de decisões. Este trabalho descreve uma abordagem de mineração de dados para extrair conhecimento valioso de dados de campanhas de telemarketing bancário, explorando cinco métodos de mineração de dados para prever a adesão a depósitos a prazo. A apresentação dessas técnicas foi avaliada com base em quatorze parâmetros de classificadores, com o desempenho geral melhor sendo alcançado pela árvore de decisão J48, que classificou corretamente 91,2% dos casos, com sensibilidade, especificidade e menor taxa de erro de 53,8%, 95,9% e 8,8%, respectivamente.

Title: An Adaptive Intelligent Management System of Advertising for Social Networks: A Case Study of Facebook
Authors: Aguilar J.; Garcia G.
Abstract: At present, social networks are strongly used for personal or professional purposes. The social networks have accumulated a large amount of information, which can be used in different ways. One of such possible purposes is advertising. In particular, when a company pays for advertising in a social network, it wants to get an ideal deployment of the ads on the network. The ideal behavior aims at reducing the high costs to pay, the number of hours to design advertising, the difficulty in the creation of ads by lots, among other things. In particular, the optimization of the production of advertising on social networks, based on the performance of the ads, is not an easy task. If we make an incorrect design, this can result in losses for a company. In this sense, this paper presents an intelligent system of management of social network advertising, based on data mining techniques, to automatically produce ads. In addition, we test our adaptive mechanism of automated production (generation) of online advertising on Facebook. Our system carries out automatic modifications and improvements of ads. Facebook is one of the more popular social networks, being widely used by companies for advertising, in order to create contents attracting the attention of users. © 2014 IEEE.

Title: Semiautomated identification and classification of customer complaints
Authors: Choe P.; Lehto M.R.; Shin G.-C.; Choi K.-Y.
Abstract: This paper examines the feasibility of extracting useful information from customer comments using a Naïve Bayes classifier. This was done for a database, obtained from a large Korean mobile telephone service provider, of 533 customer calls to call centers in 2009. After eliminating calls not containing customer complaints or comments, the remaining 383 comments were classified by an expert panel into four domains and 27 complaint categories. The four domains were Transaction-related (189 comments, 49%), Product-related (120 comments, 31%), Customer Service or Support-related (38 comments, 10%) and Customer Outreach and Marketing-related (36 comments, 9%). The comments were then randomly assigned to either a training set (257 cases, 67%) or test set (126 cases, 33%). The training set was used to develop a Naïve Bayes classifier that correctly predicted the domain 75% of the time and the specific subcategory 51% of the time for the test set. Prediction accuracy was strongly related to prediction strength for both sets of predictions, suggesting that simple filtering strategies where difficult to understand comments are flagged for expert review and easy comments are automatically classified are both technically feasible and likely to be practically valuable. Several strong predictors were also identified that corresponded to categories more detailed than those originally assigned. © 2012 Wiley Periodicals, Inc., A Wiley Company.

This aligns with the Mechanical AI category's focus on data collection and standardization, as it aims to automate customer comment analysis and improve the efficiency of identifying customer needs through segmentation into various domains and complaint categories.
resumo: Este artigo examina a viabilidade de extrair informações úteis a partir de comentários de clientes usando um classificador Naïve Bayes. Foi analisada uma base de dados de 533 chamadas de clientes a centros de atendimento em 2009, obtida de um grande provedor de serviços de telefonia móvel na Coreia. Após a eliminação de chamadas que não continham reclamações ou comentários, 383 comentários foram classificados por um painel de especialistas em quatro domínios e 27 categorias de reclamação. Os quatro domínios foram: Relacionados a Transações (189 comentários, 49%), Relacionados a Produtos (120 comentários, 31%), Relacionados a Atendimento ou Suporte ao Cliente (38 comentários, 10%) e Relacionados a Marketing e Alcance ao Cliente (36 comentários, 9%). Os comentários foram então distribuídos aleatoriamente em um conjunto de treinamento (257 casos, 67%) ou um conjunto de teste (126 casos, 33%). O conjunto de treinamento foi utilizado para desenvolver um classificador Naïve Bayes que previu corretamente o domínio 75% das vezes e a subcategoria específica 51% das vezes para o conjunto de teste. A precisão da previsão estava fortemente relacionada à força da previsão para ambos os conjuntos, sugerindo que estratégias simples de filtragem, onde comentários difíceis de entender são sinalizados para revisão de especialistas e comentários fáceis são classificados automaticamente, são tecnicamente viáveis e provavelmente valiosas na prática. Vários preditores fortes também foram identificados, correspondendo a categorias mais detalhadas do que aquelas originalmente atribuídas.

Title: Auction Advisor: An agent-based online-auction decision support system
Authors: Gregg D.G.; Walczak S.
Abstract: Online auctions are proving themselves as a viable alternative in the C2C and B2C marketplace. Several thousand new items are placed for auction every day and determining which items to bid on or when and where to sell an item are difficult questions to answer for online-auction participants. This paper presents a multiagent Auction Advisor system designed to collect data related to online auctions and use the data to help improve the decision making of auction participants. A simulation of applied Auction Advisor recommendations and a small research study that used subjects making real purchases at online auctions both indicate that online-auction buyers and sellers achieve tangible benefit from the current information acquired by and recommendations made by the Auction Advisor agents. © 2004 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.
Keywords: Autonomous agent; Data analysis; Decision support; Information retrieval; Online auction
rationale: The abstract discusses a multiagent Auction Advisor system that collects data related to online auctions and provides recommendations to improve decision-making for auction participants. This aligns closely with the Mechanical AI category, which focuses on data collection and automated processes to enhance market understanding and decision-making. The emphasis on improving auction outcomes through collected data and recommendations fits well within the definitions of Mechanical AI, particularly in data collection and standardization.
resumo: Os leilões online estão se mostrando uma alternativa viável no mercado C2C e B2C. Todos os dias, milhares de novos itens são colocados em leilão, e determinar quais itens licitar ou quando e onde vender um item são questões difíceis para os participantes. Este artigo apresenta um sistema de Assistente de Leilão multiagente projetado para coletar dados relacionados a leilões online e usar essas informações para ajudar a melhorar a tomada de decisão dos participantes. Uma simulação das recomendações do Assistente de Leilão e um pequeno estudo de pesquisa que envolveu sujeitos realizando compras reais em leilões online indicam que compradores e vendedores de leilões online obtêm benefícios tangíveis a partir das informações atuais adquiridas e das recomendações feitas pelos agentes do Assistente de Leilão.

Title: From decision support to decision automation: A 2020 vision
Authors: Bucklin R.E.; Lehmann D.R.; Little J.D.C.
Abstract: The authors discuss the long-run future of decision support systems in marketing. They argue that a growing proportion of marketing decisions can not only be supported but may also be automated. From a standpoint of both efficiency (e.g., management productivity) and effectiveness (e.g., resource allocation decisions), such automation is highly desirable. The authors describe how model-based automated decision-making is likely to penetrate various marketing decision-making environments and how such models can incorporate competitive dynamics. For example, the authors foresee that close to full automation can ultimately take place for many decisions about existing products in stable markets. Partial automation could characterize decision making for new products in stable markets and existing products in unstable markets.
Keywords: Automation; Competition; Decision support
rationale: The abstract discusses the automation of marketing decisions and the use of model-based automated decision-making, which aligns with the focus on efficiency and the automation of processes, fitting into the Mechanical AI category. It emphasizes how marketing decisions, especially in stable markets, can be automated, which is a core aspect of data collection and standardization in Mechanical AI.
resumo: Os autores discutem o futuro a longo prazo dos sistemas de suporte à decisão em marketing, argumentando que uma proporção crescente das decisões de marketing pode não apenas ser apoiada, mas também automatizada. Essa automação é desejável tanto do ponto de vista da eficiência (por exemplo, produtividade da gestão) quanto da eficácia (por exemplo, decisões sobre alocação de recursos). Eles descrevem como a tomada de decisão automatizada baseada em modelos deve penetrar em diversos ambientes de decisão de marketing e como esses modelos podem incorporar dinâmicas competitivas. Por exemplo, os autores preveem que a automação quase total pode ocorrer para muitas decisões sobre produtos existentes em mercados estáveis, enquanto a automação parcial pode caracterizar a tomada de decisão para novos produtos em mercados estáveis e produtos existentes em mercados instáveis.

resumo: Este artigo examina a viabilidade de extrair informações úteis a partir de comentários de clientes utilizando um classificador Naïve Bayes. Após a eliminação de chamadas que não continham reclamações ou comentários, 383 comentários foram classificados por um painel de especialistas em quatro domínios e 27 categorias de reclamação. Os quatro domínios foram: Relacionados a Transações (189 comentários, 49%), Relacionados a Produtos (120 comentários, 31%), Relacionados a Atendimento ou Suporte ao Cliente (38 comentários, 10%) e Relacionados a Contato e Marketing ao Cliente (36 comentários, 9%). Title: A decision support system to evaluate the quality and warranty policies for remanufactured products
Authors: Kuik S.; Ban J.; Diong L.; Qi X.
Abstract: Purpose: This paper proposes optimisation models to evaluate and examine the selling of extended warranty policies in terms of improved profits in producing/marketing remanufactured products. These models are numerically solved using a quadratic programming solution approach and implemented in the decision support system (DSS). Design/methodology/approach: The purpose of this paper is to develop the optimisation models for a DSS and evaluate different warranty policies for buyers. Findings: This study has demonstrated the flexibility and usefulness of a model-driven DSS for the quality and warranty management, which is applied to examine and evaluate different configurations (i.e. component reuse, rebuild and recycle) for remanufactured products and propose the selling of extended warranty policies for buyers. Research limitations/implications: The developed model-driven DSS can assist manufacturers to select and increase the number of components, e.g. to be reused, rebuilt, and recycled for producing a remanufactured product and propose suitable warranty policies for buyers. However, this study focusses only on the evaluation of warranty policies for specific remanufactured products in a DSS, i.e. types of air compressors for production operations in manufacturing industry. Originality/value: This study developed optimisation models to be used in a DSS for proposing the selling of extended warranty of a remanufactured product to improve customer satisfaction and maximise the gained profits for manufacturers. © 2022, Emerald Publishing Limited.

Title: INTEGRATED SMART INDUSTRY 4.0-BASED DECISION SUPPORT FOR OPTIMIZING TACTICAL-OPERATIONAL DECISIONS: CASE STUDY

Abstract: The paper considers a model for an intelligent sales-distribution network that makes decisions related to marketing, inventory control, and pricing in the entire network. Considering the importance of staying in the competitive world, using machine learning tools is of great importance. A decision support system has been used to forecast the demand. Actual sales data is inserted into the decision support system, and then, using available evidence and past performance, a decision is made to estimate the demand. Then, an intelligent algorithm for solving the mathematical model is raised, which performs the model real-time using the data received from the decision support system and provides updated results. Sensitivity analysis was performed for validation. According to the obtained results, intelligent has a great impact on the objective function values and the use of real data helps in the network performance leading to cost reduction and lost sales. Two innovations used have not been investigated simultaneously in any of the previous studies. © (2025), (American Institute of Mathematical Sciences). All rights reserved.

Title: Discovering recency, frequency, and monetary (RFM) sequential patterns from customers' purchasing data
Authors: Chen Y.-L.; Kuo M.-H.; Wu S.-Y.; Tang K.
Abstract: In response to the thriving development in electronic commerce (EC), many on-line retailers have developed Web-based information systems to handle enormous amounts of transactions on the Internet. These systems can automatically capture data on the browsing histories and purchasing records of individual customers. This capability has motivated the development of data-mining applications. Sequential pattern mining (SPM) is a useful data-mining method to discover customers' purchasing patterns over time. We incorporate the recency, frequency, and monetary (RFM) concept presented in the marketing literature to define the RFM sequential pattern and develop a novel algorithm for generating all RFM sequential patterns from customers' purchasing data. Using the algorithm, we propose a pattern segmentation framework to generate valuable information on customer purchasing behavior for managerial decision-making. Extensive experiments are carried out, using synthetic datasets and a transactional dataset collected by a retail chain in Taiwan, to evaluate the proposed algorithm and empirically demonstrate the benefits of using RFM sequential patterns in analyzing customers' purchasing data. © 2009 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.

Esses sistemas podem capturar automaticamente dados sobre os históricos de navegação e registros de compras dos clientes. Essa capacidade motivou o desenvolvimento de aplicações de mineração de dados. A mineração de padrões sequenciais (SPM) é um método útil para descobrir os padrões de compra dos clientes ao longo do tempo. Incorporamos o conceito de recência, frequência e valor monetário (RFM) da literatura de marketing para definir o padrão sequencial RFM e desenvolver um novo algoritmo para gerar todos os padrões sequenciais RFM a partir dos dados de compras dos clientes. Usando o algoritmo, propomos uma estrutura de segmentação de padrões para gerar informações valiosas sobre o comportamento de compra dos clientes para a tomada de decisões gerenciais. Experimentos extensivos foram realizados, utilizando conjuntos de dados sintéticos e um conjunto de dados transacionais coletados por uma rede de varejo em Taiwan, para avaliar o algoritmo proposto e demonstrar empiricamente os benefícios do uso de padrões sequenciais RFM na análise dos dados de compras dos clientes. © 2009 Elsevier B.V. Title: Predicting the success of ensemble algorithms in the banking sector
Authors: Dağ Ö.H.N.
Abstract: The banking sector, like other service sector, improves in accordance with the customer’s needs. Therefore, to know the needs of customers and to predict customer behaviors are very important for competition in the banking sector. Data mining uncovers relationships and hidden patterns in large data sets. Classification algorithms, one of the applications of data mining, is used very effectively in decision making. In this study, the c4.5 algorithm, a decision trees algorithm widely used in classification problems, is used in an integrated way with the ensemble machine learning methods in order to increase the efficiency of the algorithms. Data obtained via direct marketing campaigns from Portugal Banks was used to classify whether customers have term deposit accounts or not. Artificial Neural Networks and Support Vector Machines as Traditional Artificial Intelligence Methods and Bagging-C4.5 and Boosted-C.45 as ensemble-decision tree hybrid methods were used in classification. Bagging-C4.5 as ensemble-decision tree algorithm achieved more powerful classification success than other used algorithms. The ensemble-decision tree hybrid methods give better results than artificial neural networks and support vector machines as traditional artificial intelligence methods for this study. Este estudo utiliza o algoritmo c4.5, amplamente empregado em problemas de classificação, de maneira integrada com métodos de aprendizado de máquina em conjunto para aumentar a eficiência dos algoritmos. Dados obtidos por meio de campanhas de marketing direto de bancos em Portugal foram usados para classificar se os clientes possuem contas de depósito a prazo ou não. Redes Neurais Artificiais e Máquinas de Vetores de Suporte, como métodos tradicionais de inteligência artificial, e Bagging-C4.5 e Boosted-C.45, como métodos híbridos de árvore de decisão em conjunto, foram utilizados na classificação. O algoritmo Bagging-C4.5 alcançou um sucesso de classificação mais robusto do que os outros algoritmos utilizados. Os métodos híbridos de árvore de decisão em conjunto apresentaram melhores resultados do que redes neurais artificiais e máquinas de vetores de suporte neste estudo.

Title: Performance evaluation for competency of bank telemarketing prediction using data mining techniques
Authors: Rashid Farooqi M.; Iqbal N.
Abstract: In today's market there is cut throat competition in the banks and struggling hard to gain competitive advantage over each other. The banking industry has undergone tremendous changes in the way business conducted. They realizes the needs and techniques of data mining which is helpful tool to gather, store, capture data and convert into knowledge. The application of data mining enhances the performance of telemarketing process in banking industry. It also provide an insight how these techniques effectively used in banking industry to make the decision making process easier and productive. This work describes a data mining approach to extract valuable knowledge and information from a bank telemarketing campaign data. At this time, the potential of five data mining methods was explored for forecasting of term deposit subscription. The presentation of these techniques was evaluated on fourteen different classifier parameters. The overall better performance achieved by J48 decision tree which reported 91.2% correctly classified with sensitivity, specificity and lowest error rate of 53.8, 95.9 and 8.8 % respectively. © BEIESP.

A indústria bancária passou por mudanças significativas na forma como os negócios são conduzidos, reconhecendo a importância das técnicas de mineração de dados como ferramentas úteis para coletar, armazenar e transformar dados em conhecimento. A aplicação da mineração de dados melhora o desempenho do processo de telemarketing na indústria bancária e oferece insights sobre como essas técnicas podem ser utilizadas para facilitar e tornar mais produtivo o processo de tomada de decisões. Este trabalho descreve uma abordagem de mineração de dados para extrair conhecimento valioso de dados de campanhas de telemarketing bancário, explorando o potencial de cinco métodos de mineração de dados para prever a adesão a depósitos a prazo. A apresentação dessas técnicas foi avaliada em quatorze parâmetros de classificadores diferentes, com o desempenho geral melhor sendo alcançado pela árvore de decisão J48, que classificou corretamente 91,2% dos casos, com sensibilidade, especificidade e menor taxa de erro de 53,8%, 95,9% e 8,8%, respectivamente.

Title: Using multi decision tree technique to improving decision tree classifier
Authors: Maazouzi F.; Bahi H.
Abstract: The automatic classification systems, prediction and data mining are used in many applications (marketing, finance, customer relationship management...) using large databases. In this paper we describe a new data mining approach based on decision trees. In the proposed approach we built a multi-layer decision tree model, where each layer consists of several decision trees. The aim of the multi decision tree (MDT) is to improve decision tree classifier. The performances of MDT are compared with C4.5 decision tree algorithm and some ensemble of decision tree classifiers, namely bagging decision tree, boosting decision trees (BDT) and random forests decision tree. Results show substantial improvements when compared to these approaches. Copyright © 2012 Inderscience Enterprises Ltd.

Este estudo utiliza o algoritmo c4.5, amplamente empregado em problemas de classificação, de maneira integrada com métodos de aprendizado de máquina em conjunto para aumentar a eficiência dos algoritmos. Dados obtidos por meio de campanhas de marketing direto de bancos em Portugal foram utilizados para classificar se os clientes possuem contas de depósito a prazo ou não. Redes Neurais Artificiais e Máquinas de Vetores de Suporte, como métodos tradicionais de inteligência artificial, e Bagging-C4.5 e Boosted-C.45, como métodos híbridos de árvore de decisão em conjunto, foram utilizados na classificação. O algoritmo Bagging-C4.5 alcançou um sucesso de classificação mais robusto do que os outros algoritmos utilizados. Os métodos híbridos de árvore de decisão em conjunto apresentaram melhores resultados do que as redes neurais artificiais e as máquinas de vetores de suporte neste estudo. Title: Business interest associations in the USA and Europe: evaluation of digital marketing techniques applied on their websites and social networks
Authors: Ponzoa J.M.; Gómez A.; Arilla R.
Abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop a proprietary indicator to measure the digital presence of the institutions: the digital presence index. Design/methodology/approach: This research delves into how nonprofit institutions, specifically business interest associations (BIAs), have developed their internet presence by applying essential digital marketing techniques. To this end, and using big data mining tools, this study analyzes the tracking by internet users of 102 BIAs, with their respective websites in 36 countries in Europe and the USA. In addition, the presence and activity of the institutions included in this study on social networks are considered. Findings: This research serves as a basis for discussing the current gap between social reality and the digitalization of institutions. In this sense, conclusions are drawn on the importance of managerial profiles in decision-making on digitization and the necessary knowledge that, together with Web and social network managers, they must have to articulate the means and techniques that promote the internet presence of the organizations they manage. Originality/value: Conclusions are drawn according to the geographical scope of the BIAs, and an argument is made about the difficulties of connection and loss of prominence of this type of institutions among their different target audiences, especially among the youngest and most digitized. © 2022, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Business interest associations; Digital marketing; Digital presence index; Social networks
keywords: ['digital presence', 'digital marketing', 'internet presence', 'social networks', 'managerial profiles', 'decision-making', 'target audiences']
rationale: The study focuses on analyzing the digital presence and marketing strategies of nonprofit institutions, specifically BIAs, which aligns with market analysis and targeting. It uses big data mining tools to evaluate online user engagement and the effectiveness of digital marketing techniques, indicating a strategic understanding of market dynamics. The emphasis on decision-making by managerial profiles further supports its classification under Thinking AI.
resumo: Este estudo tem como objetivo desenvolver um indicador proprietário para medir a presença digital das instituições, denominado índice de presença digital. A pesquisa investiga como instituições sem fins lucrativos, especificamente associações de interesse empresarial (AIEs), têm desenvolvido sua presença na internet por meio da aplicação de técnicas essenciais de marketing digital. Utilizando ferramentas de mineração de big data, o estudo analisa o rastreamento por usuários da internet de 102 AIEs, com seus respectivos sites em 36 países da Europa e dos EUA, além de considerar a presença e atividade das instituições nas redes sociais. A pesquisa serve como base para discutir a lacuna atual entre a realidade social e a digitalização das instituições, destacando a importância dos perfis gerenciais na tomada de decisões sobre digitalização e o conhecimento necessário que, juntamente com os gerentes de web e redes sociais, devem ter para articular os meios e técnicas que promovem a presença na internet das organizações que gerenciam. Conclusões são apresentadas de acordo com o escopo geográfico das AIEs, argumentando sobre as dificuldades de conexão e a perda de destaque desse tipo de instituição entre seus diferentes públicos-alvo, especialmente entre os mais jovens e digitalizados.

Title: Recommender systems impact on Platform’s content and outcomes: the role of providers and algorithm designs
Authors: Mohammadi Darani M.; Aghaie S.
Abstract: Purpose: The study aims to investigate how recommender systems shape providers’ dynamics and content offerings on platforms, and to provide insights into algorithm designs for achieving better outcomes in platform design. Design/methodology/approach: This study employs a multi-agent simulation framework coupled with reinforcement learning models to examine the influence of different recommender system designs on providers’ perception of demand and platform content. Findings: The study reveals that recommender systems have the potential to introduce biases in providers’ understanding of user preferences, thereby impacting the variety of offerings on platforms. Moreover, it identifies algorithm design as a critical factor, with item-based collaborative filters showcasing superior performance in contexts where customers exhibit selectivity. Conversely, user-based models prove more effective in scenarios where recommendations significantly sway user decisions, ultimately boosting sales. Practical implications: In practical terms, these insights can guide platform developers in making informed decisions regarding the selection and implementation of recommender system algorithms. By tailoring algorithm choices to specific contexts, platforms can enhance user welfare, ultimately leading to improved platform performance and profitability. Originality/value: The findings underscore the importance of integrating provider dynamics and algorithmic biases into the design of recommender systems and platforms. This highlights avenues for future research to explore and refine our understanding of these dynamics. © 2024, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Digital marketing; Platform design; Recommender systems; Sales diversity
rationale: The abstract discusses the impact of recommender systems on providers' understanding of demand and platform content, which aligns with market analysis and targeting strategies. The findings highlight how different algorithm designs can influence user decision-making, revealing a focus on strategic analysis and personalization based on customer preferences. This indicates a clear connection to the Thinking AI category.
resumo: O objetivo do estudo é investigar como os sistemas de recomendação moldam a dinâmica dos provedores e as ofertas de conteúdo nas plataformas, além de fornecer insights sobre o design de algoritmos para alcançar melhores resultados no design de plataformas. A pesquisa utiliza uma estrutura de simulação multiagente combinada com modelos de aprendizado por reforço para examinar a influência de diferentes designs de sistemas de recomendação na percepção de demanda dos provedores e no conteúdo da plataforma. Os resultados revelam que os sistemas de recomendação podem introduzir vieses na compreensão das preferências dos usuários pelos provedores, impactando a variedade de ofertas nas plataformas. Além disso, identifica o design do algoritmo como um fator crítico, com filtros colaborativos baseados em itens apresentando desempenho superior em contextos onde os clientes demonstram seletividade. Em contrapartida, modelos baseados em usuários se mostram mais eficazes em cenários onde as recomendações influenciam significativamente as decisões dos usuários, aumentando as vendas. Em termos práticos, esses insights podem orientar os desenvolvedores de plataformas na tomada de decisões informadas sobre a seleção e implementação de algoritmos de sistemas de recomendação. Ao adaptar as escolhas de algoritmos a contextos específicos, as plataformas podem melhorar o bem-estar dos usuários, levando a um desempenho e lucratividade aprimorados. Os achados ressaltam a importância de integrar a dinâmica dos provedores e os vieses algorítmicos no design de sistemas de recomendação e plataformas, destacando caminhos para futuras pesquisas que explorem e refinam nossa compreensão dessas dinâmicas.

Title: Big-data AI analytics in value-chain innovation and international marketing strategy: insights from SMEs in cultural and creative industries
Authors: Zong, ZP; Anwar, MA; Khan, S; Asmi, F; Hussain, N
Abstract: Purpose Despite great consensus on the positive impact of big-data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) analytics (BDAI) on a firm's performance, it still appears to be a black box mechanism through which small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) strengthen their dynamic competencies to innovate and expand their global footprint. To fill this theoretical and empirical gap we examine the relationship between BDAI affordances, digital marketing capabilities (DMCs), value-chain innovation and international market goals.Design/methodology/approach The study incorporates the dynamic capability view an extension of the resource-based view and the knowledge-based view to empirically examine the primary data collected from marketing managers and executives of SMEs in cultural and creative industries utilizing Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) analysis.Findings The study highlights the significant role of BDAI affordances such as intelligent process recommendations, customer intelligence and market intelligence on DMCs, where DMCs significantly affect value-chain innovation and international market strategy both directly and indirectly.Research limitations/implications The study minimizes the gap in identifying the BDAI affordances to drive innovation and international market strategy in the context of SMEs in cultural and creative industries. Marketing managers can incorporate these findings to enhance their digital capabilities for competitive advantages in international markets.Originality/value The study proposes a holistic framework of BDAI affordances for the strategic use of digital resources and knowledge to transform digital capabilities into new forms of value to expand in the international market. These insights are robust and grounded in findings provided by marketing practitioners.
Keywords: Big-data-based AI analytics; Digital affordances; Digital marketing capabilities; Value-chain innovation; International market strategy; Cultural and creative industries
keywords: ['big-data-driven artificial intelligence', 'digital marketing capabilities', 'value-chain innovation', 'international market strategy', 'customer intelligence', 'market intelligence']
rationale: The abstract discusses the impact of big-data-driven AI analytics on the dynamic capabilities of SMEs, particularly in enhancing their digital marketing capabilities and driving innovation in the value chain. This aligns with the 'Thinking AI' category, as it focuses on strategic analysis, market analysis, and the use of insights to achieve international market goals. The elements of customer intelligence and market intelligence also suggest a focus on understanding the market environment and competitive advantages.
resumo: O estudo investiga como as análises de inteligência artificial impulsionadas por big data (BDAI) afetam o desempenho de pequenas e médias empresas (PMEs) nas indústrias culturais e criativas, focando na relação entre as oportunidades oferecidas pelo BDAI, as capacidades de marketing digital (DMCs), a inovação na cadeia de valor e os objetivos de mercado internacional. Utilizando a modelagem de equações estruturais, a pesquisa revela que as oportunidades do BDAI, como recomendações de processos inteligentes e inteligência de mercado, desempenham um papel significativo nas DMCs, que, por sua vez, influenciam a inovação na cadeia de valor e a estratégia de mercado internacional. As implicações sugerem que os gerentes de marketing podem usar esses achados para aprimorar suas capacidades digitais e obter vantagens competitivas. O estudo propõe um framework holístico para o uso estratégico de recursos digitais e conhecimento, visando transformar capacidades digitais em novas formas de valor para expansão no mercado internacional.

Title: The interplay of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data analytics in digital marketing and promotions: a review and research agenda
Authors: Basu R.; Aktar M.N.; Kumar S.
Abstract: In contemporary data-driven business environments, the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and data analytics has enabled the practice of digital marketing and promotions with incomparable efficiency. To provide insights into the current trends and future directions of research in this overlapping knowledge cluster, the present study examines 94 published journal articles to date obtained from the Scopus database. Utilizing the systematic performance analysis and review method (SPAR-4-SLR), the paper uses Excel and VOSviewer to present a bibliometric review. Following a thorough disciplinary analysis of the articles, the paper identifies five main research clusters representing the domain (i) AI and Digital Marketing (ii) Branding Automation and Engagement (iii) Optimizing E-Commerce and Social Media Marketing (iv) AI-Powered Personalized Marketing (v) Emerging Tools in Digital Marketing. In this paper, we draw on some of the key theories relevant to the field and develop an Antecedent-Decision-Outcome framework that examines the factors affecting the use of digital technologies and the benefits derived from them. Pivotal research questions are also articulated in this study to guide future inquiries in this evolving area of study. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2024.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence; Bibliometric review; Digital marketing; Digital promotions; Machine learning
keywords: ['artificial intelligence', 'digital marketing', 'machine learning', 'personalized marketing', 'e-commerce', 'branding automation', 'data analytics']
rationale: The abstract discusses the application of AI and data analytics in enhancing digital marketing efficiency, focusing on market analysis, targeting, and personalization. The identified research clusters align with the strategic analysis aspects of Thinking AI, particularly in optimizing marketing efforts and personalizing experiences based on customer data. There is no emphasis on emotional understanding or relational aspects that would indicate Feeling AI, nor does it focus solely on automated processes that would classify it as Mechanical AI.
resumo: Em ambientes de negócios contemporâneos orientados por dados, a adoção de inteligência artificial (IA), aprendizado de máquina (ML) e análise de dados possibilitou a prática de marketing digital e promoções com eficiência incomparável. Este estudo examina 94 artigos de revistas publicados até o momento, obtidos da base de dados Scopus, para fornecer insights sobre as tendências atuais e direções futuras da pesquisa nesse campo. Utilizando o método de análise de desempenho sistemático e revisão (SPAR-4-SLR), o artigo apresenta uma revisão bibliométrica por meio do Excel e VOSviewer. Após uma análise disciplinar minuciosa dos artigos, o estudo identifica cinco principais clusters de pesquisa: (i) IA e Marketing Digital, (ii) Automação de Branding e Engajamento, (iii) Otimização de E-Commerce e Marketing em Mídias Sociais, (iv) Marketing Personalizado Potencializado por IA, e (v) Ferramentas Emergentes em Marketing Digital. O artigo também aborda algumas das principais teorias relevantes para o campo e desenvolve um framework de Antecedente-Decisão-Resultado que examina os fatores que afetam o uso de tecnologias digitais e os benefícios decorrentes delas. Questões de pesquisa fundamentais são articuladas para orientar investigações futuras nesta área em evolução.

Title: The evolution of digital marketing technologies: a fuzzy TOPSIS approach to selected technology in E-commerce platform
Authors: Kumar V.; Kumar R.; Goel R.; Singh T.; Kaur M.J.
Abstract: The transition from physical market to tech markets has made business grow leaps and bounds. The stage of such revolution is not only backed by challenges but also role of varied factors influencing the extent of implementation of Digital Market Technology at both national and international levels. For few industries it can be a choice however examining the ecommerce sector the digital marketing technology reflects a significant role in effective execution of business and expansion in global world. The constant need for upgradation of product has led to the increasing importance of digital market technology. The study aims to investigate the impact of digital market technology with specific reference to Ecommerce Industry. The data is collected through the interviews convened with expertise in Digital Technology in Ecommerce. A total number of 25 experts were included in the study. Category of three decision makers were selected for further analysis. The study incorporated the robust methodology of fuzzy Topsis that involves selective judgement in determining the relative importance of digital technology in Digital Marketing in Ecommerce. These methods are well-equipped to handle imprecise and uncertain information. One of the significant advantages of these methods is their capacity to address both quantitative and qualitative criteria. The findings indicate that cloud marketing is at the top of the list, followed by big data analysis. The paper concludes by highlighting the importance of digital technology for consumers as well as for management to make strategic decisions, which is imperative for survival in the global economy. © The Author(s) under exclusive licence to The Society for Reliability Engineering, Quality and Operations Management (SREQOM), India and The Division of Operation and Maintenance, Lulea University of Technology, Sweden 2024.
Keywords: Business; Consumers; Digital marketing cyber physical; Digital technology; Electronic commerce
keywords: ['digital market technology', 'ecommerce', 'cloud marketing', 'big data analysis', 'strategic decisions']
rationale: The abstract discusses the impact of digital market technology on the ecommerce industry, emphasizing the importance of data analysis and strategic decision-making. It highlights how methodologies like fuzzy Topsis can analyze both quantitative and qualitative data, which aligns with market analysis and targeting aspects of Thinking AI. The findings focus on the role of cloud marketing and big data analysis, which are crucial for gaining competitive advantages and making informed marketing decisions.
resumo: A transição do mercado físico para os mercados tecnológicos impulsionou o crescimento dos negócios. Essa revolução é acompanhada por desafios e por diversos fatores que influenciam a implementação da Tecnologia de Mercado Digital em níveis nacional e internacional. Para algumas indústrias, pode ser uma escolha, mas no setor de e-commerce, a tecnologia de marketing digital desempenha um papel significativo na execução eficaz dos negócios e na expansão global. A necessidade constante de atualização de produtos aumentou a importância da tecnologia de mercado digital. O estudo investiga o impacto dessa tecnologia com foco na Indústria de Ecommerce, coletando dados por meio de entrevistas com 25 especialistas em Tecnologia Digital no Ecommerce. Três tomadores de decisão foram selecionados para análise adicional. A pesquisa utilizou a metodologia robusta do fuzzy Topsis, que envolve julgamento seletivo para determinar a importância relativa da tecnologia digital no Marketing Digital no Ecommerce. Esses métodos são adequados para lidar com informações imprecisas e incertas, abordando critérios quantitativos e qualitativos. Os resultados indicam que o marketing em nuvem está no topo da lista, seguido pela análise de big data. O artigo conclui ressaltando a importância da tecnologia digital para consumidores e para a gestão na tomada de decisões estratégicas, essenciais para a sobrevivência na economia global.

Title: Developing big data enabled Marketing 4.0 framework
Authors: Mukhopadhyay S.; Singh R.K.; Jain T.
Abstract: Due to the industrial revolution and, thereby with, the emergence of Industry 4.0, there has been an impact on the marketing of business firms, enabling them to digitally transform and adopt Marketing 4.0 practices supported by smart technologies. One of these is Big Data Analytics (BDA), which enables a firm to improve its marketing practices. The main objective of this study is to evaluate how integrating big data technology improves the marketing strategies of Indian FMCG companies operating in a dynamic and highly competitive market distinguished by its size and diversity, constantly changing consumer behaviour, and Marketing 4.0 trends. This study adopts a systematic approach to coding an interview with seasoned Indian FMCG professionals to explain the capabilities of Big Data in molding marketing practices. A framework is constructed based on the same. The theoretical and practical implications are discussed to visualize its applicability in business. Further, the Resource-based View (RBV) theory is discussed for describing the insights into the role and adoption of Big Data by Indian FMCG firms for enhancing performance and achieving competitiveness, along with demonstrating its benefits for decision-making, customer loyalty and internal capability assessment. © 2024 The Author(s)
Keywords: Big data analytics; Digital marketing; FMCG; Marketing 4.0; Resource based view
keywords: ['Big Data Analytics', 'marketing strategies', 'competitive market', 'consumer behaviour', 'decision-making', 'customer loyalty']
rationale: The abstract discusses how Big Data Analytics (BDA) can improve marketing strategies for Indian FMCG companies, indicating a focus on market analysis and the evaluation of marketing practices in a competitive environment. The use of BDA to enhance decision-making and customer loyalty aligns closely with the definitions and examples provided for Thinking AI, particularly in the context of market analysis and competitive advantages.
resumo: Devido à revolução industrial e ao surgimento da Indústria 4.0, houve um impacto no marketing das empresas, permitindo que elas se transformassem digitalmente e adotassem práticas de Marketing 4.0 apoiadas por tecnologias inteligentes. Uma dessas tecnologias é a Análise de Big Data (BDA), que permite que uma empresa melhore suas práticas de marketing. O principal objetivo deste estudo é avaliar como a integração da tecnologia de big data melhora as estratégias de marketing das empresas de bens de consumo rápido (FMCG) da Índia, que operam em um mercado dinâmico e altamente competitivo, caracterizado por seu tamanho e diversidade, comportamento do consumidor em constante mudança e tendências de Marketing 4.0. Este estudo adota uma abordagem sistemática para codificar uma entrevista com profissionais experientes do setor FMCG indiano, a fim de explicar as capacidades do Big Data na formação das práticas de marketing. Um framework é construído com base nisso. As implicações teóricas e práticas são discutidas para visualizar sua aplicabilidade nos negócios. Além disso, a teoria da Visão Baseada em Recursos (RBV) é discutida para descrever as percepções sobre o papel e a adoção do Big Data pelas empresas FMCG indianas para melhorar o desempenho e alcançar competitividade, além de demonstrar seus benefícios para a tomada de decisões, lealdade do cliente e avaliação de capacidades internas.

Title: The role of absorptive capacity in the use of digital marketing analytics for effective marketing decisions
Authors: Proença, M; Martins, TS
Abstract: According to the literature, companies that use consumer data from digital marketing can have better results than those that do not. However, investments in analytics have gradually declined and most research does not place the use of data in strategic processes. Thus, this paper proposes a model to evaluate the incorporation of external knowledge generated by data, with the organization's internal knowledge, through the insertion of the absorptive capacity as a mediator between the use of digital marketing data and the effectiveness of marketing decision-making. To this end, a survey of 144 Brazilian retail companies was conducted and it was found that there is mediation, but it is partial. The findings suggest some insights into actions that can be taken to improve the use of data by the organization, such as the importance of disseminating marketing data, so that it can be used strategically by decision-makers.
Keywords: Absorptive capacity; Marketing decision-making effectiveness; Digital marketing analytics; Marketing; Retail
keywords: ['consumer data', 'strategic processes', 'marketing decision-making', 'external knowledge', 'internal knowledge', 'absorptive capacity', 'effectiveness']
rationale: The abstract discusses the evaluation of how external data and internal knowledge can improve marketing decision-making, which aligns with the focus on market analysis and the strategic use of data for competitive advantages. The incorporation of absorptive capacity as a mediator suggests a sophisticated analysis of data rather than just mechanical collection or emotional understanding, which aligns it closely with the Thinking AI category.
resumo: De acordo com a literatura, empresas que utilizam dados de consumidores provenientes do marketing digital podem obter resultados melhores do que aquelas que não o fazem. No entanto, os investimentos em análises têm diminuído gradualmente e a maioria das pesquisas não considera o uso de dados em processos estratégicos. Assim, este artigo propõe um modelo para avaliar a incorporação do conhecimento externo gerado por dados, juntamente com o conhecimento interno da organização, através da inserção da capacidade absorvente como mediadora entre o uso de dados de marketing digital e a eficácia da tomada de decisões de marketing. Para isso, foi realizada uma pesquisa com 144 empresas de varejo brasileiras e constatou-se que há mediação, mas é parcial. Os achados sugerem algumas ideias sobre ações que podem ser tomadas para melhorar o uso de dados pela organização, como a importância de disseminar dados de marketing, para que possam ser utilizados estrategicamente pelos tomadores de decisão.

Title: Factors Influencing ChatGpt Adoption for Product Research and Information Retrieval
Authors: Gude V.
Abstract: In recent months, Generative AI-based systems have become increasingly prevalent for public use. Traditionally, people use Google and other search platforms to research a product before purchasing. However, with the integration of ChatGPT into Bing and Google’s announcement of BARD, these models have the potential to impact how customers search for and discover products significantly. This article aims to understand whether people will shift from traditional to Generative AI-based search engines. The research examines the factors influencing purchase decisions and the likelihood of individuals using ChatGPT instead of traditional search engines and other sources. The results indicate that gender, product knowledge, and preference for online or retail store purchases can help predict their inclination to switch to ChatGPT. The paper also discusses people’s trust in Generative AI and the influence of demographic features on their attitude toward these machine learning systems. © 2023 International Association for Computer Information Systems.
Keywords: Digital marketing; generative AI; product research
rationale: The abstract discusses the impact of Generative AI on consumer behavior, specifically how customers may shift from traditional search engines to AI-based systems like ChatGPT. This involves market analysis of consumer preferences and the factors that influence purchase decisions, aligning closely with the 'Thinking AI' category, which focuses on market analysis and targeting. The mention of demographic influences on attitudes towards AI also supports this classification.
resumo: Nos últimos meses, sistemas baseados em IA Generativa tornaram-se cada vez mais comuns para uso público. Tradicionalmente, as pessoas utilizam o Google e outras plataformas de busca para pesquisar um produto antes da compra. No entanto, com a integração do ChatGPT no Bing e o anúncio do BARD pelo Google, esses modelos têm o potencial de impactar significativamente a forma como os clientes buscam e descobrem produtos. Este artigo visa entender se as pessoas mudarão de motores de busca tradicionais para aqueles baseados em IA Generativa. A pesquisa examina os fatores que influenciam as decisões de compra e a probabilidade de indivíduos utilizarem o ChatGPT em vez de motores de busca tradicionais e outras fontes. Os resultados indicam que gênero, conhecimento sobre o produto e preferência por compras online ou em lojas físicas podem ajudar a prever a inclinação para mudar para o ChatGPT. O artigo também discute a confiança das pessoas na IA Generativa e a influência de características demográficas sobre sua atitude em relação a esses sistemas de aprendizado de máquina.

Title: Evaluating strategies for promoting retail mobile channel using a hidden Markov model
Authors: Chen J.; Rao V.R.
Abstract: With the proliferation of mobile communication technology, many firms, including retailers and consumer banks, are making efforts to develop mobile platforms to better engage with their customers and reduce operational costs. However, the cost advantage of these mobile technologies will not yield fruition unless the mobile channel accounts for a significant share of total transactions. In this article, we explore potential options for firms to promote usage of the mobile channel. To achieve this, we propose a hidden Markov model to both model customers’ decisions and assess different managerial strategies through simulations. While we apply our proposed model to data from a leading financial institution, our approach is equally applicable to other retail settings. The results show that customers’ choices of services and channels are sensitive to process time by type of channel. A 10% increase in process time through non-mobile channels leads to a nearly 14% increase in utilization of mobile banking channel. Therefore, retailing firms could potentially influence customers’ choice of different channels by changing channel-specific process times. Motivated by these findings, we present and compare performances across five different policies, in promoting the usage of mobile channel. Drawing on our simulation results, we also make personalized policy recommendations to firms facing different levels of financial constraints. For those with financial constraints, we recommend a policy of increasing process time for a selected subset of service requests through non-mobile channels. Firms not constrained by the resources might be better off improving process time with the mobile channel by targeting customers identified as having a better relationship with the firm. © 2022 New York University
Keywords: Customer relationship management; Digital marketing; Hidden Markov model; Mobile channel
keywords: ['mobile platform', 'customer engagement', 'managerial strategies', 'simulation', 'process time', 'channel utilization', 'policy recommendations']
rationale: The abstract discusses how firms can promote the usage of mobile channels by analyzing customer behavior and decision-making through a hidden Markov model. It focuses on market analysis and targeting strategies by assessing the impact of process times on customer choice of channels. This aligns closely with the Thinking AI category, which emphasizes market analysis and targeting the best strategies for customer engagement.
resumo: Com a proliferação da tecnologia de comunicação móvel, muitas empresas, incluindo varejistas e bancos, estão se esforçando para desenvolver plataformas móveis que melhorem o engajamento com os clientes e reduzam custos operacionais. No entanto, a vantagem de custo dessas tecnologias móveis não será aproveitada a menos que o canal móvel represente uma parte significativa das transações totais. Este artigo explora opções potenciais para as empresas promoverem o uso do canal móvel. Propomos um modelo oculto de Markov para modelar as decisões dos clientes e avaliar diferentes estratégias gerenciais por meio de simulações. Embora apliquemos nosso modelo a dados de uma instituição financeira líder, nossa abordagem é igualmente aplicável a outros ambientes de varejo. Os resultados mostram que as escolhas dos clientes por serviços e canais são sensíveis ao tempo de processamento por tipo de canal. Um aumento de 10% no tempo de processamento através de canais não móveis leva a um aumento de quase 14% na utilização do canal de banco móvel. Portanto, as empresas de varejo poderiam influenciar a escolha dos clientes por diferentes canais alterando os tempos de processamento específicos de cada canal. Motivados por essas descobertas, apresentamos e comparamos desempenhos em cinco políticas diferentes para promover o uso do canal móvel. Com base em nossos resultados de simulação, também fazemos recomendações de políticas personalizadas para empresas que enfrentam diferentes níveis de restrições financeiras. Para aquelas com restrições financeiras, recomendamos uma política de aumento do tempo de processamento para um subconjunto selecionado de solicitações de serviço através de canais não móveis. Empresas que não estão limitadas por recursos podem se beneficiar mais ao melhorar o tempo de processamento no canal móvel, direcionando-se a clientes identificados como tendo um melhor relacionamento com a empresa.

Title: “Hacking marketing”: how do firms develop marketers' expertise and practices in a digital era?
Authors: Hafezieh N.; Pollock N.; Ryan A.
Abstract: Purpose: Digital technologies, digitalised consumers and the torrent of customer data have been transforming marketing practice. In discussing such trends, existing research has either focussed on the skills marketers need or broad-based approaches such as agile methods but has given less consideration to just how such skills or approaches might be developed and used in marketers' day-to-day activities and in the organisation of marketing in the firm. This is what the authors address in this paper. Design/methodology/approach: This paper adopts an in-depth case study approach to examine an exemplary digital enterprise in transformation of their digital marketing. The insights were gathered from 25 interviews, netnography and document analysis of the case organisation in addition to 10 interviews with independent experts. Findings: Drawing on practice-oriented approach, the authors show how organisations respond to the emerging trends of digital consumers and big data by taking a ‘hacking marketing’ approach and developing novel marketing expertise at disciplinary boundaries. The authors put forward three sets of practices that enable and shape the hacking marketing approach. These include spanning the expertise boundary, making value measurable and experimenting through which their adaptive, iterative and multidisciplinary work occurs. This explains how managing digital consumers and big data is not within the realm of information technology (IT) functions but marketing and how marketing professionals are changing their practice and moving their disciplinary boundaries. Practical implications: This study offers practical contributions for firms in terms of identifying new work practices and expertise that marketing specialists need in managing digital platforms, digitalised consumers and big data. This study’s results show that enterprises need to design and implement strong training programmes to prepare their marketing workforce in adopting experimentations of agile approach and data-driven decision making. In addition, Marketing education should be changed so that programmes consider a review of their courses and include the novel marketing models and approaches into their curriculum. Originality/value: This study contributes to the nascent discussions by unpacking how enterprises can develop new marketing expertise and practices beyond skillsets and how such practices form new hacking marketing approach which addresses the problem of the inability of the conventional marketing approach to show its value within the firm. © 2023, Emerald Publishing Limited.

Title: Machine learning and AI in marketing – Connecting computing power to human insights
Authors: Ma L.; Sun B.
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents driven by machine learning algorithms are rapidly transforming the business world, generating heightened interest from researchers. In this paper, we review and call for marketing research to leverage machine learning methods. We provide an overview of common machine learning tasks and methods, and compare them with statistical and econometric methods that marketing researchers traditionally use. We argue that machine learning methods can process large-scale and unstructured data, and have flexible model structures that yield strong predictive performance. Meanwhile, such methods may lack model transparency and interpretability. We discuss salient AI-driven industry trends and practices, and review the still nascent academic marketing literature which uses machine learning methods. More importantly, we present a unified conceptual framework and a multi-faceted research agenda. From five key aspects of empirical marketing research: method, data, usage, issue, and theory, we propose a number of research priorities, including extending machine learning methods and using them as core components in marketing research, using the methods to extract insights from large-scale unstructured, tracking, and network data, using them in transparent fashions for descriptive, causal, and prescriptive analyses, using them to map out customer purchase journeys and develop decision-support capabilities, and connecting the methods to human insights and marketing theories. Opportunities abound for machine learning methods in marketing, and we hope our multi-faceted research agenda will inspire more work in this exciting area. © 2020 Elsevier B.V.

resumo: Agentes de inteligência artificial (IA) impulsionados por algoritmos de aprendizado de máquina estão transformando rapidamente o mundo dos negócios, gerando um interesse crescente entre os pesquisadores. Este artigo revisa e propõe que a pesquisa em marketing aproveite os métodos de aprendizado de máquina. Apresentamos uma visão geral das tarefas e métodos comuns de aprendizado de máquina, comparando-os com métodos estatísticos e econométricos tradicionalmente utilizados por pesquisadores de marketing. Argumentamos que os métodos de aprendizado de máquina podem processar dados em larga escala e não estruturados, possuindo estruturas de modelo flexíveis que oferecem forte desempenho preditivo. No entanto, esses métodos podem carecer de transparência e interpretabilidade. Discutimos tendências e práticas relevantes impulsionadas por IA na indústria e revisamos a literatura acadêmica de marketing, ainda em desenvolvimento, que utiliza métodos de aprendizado de máquina. Mais importante, apresentamos uma estrutura conceitual unificada e uma agenda de pesquisa multifacetada. A partir de cinco aspectos-chave da pesquisa empírica em marketing: método, dados, uso, questões e teoria, propomos várias prioridades de pesquisa, incluindo a extensão dos métodos de aprendizado de máquina e seu uso como componentes centrais na pesquisa em marketing, a extração de insights a partir de dados não estruturados, de rastreamento e de rede em larga escala, a utilização dos métodos de forma transparente para análises descritivas, causais e prescritivas, o mapeamento das jornadas de compra dos clientes e o desenvolvimento de capacidades de suporte à decisão, além de conectar os métodos a insights humanos e teorias de marketing. Title: Evaluation and decision making in social media marketing
Authors: Keegan B.J.; Rowley J.
Abstract: Purpose: As organisations are increasing their investment in social media marketing (SMM), evaluation of such techniques is becoming increasingly important. The purpose of this paper is to contribute to knowledge regarding SMM strategy by developing a stage model of SMM evaluation and uncovering the challenges in this process. Design/methodology/approach: Interviews were conducted with 18 key informants working for specialist SMM agencies. Such informants are a particularly rich source, since they manage social media campaigns for a wide range of clients. An exploratory research was conducted and thematic analysis surfaced the key components of the SMM evaluation process and associated challenges. Findings: The SMM evaluation framework is developed. This framework has the following six stages: setting evaluation objectives, identifying key performance indicators (KPIs), identifying metrics, data collection and analysis, report generation and management decision making. Challenges associated with each stage of the framework are identified, and discussed with a view to better understanding decision making associated with social media strategies. Two key challenges are the agency-client relationship and the available social analytics tools. Originality/value: Despite an increasing body of research on social media objectives, KPIs and metrics, no previous study has explored how these components are embedded in a marketing campaign planning process. The paper also offers insights in the factors that make SMM evaluation complex and challenging. Recommendations for further research and practice are offered. © 2017, © Emerald Publishing Limited.

Foram realizadas entrevistas com 18 informantes-chave de agências especializadas em SMM, que gerenciam campanhas de mídia social para diversos clientes. A pesquisa exploratória e a análise temática revelaram os componentes principais do processo de avaliação de SMM e os desafios associados. Um framework de avaliação de SMM foi desenvolvido, composto por seis etapas: definição de objetivos de avaliação, identificação de indicadores-chave de desempenho (KPIs), identificação de métricas, coleta e análise de dados, geração de relatórios e tomada de decisões gerenciais. Os desafios relacionados a cada etapa do framework foram identificados, destacando a relação agência-cliente e as ferramentas de análise social disponíveis. Apesar do crescente volume de pesquisas sobre objetivos, KPIs e métricas de mídia social, nenhum estudo anterior explorou como esses componentes estão integrados no processo de planejamento de campanhas de marketing. O artigo também oferece insights sobre os fatores que tornam a avaliação de SMM complexa e desafiadora, além de recomendações para futuras pesquisas e práticas.

Title: Consumer decisions with artificially intelligent voice assistants
Authors: Dellaert B.G.C.; Shu S.B.; Arentze T.A.; Baker T.; Diehl K.; Donkers B.; Fast N.J.; Häubl G.; Johnson H.; Karmarkar U.R.; Oppewal H.; Schmitt B.H.; Schroeder J.; Spiller S.A.; Steffel M.
Abstract: Consumers are widely adopting Artificially Intelligent Voice Assistants (AIVAs). AIVAs now handle many different everyday tasks and are also increasingly assisting consumers with purchasing decisions, making AIVAs a rich topic for marketing researchers. We develop a series of propositions regarding how consumer decision-making processes may change when moved from traditional online purchase environments to AI-powered voice-based dialogs, in the hopes of encouraging further academic thinking and research in this rapidly developing, high impact area of consumer-firm interaction. We also provide suggestions for marketing managers and policymakers on points to pay attention to when they respond to the proposed effects of AIVAs on consumer decisions. © 2020, The Author(s).

Title: Why strategy is key for successful social media sales
Authors: Lindsey-Mullikin J.; Borin N.
Abstract: Many successful companies spend substantial time and effort engaging with potential consumers on social media sites. They determine how consumers spend their time online and develop interesting content to increase awareness and enjoyment of the brand—often only to lose those potential customers because the purchase process becomes too difficult once consumers have decided to buy the product. New technology recently introduced by third-party vendors allows companies to offer a sales option directly on social media websites such as Facebook and Instagram. In this article, we present the effects on the consumer decision process created by the ‘Buy Now’ option across the consideration, evaluation, purchase, and post-purchase stages. We compare and contrast three distinct decision models: (1) traditional media only, (2) traditional media and social media with only a communication capability, and (3) traditional media and social media with the added function of immediate purchase. We argue that though the possibility of buying on social media will decrease the number of brands considered and evaluated, the number of purchases and amount of brand advocacy will increase significantly due to the ease of purchase. We conclude with some recommendations on future research. © 2017 Kelley School of Business, Indiana University

resumo: Muitas empresas de sucesso dedicam tempo e esforço consideráveis para se envolver com consumidores em redes sociais. Elas analisam como os consumidores utilizam seu tempo online e desenvolvem conteúdo interessante para aumentar a conscientização e o prazer com a marca, muitas vezes perdendo esses potenciais clientes devido à dificuldade do processo de compra. Novas tecnologias introduzidas por fornecedores de terceiros permitem que as empresas ofereçam opções de venda diretamente em sites de redes sociais como Facebook e Instagram. Este artigo apresenta os efeitos da opção 'Comprar Agora' no processo de decisão do consumidor nas etapas de consideração, avaliação, compra e pós-compra. Comparamos três modelos de decisão distintos: (1) apenas mídia tradicional, (2) mídia tradicional e mídia social com apenas capacidade de comunicação, e (3) mídia tradicional e mídia social com a função adicional de compra imediata. Argumentamos que, embora a possibilidade de comprar em redes sociais diminua o número de marcas consideradas e avaliadas, o número de compras e a quantidade de defesa da marca aumentarão significativamente devido à facilidade de compra. Concluímos com algumas recomendações para pesquisas futuras.

Title: Data-driven marketing for growth and profitability
Authors: Grandhi B.; Patwa N.; Saleem K.
Abstract: Purpose: In the current business environment, more uncertain than ever before, understanding consumer behavior is an integral part of an organization's strategic planning and execution process. It is the key driver for becoming a market leader. Therefore, it is important that all processes in business are customer centric. Marketers need to harness big data by engaging in data driven-marketing (DDM) to help organizations choose the “right” customers, to “keep” and “grow” them and to sustain “growth” and “profitability”. This research examines DDM adoption practices and how companies can aim to enhance shareholder value by bringing about “customer centricity”. Design/methodology/approach: An online survey conducted in 2016 received 180 responses from junior, middle and senior executives. Of the total responses, 26% were from senior management, 39% from middle management and the remaining 35% from junior management. Industries represented in the survey included retail, BFSI, healthcare and government, automobile, telecommunication, transport and logistics and IT. Other industries represented were aviation, marketing research and consulting, hospitality, advertising and media and human resource. Findings: Success of DDM depends upon how well an organization embraces the practice. The first and foremost indicator of an organization's commitment is the extent of resources invested for DDM. Respondents were divided into four categories; Laggards, Dabblers, Contenders and Leaders based on their “current level of investments” and “willingness to enhance investments” soon. Research limitations/implications: With storming digital age and the development of analytics, the process of decision-making has gained significant importance. Judgment and intuition too are critical to the process. Choosing an appropriate action cannot be done strictly on a rational basis. Practical implications: The results of the study offer interesting implications for managing the growing sea of data. An iterative and incremental approach is the need of the hour, even if it has to start with baby steps, to invest in and reap the fruits of DDM. The intention to use any system is always dependent on two primary belief factors: perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use; however, attitudes and social factors are equally important. Originality/value: There is a dearth of knowledge with regards to who is and is not adopting DDM, and how best big data can be harnessed for enhancing effectiveness and efficiency of marketing budget. It is, therefore, imperative to build a knowledge base on DDM practices, challenges and opportunities. Better use of data can help companies enhance shareholder value by bringing about “customer centricity”. © 2020, Emerald Publishing Limited.

A pesquisa, realizada por meio de uma pesquisa online em 2016 com 180 executivos de diferentes níveis, revela que o sucesso do DDM depende do comprometimento da organização e dos recursos investidos.
