Title: The transition from traditional to digital marketing: a study of the evolution of e-marketing in the Indian hotel industry
Authors: Kapoor R.; Kapoor K.
Abstract: Purpose: The study aims at analyzing the adoption and preference of E-Marketing tools in five-star hotels in India. This paper also explores the scope of artificial intelligence and the challenges with regards to its application. Design/methodology/approach: A qualitative approach is adopted for this research, wherein the data has been collected through conducting one on one telephonic interviews (some in questionnaire format) and a roundtable conference with the general managers and marketing communication managers of 30 New Delhi/National Capital Region (NCR) hotels respectively to understand the transition from traditional to digital marketing era and how are they using various social media marketing tools. Findings: This study aims to inform how digitalization has benefitted the industry in various aspects and its comparison to the traditional marketing methods. It also discovers the future of artificial intelligence in the Indian hospitality space. Practical implications: This study aims to help managerial decision-making in the application of various E-marketing tools and strategies, suggesting the right mix of both traditional and digital marketing platforms. Originality/value: Arguably this is one of a kind study, as there has been no such research done specifically aiming at the five-star hotels of the Indian market. The findings will help the industry explore and enhance their digital presence by suggesting the appropriate mix of both traditional and digital approaches and can be used as a good source for further exploring the perspective of digitalization by academicians as well. © 2021, Emerald Publishing Limited.

Title: Inventory competition, artificial intelligence, and quality improvement decisions in supply chains with digital marketing
Authors: Salhab H.A.; Allahham M.; Abu-Alsondos I.A.; Frangieh R.H.; Alkhwaldi A.F.; Ali B.J.A.
Abstract: This research examines the synergistic influence of inventory competition, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, and digital marketing intensity on quality improvement decisions within contemporary supply chains. With a focus on enhancing product and service quality, we investigate the intricate relationships among these variables. A quantitative approach involving 380 supply chain professionals reveals that heightened inventory competition, increased AI adoption, and robust digital marketing significantly contribute to quality enhancement initiatives. The study builds upon prior research by empirically validating these connections and offers practical insights for supply chain practitioners. The findings underscore the strategic imperative of organizations to strategically balance these factors to optimize their quality management strategies, fostering customer satisfaction and competitiveness. While offering valuable contributions, the study acknowledges limitations in terms of self-reported data and a specific respondent group. Future research could extend this investigation to diverse industries and geographical contexts. In the end, this study sheds light on the complex interplay that exists between inventory competition, the use of AI, digital marketing, and judgments about quality improvement. As a result, a road map has been provided for efficient quality management of supply chains in the digital age. © 2023 Growing Science Ltd. All rights reserved.

resumo: Esta pesquisa examina a influência sinérgica da competição de inventário, adoção de inteligência artificial (IA) e intensidade de marketing digital nas decisões de melhoria da qualidade dentro das cadeias de suprimento contemporâneas. Com foco na melhoria da qualidade de produtos e serviços, investigamos as relações complexas entre essas variáveis. Uma abordagem quantitativa envolvendo 380 profissionais de cadeias de suprimento revela que a competição de inventário elevada, a adoção crescente de IA e um marketing digital robusto contribuem significativamente para iniciativas de melhoria da qualidade. O estudo baseia-se em pesquisas anteriores, validando empiricamente essas conexões e oferecendo insights práticos para profissionais da cadeia de suprimento. Os resultados ressaltam a necessidade estratégica das organizações de equilibrar esses fatores para otimizar suas estratégias de gestão da qualidade, promovendo satisfação do cliente e competitividade. Embora ofereça contribuições valiosas, o estudo reconhece limitações em relação a dados autorrelatados e a um grupo específico de respondentes. Pesquisas futuras poderiam expandir essa investigação para diversas indústrias e contextos geográficos. No final, este estudo ilumina a complexa interação entre competição de inventário, uso de IA, marketing digital e julgamentos sobre melhoria da qualidade, fornecendo um roteiro para a gestão eficiente da qualidade nas cadeias de suprimento na era digital. © 2023 Growing Science Ltd. Title: Transition from traditional to digital marketing: a study of evolution of E-marketing in the Indian hotel industry
Authors: Kapoor, R; Kapoor, K
Abstract: Purpose The study aims at analyzing the adoption and preference of E-Marketing tools in five-star hotels in India. This paper also explores the scope of artificial intelligence and the challenges with regards to its application. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative approach is adopted for this research, wherein the data has been collected through conducting one on one telephonic interviews (some in questionnaire format) and a roundtable conference with the general managers and marketing communication managers of 30 New Delhi/National Capital Region (NCR) hotels respectively to understand the transition from traditional to digital marketing era and how are they using various social media marketing tools. Findings This study aims to inform how digitalization has benefitted the industry in various aspects and its comparison to the traditional marketing methods. It also discovers the future of artificial intelligence in the Indian hospitality space. Practical implications This study aims to help managerial decision-making in the application of various E-marketing tools and strategies, suggesting the right mix of both traditional and digital marketing platforms. Originality/value Arguably this is one of a kind study, as there has been no such research done specifically aiming at the five-star hotels of the Indian market. The findings will help the industry explore and enhance their digital presence by suggesting the appropriate mix of both traditional and digital approaches and can be used as a good source for further exploring the perspective of digitalization by academicians as well.

resumo: O objetivo do estudo é analisar a adoção e preferência por ferramentas de E-Marketing em hotéis cinco estrelas na Índia, além de explorar o potencial da inteligência artificial e os desafios relacionados à sua aplicação. A pesquisa adotou uma abordagem qualitativa, coletando dados por meio de entrevistas telefônicas individuais e uma conferência com gerentes gerais e gerentes de comunicação de marketing de 30 hotéis na região de Nova Délhi. Os resultados mostram como a digitalização beneficiou a indústria em vários aspectos e sua comparação com métodos de marketing tradicionais, além de investigar o futuro da inteligência artificial no setor de hospitalidade indiano. O estudo visa auxiliar na tomada de decisões gerenciais sobre a aplicação de diversas ferramentas e estratégias de E-Marketing, sugerindo a combinação adequada de plataformas de marketing tradicionais e digitais. Este estudo é único, pois não há pesquisas anteriores focadas especificamente nos hotéis cinco estrelas do mercado indiano, e suas descobertas podem ajudar a indústria a explorar e melhorar sua presença digital.

Title: Do conversational platforms represent the next big digital marketing opportunity?
Authors: Copulsky J.
Abstract: This paper examines the evolution of conversational platforms. Over the next three to five years, the technology will likely evolve rapidly, allowing conversational platforms to move beyond established customer service use cases to applications that facilitate more informed customer decision-making and create more immersive brand engagement experiences. Marketers will need to sort through the legal, regulatory and brand trust issues associated with the Big Data generated by conversational platforms, as well as integrate conversational platforms into their user experience roadmap, data strategies and marketing technology stack. © Henry Stewart Publications.

resumo: Este artigo examina a evolução das plataformas de conversação. Nos próximos três a cinco anos, a tecnologia deve evoluir rapidamente, permitindo que as plataformas de conversação vão além dos casos de uso estabelecidos em atendimento ao cliente, para aplicações que facilitem uma tomada de decisão mais informada por parte dos clientes e criem experiências de engajamento de marca mais imersivas. Os profissionais de marketing precisarão lidar com questões legais, regulatórias e de confiança da marca associadas ao Big Data gerado pelas plataformas de conversação, além de integrar essas plataformas em seu roteiro de experiência do usuário, estratégias de dados e pilha de tecnologia de marketing. © Henry Stewart Publications.

Title: A high-performance turnkey system for customer lifetime value prediction in retail brands: Forthcoming in quantitative marketing and economics
Authors: Yan Y.; Resnick N.
Abstract: Customer lifetime value (CLV) modeling underpins modern marketing analytics, enabling the development of tailored customer relationship management strategies based on the predicted future value of their customers. As part of Amperity’s enterprise customer data platform (CDP), we deploy and maintain a CLV prediction system that caters to a rapidly growing list of brands across various industries, purchase behaviors, and scales. Given the impracticality of developing bespoke models for each brand, our solution must be adaptive, generalizable, and high-performing ”out of the box”. Furthermore, our platform demands daily prediction updates to facilitate prompt marketing decisions. This paper introduces a turnkey CLV prediction system that achieves state-of-the-art performance across a diverse set of brands. This system has several contributions: 1) the use of encodings and embeddings to incorporate signals from high-cardinality data; 2) a multi-stage churn-CLV modeling framework that augments additional flexibility in adjusting churn probabilities, subsequently reducing CLV prediction errors while maintaining a synergistic learning process; 3) a feature-weighted ensemble of both generative and discriminative models to accommodate diverse underlying purchase patterns. Empirical results show that our enhanced model consistently surpasses benchmark performances for twelve retail brands across six evaluation intervals from June 2020 to September 2022. © The Author(s) 2023. corrected publication 2023.
Keywords: Churn prediction; Customer data platform; Customer lifetime value; Ensemble modeling; M31; Marketing analytics
keywords: ['customer lifetime value', 'CLV prediction', 'marketing decisions', 'predictive modeling', 'customer relationship management', 'purchase behaviors']
rationale: The abstract focuses on a CLV prediction system that enhances marketing analytics for brands by providing tailored customer relationship strategies based on predicted future values. This aligns closely with the 'Thinking AI' category, specifically in market analysis and targeting, as it utilizes predictive modeling and analytics to inform marketing decisions. The use of diverse models and frameworks to improve predictions further supports strategic analysis.
resumo: O modelo de valor do tempo de vida do cliente (CLV) é fundamental para a análise de marketing moderna, permitindo o desenvolvimento de estratégias de gestão de relacionamento com o cliente personalizadas com base no valor futuro previsto dos clientes. Como parte da plataforma de dados de clientes (CDP) da Amperity, implementamos e mantemos um sistema de previsão de CLV que atende a uma lista em rápido crescimento de marcas em diversas indústrias, comportamentos de compra e escalas. Dada a impraticabilidade de desenvolver modelos sob medida para cada marca, nossa solução deve ser adaptável, generalizável e de alto desempenho "pronta para uso". Além disso, nossa plataforma exige atualizações diárias de previsões para facilitar decisões de marketing rápidas. Este artigo apresenta um sistema de previsão de CLV que alcança desempenho de ponta em um conjunto diversificado de marcas. Este sistema possui várias contribuições: 1) o uso de codificações e embeddings para incorporar sinais de dados de alta cardinalidade; 2) uma estrutura de modelagem de churn-CLV em múltiplas etapas que aumenta a flexibilidade na ajustação das probabilidades de churn, reduzindo assim os erros de previsão de CLV enquanto mantém um processo de aprendizado sinérgico; 3) um ensemble ponderado por características de modelos generativos e discriminativos para acomodar diversos padrões de compra subjacentes. Resultados empíricos mostram que nosso modelo aprimorado supera consistentemente desempenhos de referência para doze marcas de varejo em seis intervalos de avaliação de junho de 2020 a setembro de 2022.

Title: Understanding the relationship between marketing analytics, customer agility, and customer satisfaction: A longitudinal perspective.
Authors: Agag, G; Shehawy, YM; Almoraish, A; Eid, R; Lababdi, HC; Labben, TG; Abdo, SS
Abstract: Shifting towards a more data-driven culture is a key antecedent of business success in today's digital era. Previous research has paid attention to exploring the influence of marketing analytics on business performance, and rarely examined how the use of marketing analytics influences customer agility and satisfaction. According to the dynamic capabilities view and using previous studies, we developed a conceptual framework to explore the effect of marketing analytics use on customer agility and customer satisfaction. In Study 1, we utilised cross-sectional data collected from 468 managers from various industries. In study 2, we employed longitudinal data in a threewave longitudinal utilising a cross-lagged panel model. Study 1 indicated that data acquisition and tool acquisition are key drivers in adopting marketing analytics. Marketing analytics use has stronger effect on customer agility when market turbulence is high. They also revealed that the influence of customer agility on customer satisfaction in such conditions is stronger. Study 2 revealed that marketing analytics use at time point T1 has a significant and positive influence on customer agility at time point T2, while customer agility at time point T2 has a significant and positive influence on customer satisfaction at time point T3. These findings indicate strong temporal effects between marketing analytics use, customer agility, and customer satisfaction. The findings suggest that researchers should look beyond direct effects of marketing analytics use and shift their attention on how a marketing analytics can be leveraged to enable and support dynamic capabilities and customer satisfaction.
Keywords: Marketing analytics use; Customer agility; Customer satisfaction; Data-driven culture; Market turbulence
rationale: The abstract discusses the use of marketing analytics and its impact on customer agility and satisfaction, which aligns with the focus on market analysis, targeting, and personalization found in Thinking AI. The emphasis on the relationships and temporal effects between marketing analytics use and customer outcomes indicates a strategic analysis approach to marketing rather than emotional or purely mechanical processes.
resumo: A transição para uma cultura mais orientada por dados é um fator chave para o sucesso empresarial na era digital atual. Pesquisas anteriores focaram na influência da análise de marketing no desempenho dos negócios, raramente examinando como o uso de análises de marketing afeta a agilidade e a satisfação do cliente. Com base na visão das capacidades dinâmicas e em estudos anteriores, foi desenvolvido um modelo conceitual para explorar o efeito do uso de análises de marketing na agilidade e na satisfação do cliente. No Estudo 1, foram utilizados dados transversais coletados de 468 gerentes de diversas indústrias. No Estudo 2, foram empregados dados longitudinais em um modelo de painel com três ondas. O Estudo 1 indicou que a aquisição de dados e a aquisição de ferramentas são fatores-chave na adoção de análises de marketing. O uso de análises de marketing tem um efeito mais forte na agilidade do cliente quando a turbulência do mercado é alta, e a influência da agilidade do cliente na satisfação do cliente nessas condições é mais intensa. O Estudo 2 revelou que o uso de análises de marketing no ponto T1 tem uma influência positiva e significativa na agilidade do cliente no ponto T2, enquanto a agilidade do cliente no ponto T2 tem uma influência positiva e significativa na satisfação do cliente no ponto T3. Esses achados indicam fortes efeitos temporais entre o uso de análises de marketing, a agilidade do cliente e a satisfação do cliente, sugerindo que os pesquisadores devem ir além dos efeitos diretos do uso de análises de marketing e focar em como essas análises podem ser aproveitadas para habilitar e apoiar capacidades dinâmicas e a satisfação do cliente.

Title: Teaching marketing analytics: a pricing case study for quantitative and substantive marketing skills
Authors: Skiera B.; Jürgensmeier L.
Abstract: This article describes a data-driven case study for teaching and assessing students’ skills in marketing analytics, specifically in pricing. This case study combines teaching econometrics to analyze data and substantive marketing to derive managerial insights. The econometric challenge requires students to set up and implement a regression analysis to derive the demand function, detect multicollinearity, and select appropriate data visualizations. The substantive challenge requires deriving optimal pricing decisions and understanding how the parameters of the demand function impact optimal prices and the associated profit. We test the case study in a marketing analytics exam and discuss the performance of 134 students. Beyond assessing student performance in an exam, the case study facilitates teaching through in-class group work or assignments. Free of charge, under a liberal CC BY license, we encourage other educators to use the case study in their teaching. We provide the necessary data and a sample solution using the statistical programming language R. © The Author(s) 2024.
Keywords: Case study; Data science; Education; Marketing analytics; Pricing; Teaching
rationale: The abstract focuses on a case study that teaches and assesses students' skills in marketing analytics, particularly in pricing strategies and econometrics. The emphasis on analyzing data to derive managerial insights and making optimal pricing decisions aligns closely with the 'Market analysis' and 'Targeting' aspects of Thinking AI. The use of regression analysis and demand functions suggests a strategic analytical approach rather than automation or emotional understanding.
resumo: Este artigo descreve um estudo de caso baseado em dados para ensinar e avaliar as habilidades dos alunos em análise de marketing, especificamente em precificação. O estudo combina o ensino de econometria para analisar dados e marketing substantivo para derivar insights gerenciais. O desafio econométrico exige que os alunos configurem e implementem uma análise de regressão para derivar a função de demanda, detectem multicolinearidade e selecionem visualizações de dados apropriadas. O desafio substantivo requer a derivação de decisões de precificação ótimas e a compreensão de como os parâmetros da função de demanda impactam os preços ótimos e o lucro associado. Testamos o estudo de caso em um exame de análise de marketing e discutimos o desempenho de 134 alunos. Além de avaliar o desempenho dos alunos em um exame, o estudo de caso facilita o ensino por meio de trabalho em grupo em sala de aula ou tarefas. Gratuitamente, sob uma licença liberal CC BY, incentivamos outros educadores a utilizarem o estudo de caso em seu ensino. Fornecemos os dados necessários e uma solução de exemplo usando a linguagem de programação estatística R.

Title: Benefits, challenges and future developments in digital analytics in German-speaking countries: An empirical analysis
Authors: Zumstein D.; Brauer C.; Zelic A.
Abstract: This paper presents the results of a survey, conducted in 2020, to gauge the current standing of digital analytics in Germany, Switzerland and Austria. The findings highlight the increasing maturity level, benefits, challenges and future developments in the field. The research confirms that digital analytics supports the analysis and optimisation of digital marketing campaigns, user experience, search engine marketing and data-driven decisions. For many of the companies analysed, the most important challenges were reported to be data quality, lack of skills and data culture; however, maturity level, capabilities, agility and professionalism in digital analytics are steadily increasing, and artificial intelligence is enjoying many new and different applications within the fields of sales and marketing. These findings suggest that companies in German-speaking countries should focus on improving data quality and data culture. © Henry Stewart Publications 2054-7544 (2022).
Keywords: Artificial intelligence; Big Data; Business analytics; Digital analytics; Marketing analytics; Maturity level; Web analytics
rationale: The abstract discusses digital analytics in the context of supporting the analysis and optimization of digital marketing campaigns and data-driven decisions. It emphasizes market analysis, the identification of challenges, and the increasing maturity of companies in utilizing analytics. This aligns well with the 'Thinking AI' category, which focuses on market analysis and targeting.
resumo: Este artigo apresenta os resultados de uma pesquisa realizada em 2020 para avaliar a situação atual da análise digital na Alemanha, Suíça e Áustria. Os achados destacam o aumento do nível de maturidade, benefícios, desafios e desenvolvimentos futuros na área. A pesquisa confirma que a análise digital apoia a análise e otimização de campanhas de marketing digital, experiência do usuário, marketing em motores de busca e decisões baseadas em dados. Para muitas das empresas analisadas, os principais desafios relatados foram a qualidade dos dados, a falta de habilidades e a cultura de dados; no entanto, o nível de maturidade, capacidades, agilidade e profissionalismo na análise digital estão aumentando constantemente, e a inteligência artificial está desfrutando de muitas novas e diferentes aplicações nos campos de vendas e marketing. Esses achados sugerem que as empresas nos países de língua alemã devem se concentrar em melhorar a qualidade dos dados e a cultura de dados.

Title: Marketing analytics capability, artificial intelligence adoption, and firms? competitive advantage: Evidence from the manufacturing industry
Authors: Hossain, MA; Agnihotri, R; Rushan, MRI; Rahman, MS; Sumi, SF
Abstract: Data-driven analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) have become the most crucial aspects of today's industrial marketing management. Although many firms have embraced analytics and AI strategies, corresponding academic advances have been slow. This research investigates how industrial goods manufacturers sustain their competitive advantage in export markets, convincing buyers in a competitive data-rich business environment. The evidence has been taken from the RMG (readymade garment) industry, one of the largest manufacturing industries significantly attached to the export markets. Utilizing multi-phase research design, the study reveals that firms marketing analytics capability play a vital role in sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring the market, consequently leading to a sustained competitive advantage. The performance of sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring becomes higher for a firm when they adopt AI on the strength of the marketing analytics platform. These findings exhibit the latest avenue of exploration within marketing analytics and AI's academic research paradigm. Further, in practice, managers will be aware of the facts that create resilience in this specific industry context.
Keywords: Marketing analytics capability; AI adoption; Market sensing; Market seizing; Market reconfiguration; Manufacturing industry; B2B export market
rationale: The abstract discusses the role of marketing analytics and AI in sustaining competitive advantage, particularly in the context of the RMG industry. It emphasizes the importance of analyzing market conditions and leveraging data to enhance performance, which aligns closely with the definition of Thinking AI focused on market analysis and identifying competitive advantages.
resumo: A análise orientada por dados e a inteligência artificial (IA) tornaram-se aspectos cruciais na gestão de marketing industrial atual. Embora muitas empresas tenham adotado estratégias de análise e IA, os avanços acadêmicos correspondentes têm sido lentos. Esta pesquisa investiga como os fabricantes de bens industriais mantêm sua vantagem competitiva em mercados de exportação, convencendo compradores em um ambiente de negócios rico em dados. As evidências foram coletadas da indústria de vestuário pronto (RMG), uma das maiores indústrias de manufatura fortemente ligada aos mercados de exportação. Utilizando um design de pesquisa em múltiplas fases, o estudo revela que a capacidade analítica de marketing das empresas desempenha um papel vital na percepção, apropriação e reconfiguração do mercado, levando, consequentemente, a uma vantagem competitiva sustentável. O desempenho na percepção, apropriação e reconfiguração aumenta para uma empresa quando ela adota IA com base na plataforma de análise de marketing. Essas descobertas apresentam uma nova avenue de exploração dentro do paradigma de pesquisa acadêmica em análise de marketing e IA. Além disso, na prática, os gerentes estarão cientes dos fatores que criam resiliência neste contexto específico da indústria.

Title: Retail forecasting: Research and practice
Authors: Fildes R.; Ma S.; Kolassa S.
Abstract: This paper reviews the research literature on forecasting retail demand. We begin by introducing the forecasting problems that retailers face, from the strategic to the operational, as sales are aggregated over products to stores and to the company overall. Aggregated forecasting supports strategic decisions on location. Product-level forecasts usually relate to operational decisions at the store level. The factors that influence demand, and in particular promotional information, add considerable complexity, so that forecasters potentially face the dimensionality problem of too many variables and too little data. The paper goes on to evaluate evidence on comparative forecasting accuracy. Although causal models outperform simple benchmarks, adequate evidence on machine learning methods has not yet accumulated. Methods for forecasting new products are examined separately, with little evidence being found on the effectiveness of the various approaches. The paper concludes by describing company forecasting practices, offering conclusions as to both research gaps and barriers to improved practice. © 2019 International Institute of Forecasters
Keywords: Comparative accuracy; Forecasting practice; Marketing analytics; New products; Product hierarchies; Retail forecasting; Social media data
rationale: The abstract discusses the forecasting of retail demand, which involves understanding market dynamics and the factors affecting sales. It emphasizes the strategic and operational decisions retailers make based on sales forecasts. Additionally, the evaluation of forecasting methods points towards market analysis and targeting strategies, particularly in assessing promotional impacts. This aligns closely with the Thinking AI category which focuses on market analysis and targeting.
resumo: Este artigo revisa a literatura de pesquisa sobre previsão de demanda no varejo. Começamos apresentando os problemas de previsão que os varejistas enfrentam, desde os estratégicos até os operacionais, à medida que as vendas são agregadas por produtos, lojas e pela empresa como um todo. A previsão agregada apoia decisões estratégicas sobre localização. As previsões em nível de produto geralmente se relacionam a decisões operacionais no nível da loja. Os fatores que influenciam a demanda, em particular as informações promocionais, adicionam considerável complexidade, de modo que os preditores enfrentam potencialmente o problema de dimensionalidade de muitas variáveis e poucos dados. O artigo avalia evidências sobre a precisão comparativa das previsões. Embora modelos causais superem benchmarks simples, evidências adequadas sobre métodos de aprendizado de máquina ainda não se acumularam. Métodos para prever novos produtos são examinados separadamente, com poucas evidências encontradas sobre a eficácia das várias abordagens. O artigo conclui descrevendo as práticas de previsão das empresas, oferecendo conclusões sobre lacunas de pesquisa e barreiras para a melhoria das práticas. © 2019 International Institute of Forecasters

Title: Machine learning and artificial intelligence use in marketing: a general taxonomy
Authors: De Mauro A.; Sestino A.; Bacconi A.
Abstract: The emergence of consumer-generated data and the growing availability of Machine Learning (ML) techniques are revolutionizing marketing practices. Marketers and researchers are far from having a thorough understanding of the broad range of opportunities ML applications offer in creating and maintaining a competitive business advantage. In this paper, we propose a taxonomy of ML use cases in marketing based on a systematic review of academic and business literature. We have identified 11 recurring use cases, organized in 4 homogeneous families which correspond to the fundamentals leverage areas of ML in marketing, namely: shopper fundamentals, consumption experience, decision making, and financial impact. We discuss the recurring patterns identified in the taxonomy and provide a conceptual framework for its interpretation and extension, highlighting practical implications for marketers and researchers. © The Author(s) 2022.
Keywords: Analytics; Artificial intelligence; Big Data; Machine learning; Marketing; Marketing analytics
rationale: The abstract discusses the use of Machine Learning (ML) in marketing, focusing on various applications that enhance decision making, analysis of consumption experiences, and financial impacts. The identification of use cases and their organization into families aligns with strategic analysis in marketing, which corresponds to the Thinking AI category.
resumo: A emergência de dados gerados por consumidores e a crescente disponibilidade de técnicas de Aprendizado de Máquina (ML) estão revolucionando as práticas de marketing. Profissionais de marketing e pesquisadores ainda não compreendem completamente a ampla gama de oportunidades que as aplicações de ML oferecem para criar e manter uma vantagem competitiva nos negócios. Neste artigo, propomos uma taxonomia de casos de uso de ML em marketing com base em uma revisão sistemática da literatura acadêmica e de negócios. Identificamos 11 casos de uso recorrentes, organizados em 4 famílias homogêneas que correspondem às áreas fundamentais de alavancagem de ML em marketing: fundamentos do comprador, experiência de consumo, tomada de decisão e impacto financeiro. Discutimos os padrões recorrentes identificados na taxonomia e fornecemos um quadro conceitual para sua interpretação e extensão, destacando implicações práticas para profissionais de marketing e pesquisadores.

Title: Does marketing analytics capability boost firms' competitive marketing performance in data-rich business environment?
Authors: Rahman M.S.; Hossain M.A.; Abdel Fattah F.A.M.
Abstract: Purpose: Few well-documented studies have explained the importance of researching firms' marketing analytics capability (FMAC). In spite of its significance, there is scant attention to conceptualising and empirically investigating FMAC and its consequences in a data-driven business context. Thus, this study aims to develop and test a conceptual model that relates FMAC and its repercussions in the data-rich business environment. Design/methodology/approach: This study analysed the data from 250 managers amongst large and medium-sized manufacturing and service-intensive firms. Furthermore, this research performed an empirical study by using operationalised questionnaire survey method to verify the hypotheses and reach its theoretical and managerial implications. Structural equation modelling with maximum-likelihood estimation method was applied to verify the validity of the proposed research model. Findings: Multivariate analysis results show that FMAC significantly influences firms' competitive marketing performance (FCMP) with the presence of holistic marketing decision-making (HMDM) as a mediator. Moreover, adoption of artificial intelligence (AAI) enhances the relationship of FMAC-HMDM and FMAC-FCMP linkages. Practical implications: This study analyses how FMAC can enhance FCMP and contributes to resource-based views and technological capability theories. From a managerial perspective, guidelines are provided for marketers to adopt advance technologies, such as AI, to optimise FMAC and HMDM to achieve competitive marketing performance. Originality/value: Believing that “how to be competitive in marketing performance under data-rich-environment”, this research is the first to use the data of a firm manager to facilitate the understanding of FMAC, which provides a new direction for improving marketing performance. In addition, HMDM and AAI are also proposed for firms to optimise FCMP. © 2021, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence; Competitive marketing performance; Holistic marketing decision; Marketing analytics capability
keywords: ['marketing analytics capability', 'competitive marketing performance', 'holistic marketing decision-making', 'adoption of artificial intelligence', 'empirical study']
rationale: The abstract discusses the relationship between firms' marketing analytics capability (FMAC) and their competitive marketing performance (FCMP), emphasizing the importance of market analysis and decision-making in a data-driven environment. The mention of using artificial intelligence to enhance these relationships further aligns with the strategic analysis focus of Thinking AI.
resumo: Este estudo investiga a capacidade analítica de marketing das empresas (FMAC) e suas consequências em um ambiente de negócios orientado por dados. Analisando dados de 250 gerentes de empresas de médio e grande porte, a pesquisa utiliza um questionário operacionalizado para testar hipóteses e implicações teóricas e gerenciais. Os resultados mostram que a FMAC influencia significativamente o desempenho competitivo de marketing das empresas (FCMP), mediado pela tomada de decisão de marketing holística (HMDM). Além disso, a adoção de inteligência artificial (AAI) potencializa as relações entre FMAC-HMDM e FMAC-FCMP. As implicações práticas incluem diretrizes para que os profissionais de marketing adotem tecnologias avançadas, como IA, para otimizar FMAC e HMDM, visando melhorar o desempenho de marketing competitivo. Este estudo é pioneiro ao utilizar dados de gerentes para entender a FMAC e propõe HMDM e AAI como estratégias para otimizar o FCMP.

Title: Eye tracking technology to audit google analytics: Analysing digital consumer shopping journey in fashion m-retail
Authors: Tupikovskaja-Omovie Z.; Tyler D.
Abstract: Rapid changes in digital consumer behaviour, influenced by exponential adoption of smartphones, require timely and sophisticated responses from retailers to these consumer needs. With a growing amount of big data available, fashion retailers need to innovate and develop more sophisticated analytics for new consumer behaviours such as m-commerce. This research has considered how Google Analytics data can be applied to develop customer journey maps to understand digital consumer behaviour. A multi-method research design was used, incorporating an innovative mobile eye tracking technology and mobile fashion consumer data from Google Analytics. Digital customers’ shopping journeys on the fashion retailer's website were mapped using data sourced from eye tracking and Google Analytics, gathered in parallel. The comparison of these shopping journeys allowed a critical evaluation of the precision and usefulness of the Google Analytics database. Google Analytics tracked only half of the digital users’ activities, whereas eye tracking data documented digital consumers’ interaction with all elements of the fashion retailer's website. The conclusion reached is that eye tracking can be used to audit the Google Analytics database for potential gaps in data and also to inform and improve marketing decision-making. © 2020 Elsevier Ltd

Com a crescente quantidade de big data disponível, os varejistas de moda precisam inovar e desenvolver análises mais sofisticadas para novos comportamentos de consumo, como o m-commerce. Esta pesquisa considerou como os dados do Google Analytics podem ser aplicados para desenvolver mapas da jornada do cliente e entender o comportamento digital do consumidor. Um design de pesquisa multimétodo foi utilizado, incorporando uma tecnologia inovadora de rastreamento ocular móvel e dados de consumidores de moda móveis do Google Analytics. As jornadas de compra dos clientes digitais no site do varejista de moda foram mapeadas usando dados obtidos do rastreamento ocular e do Google Analytics, coletados em paralelo. O Google Analytics rastreou apenas metade das atividades dos usuários digitais, enquanto os dados de rastreamento ocular documentaram a interação dos consumidores digitais com todos os elementos do site do varejista de moda. A conclusão é que o rastreamento ocular pode ser usado para auditar o banco de dados do Google Analytics em busca de possíveis lacunas nos dados e também para informar e melhorar a tomada de decisões de marketing.

Title: Data-driven marketing for growth and profitability
Authors: Grandhi B.; Patwa N.; Saleem K.
Abstract: Purpose: In the current business environment, more uncertain than ever before, understanding consumer behavior is an integral part of an organization's strategic planning and execution process. It is the key driver for becoming a market leader. Therefore, it is important that all processes in business are customer centric. This research examines DDM adoption practices and how companies can aim to enhance shareholder value by bringing about “customer centricity”. Design/methodology/approach: An online survey conducted in 2016 received 180 responses from junior, middle and senior executives. Of the total responses, 26% were from senior management, 39% from middle management and the remaining 35% from junior management. Industries represented in the survey included retail, BFSI, healthcare and government, automobile, telecommunication, transport and logistics and IT. Other industries represented were aviation, marketing research and consulting, hospitality, advertising and media and human resource. Findings: Success of DDM depends upon how well an organization embraces the practice. The first and foremost indicator of an organization's commitment is the extent of resources invested for DDM. Respondents were divided into four categories; Laggards, Dabblers, Contenders and Leaders based on their “current level of investments” and “willingness to enhance investments” soon. Research limitations/implications: With storming digital age and the development of analytics, the process of decision-making has gained significant importance. Judgment and intuition too are critical to the process. Choosing an appropriate action cannot be done strictly on a rational basis. Practical implications: The results of the study offer interesting implications for managing the growing sea of data. An iterative and incremental approach is the need of the hour, even if it has to start with baby steps, to invest in and reap the fruits of DDM. The intention to use any system is always dependent on two primary belief factors: perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use; however, attitudes and social factors are equally important. Originality/value: There is a dearth of knowledge with regards to who is and is not adopting DDM, and how best big data can be harnessed for enhancing effectiveness and efficiency of marketing budget. It is, therefore, imperative to build a knowledge base on DDM practices, challenges and opportunities. Better use of data can help companies enhance shareholder value by bringing about “customer centricity”. © 2020, Emerald Publishing Limited.

resumo: O objetivo deste estudo é entender o comportamento do consumidor em um ambiente de negócios incerto, enfatizando a importância do marketing orientado a dados (DDM) para que as organizações se tornem líderes de mercado. Title: Marketing analytics for data-rich environments
Authors: Wedel M.; Kannan P.K.
Abstract: The authors provide a critical examination of marketing analytics methods by tracing their historical development, examining their applications to structured and unstructured data generated within or external to a firm, and reviewing their potential to support marketing decisions. The authors identify directions for new analytical research methods, addressing (1) analytics for optimizingmarketing-mix spending in a data-rich environment, (2) analytics for personalization, and (3) analytics in the context of customers' privacy and data security. They review the implications for organizations that intend to implement big data analytics. Finally, turning to the future, the authors identify trends that will shape marketing analytics as a discipline as well as marketing analytics education. © 2016, American Marketing Association.
Keywords: Big data; Marketing analytics; Marketing mix; Personalization; Privacy
rationale: The abstract discusses marketing analytics methods, focusing on their historical development and applications to structured and unstructured data. It emphasizes the potential of analytics to support marketing decisions, especially in optimizing marketing-mix spending and personalization. These themes align closely with the 'Thinking AI' category, which focuses on market analysis, targeting, and personalization strategies based on customer data.
resumo: Os autores realizam uma análise crítica dos métodos de análise de marketing, traçando seu desenvolvimento histórico, examinando suas aplicações a dados estruturados e não estruturados gerados dentro ou fora de uma empresa e revisando seu potencial para apoiar decisões de marketing. Eles identificam direções para novos métodos de pesquisa analítica, abordando (1) análises para otimização de gastos com marketing em um ambiente rico em dados, (2) análises para personalização e (3) análises no contexto da privacidade e segurança dos dados dos clientes. Por fim, ao olhar para o futuro, identificam tendências que moldarão a análise de marketing como disciplina, bem como a educação em análise de marketing.

Title: Big Data and consumer behavior: imminent opportunities
Authors: Hofacker C.F.; Malthouse E.C.; Sultan F.
Abstract: Purpose – The purpose of this paper is to assess how the study of consumer behavior can benefit from the presence of Big Data. Design/methodology/approach – This paper offers a conceptual overview of potential opportunities and changes to the study of consumer behavior that Big Data will likely bring. Findings – Big Data have the potential to further our understanding of each stage in the consumer decision-making process. While the field has traditionally moved forward using a priori theory followed by experimentation, it now seems that the nature of the feedback loop between theory and results may shift under the weight of Big Data. Research limitations/implications – A new data culture is now represented in marketing practice. The new group advocates inductive data mining and A/B testing rather than human intuition harnessed for deduction. The group brings with it interest in numerous secondary data sources. However, Big Data may be limited by poor quality, unrepresentativeness and volatility, among other problems. Practical implications – Managers who need to understand consumer behavior will need a workforce with different skill sets than in the past, such as Big Data consumer analytics. Originality/value – To the authors' knowledge, this is one of the first articles to assess how the study of consumer behavior can evolve in the context of the Big Data revolution. © 2016, © Emerald Group Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Big Data; Consumer behavior; Marketing analytics

resumo: O objetivo deste artigo é avaliar como o estudo do comportamento do consumidor pode se beneficiar da presença de Big Data. O artigo oferece uma visão conceitual das oportunidades e mudanças que o Big Data provavelmente trará para o estudo do comportamento do consumidor. Os dados massivos têm o potencial de aprofundar nossa compreensão de cada etapa do processo de tomada de decisão do consumidor. Embora o campo tenha avançado tradicionalmente utilizando teoria a priori seguida de experimentação, agora parece que a natureza do ciclo de feedback entre teoria e resultados pode mudar sob o peso do Big Data. Uma nova cultura de dados está agora representada na prática de marketing, defendendo a mineração de dados indutiva e testes A/B em vez da intuição humana para dedução, trazendo interesse em diversas fontes de dados secundários. No entanto, o Big Data pode ser limitado por problemas como baixa qualidade, falta de representatividade e volatilidade. Os gerentes que precisam entender o comportamento do consumidor precisarão de uma força de trabalho com habilidades diferentes das do passado, como análise de consumidores com Big Data. Até onde os autores sabem, este é um dos primeiros artigos a avaliar como o estudo do comportamento do consumidor pode evoluir no contexto da revolução do Big Data.

Title: Retail forecasting: Research and practice
Authors: Fildes R.; Ma S.; Kolassa S.
Abstract: This paper reviews the research literature on forecasting retail demand. We begin by introducing the forecasting problems that retailers face, from the strategic to the operational, as sales are aggregated over products to stores and to the company overall. Aggregated forecasting supports strategic decisions on location. Product-level forecasts usually relate to operational decisions at the store level. The factors that influence demand, and in particular promotional information, add considerable complexity, so that forecasters potentially face the dimensionality problem of too many variables and too little data. The paper goes on to evaluate evidence on comparative forecasting accuracy. Although causal models outperform simple benchmarks, adequate evidence on machine learning methods has not yet accumulated. Methods for forecasting new products are examined separately, with little evidence being found on the effectiveness of the various approaches. The paper concludes by describing company forecasting practices, offering conclusions as to both research gaps and barriers to improved practice. © 2019 International Institute of Forecasters
Keywords: Comparative accuracy; Forecasting practice; Marketing analytics; New products; Product hierarchies; Retail forecasting; Social media data
rationale: The abstract discusses the forecasting of retail demand, which involves understanding market dynamics and the factors affecting sales. It emphasizes the strategic and operational decisions retailers make based on sales forecasts. Additionally, the evaluation of forecasting methods points towards market analysis and targeting strategies, particularly in assessing promotional impacts. This aligns closely with the Thinking AI category which focuses on market analysis and targeting.
resumo: Este artigo revisa a literatura de pesquisa sobre previsão de demanda no varejo. Começamos apresentando os problemas de previsão que os varejistas enfrentam, desde os estratégicos até os operacionais, à medida que as vendas são agregadas por produtos, lojas e pela empresa como um todo. A previsão agregada apoia decisões estratégicas sobre localização. As previsões em nível de produto geralmente se relacionam a decisões operacionais no nível da loja. Os fatores que influenciam a demanda, em particular as informações promocionais, adicionam considerável complexidade, de modo que os previsores enfrentam potencialmente o problema de dimensionalidade de muitas variáveis e poucos dados. O artigo avalia evidências sobre a precisão comparativa das previsões. Embora modelos causais superem benchmarks simples, evidências adequadas sobre métodos de aprendizado de máquina ainda não se acumularam. Métodos para prever novos produtos são examinados separadamente, com pouca evidência encontrada sobre a eficácia das várias abordagens. O artigo conclui descrevendo as práticas de previsão das empresas, oferecendo conclusões sobre lacunas de pesquisa e barreiras à melhoria das práticas.

Title: Fostering B2B sales with customer big data analytics
Authors: Hallikainen, H; Savimäki, E; Laukkanen, T
Abstract: This study focuses on the use of big data analytics in managing B2B customer relationships and examines the effects of big data analytics on customer relationship performance and sales growth using a multi-industry dataset from 417 B2B firms. The study also examines whether analytics culture within a firm moderates these effects. The study finds that the use of customer big data significantly fosters sales growth (i.e. monetary performance outcomes) and enhances the customer relationship performance (non-monetary performance outcomes). However, the latter effect is stronger for firms which have an analytics culture which supports marketing analytics, whereas the former effect remains unchanged regardless of the analytics culture. The study empirically confirms that customer big data analytics improves customer relationship performance and sales growth in B2B firms.
Keywords: Big data analytics; Customer analytics; Marketing analytics; Firm performance; Customer relationship management; Big data-enhanced database marketing

O estudo também investiga se a cultura analítica dentro de uma empresa modera esses efeitos. Os resultados mostram que o uso de big data do cliente promove significativamente o crescimento das vendas (ou seja, resultados de desempenho monetário) e melhora o desempenho do relacionamento com o cliente (resultados de desempenho não monetário). No entanto, o efeito sobre o desempenho do relacionamento é mais forte em empresas que possuem uma cultura analítica que apoia análises de marketing, enquanto o efeito sobre o crescimento das vendas permanece inalterado, independentemente da cultura analítica. O estudo confirma empiricamente que a análise de big data do cliente melhora o desempenho do relacionamento com o cliente e o crescimento das vendas em empresas B2B.

Title: A dynamic capability view of marketing analytics: Evidence from UK firms
Authors: Cao G.; Duan Y.; El Banna A.
Abstract: While marketing analytics plays an important role in generating insights from big data to improve marketing decision-making and firm competitiveness, few academic studies have investigated the mechanisms through which it can be used to achieve sustained competitive advantage. To close this gap, this study draws on the dynamic capability view to posit that a firm can attain sustained competitive advantage from its sensing, seizing and reconfiguring capabilities, which are manifested by the use of marketing analytics, marketing decision-making, and product development management. This study also examines the impact of the antecedents of marketing analytics use on marketing related processes. The analysis of a survey of 221 UK firm managers demonstrates: (a) the positive impact of marketing analytics use on both marketing decision-making and product development management; (b) the effect of the latter two on sustained competitive advantage; (c) the indirect effect of data availability on both marketing decision-making and production development management; and (d) the indirect effect of managerial support on marketing decision-making. The research model proposed in this study provides insights into how marketing analytics can be used to achieve sustained competitive advantage. © 2018 Elsevier Inc.
Keywords: Dynamic capability view; Marketing analytics; Marketing decision-making; Product development management; Sustained competitive advantage

rationale: The abstract discusses the use of marketing analytics in enhancing marketing decision-making, product development management, and ultimately achieving sustained competitive advantage. This aligns closely with the focus of Thinking AI on market analysis and competitive advantages. The findings indicate the positive impact of marketing analytics on strategic processes, which is characteristic of Thinking AI applications.
resumo: A análise de marketing desempenha um papel importante na geração de insights a partir de grandes volumes de dados para melhorar a tomada de decisões de marketing e a competitividade das empresas. No entanto, poucos estudos acadêmicos investigaram os mecanismos pelos quais ela pode ser utilizada para alcançar uma vantagem competitiva sustentável. Para preencher essa lacuna, este estudo baseia-se na visão de capacidades dinâmicas para afirmar que uma empresa pode obter vantagem competitiva sustentável por meio de suas capacidades de percepção, apropriação e reconfiguração, manifestadas pelo uso de análises de marketing, tomada de decisões de marketing e gestão do desenvolvimento de produtos. O estudo também examina o impacto dos antecedentes do uso de análises de marketing nos processos relacionados ao marketing. A análise de uma pesquisa com 221 gerentes de empresas do Reino Unido demonstra: (a) o impacto positivo do uso de análises de marketing tanto na tomada de decisões de marketing quanto na gestão do desenvolvimento de produtos; (b) o efeito destes dois últimos na vantagem competitiva sustentável; (c) o efeito indireto da disponibilidade de dados tanto na tomada de decisões de marketing quanto na gestão do desenvolvimento de produtos; e (d) o efeito indireto do apoio gerencial na tomada de decisões de marketing. O modelo de pesquisa proposto neste estudo fornece insights sobre como as análises de marketing podem ser utilizadas para alcançar uma vantagem competitiva sustentável.

Title: Role of big data in decision making
Authors: Jeble S.; Kumari S.; Patil Y.
Abstract: Information systems coupled with internet, cloud computing, mobile devices and Internet of Things have led to massive volumes of data, commonly referred as big data. It includes mix of structured, semi-structured and unstructured real-time data, constituting of data warehouse, OLAP, ETL and information. Business firms and academicians have designed unique ways of tapping value from big data. There is a great scope of using large datasets as an additional input for making decisions. The aim of the paper is to explore the role of big data in these areas for making better decisions. Here we explore how big data can be used to make smart and real-time decisions for improving business results. The paper undergoes literature review and secondary data to provide a conceptual overview of potential opportunities of big data in decision making. The paper discusses the concept of big data, its role in decision making and also the competitive advantage of big data for different firms. The paper also discusses a framework for managing data in decision making. The topic must be addressed for taking better decisions for firms which will contribute to high quality knowledge. © Operations and Supply Chain Management. All rights reserved.
Keywords: Big data; Big data analytics; Marketing analytics; Social media analytics
Publisher: Operations and Supply Chain Management Forum
rationale: The abstract emphasizes the role of big data in enhancing decision-making processes within business firms, focusing on market analysis and competitive advantages derived from data. It discusses how businesses can leverage large datasets to make smarter, real-time decisions, which aligns closely with the 'Thinking AI' category that focuses on market analysis and targeting.
resumo: Sistemas de informação associados à internet, computação em nuvem, dispositivos móveis e Internet das Coisas resultaram em volumes massivos de dados, comumente chamados de big data. Isso inclui uma mistura de dados estruturados, semi-estruturados e não estruturados em tempo real, constituindo data warehouse, OLAP, ETL e informações. Empresas e acadêmicos desenvolveram maneiras únicas de extrair valor do big data. Há um grande potencial para usar grandes conjuntos de dados como um insumo adicional na tomada de decisões. O objetivo do artigo é explorar o papel do big data nessas áreas para melhorar a tomada de decisões. O artigo investiga como o big data pode ser utilizado para tomar decisões inteligentes e em tempo real, melhorando os resultados empresariais. O texto realiza uma revisão da literatura e utiliza dados secundários para fornecer uma visão conceitual das oportunidades potenciais do big data na tomada de decisões. Discute o conceito de big data, seu papel na tomada de decisões e a vantagem competitiva que oferece a diferentes empresas. Além disso, apresenta um framework para gerenciar dados na tomada de decisões. O tema deve ser abordado para que as empresas tomem decisões melhores, contribuindo para um conhecimento de alta qualidade.

Title: Marketing analytics capability, artificial intelligence adoption, and firms? competitive advantage: Evidence from the manufacturing industry
Authors: Hossain, MA; Agnihotri, R; Rushan, MRI; Rahman, MS; Sumi, SF
Abstract: Data-driven analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) have become the most crucial aspects of today's industrial marketing management. Although many firms have embraced analytics and AI strategies, corresponding academic advances have been slow. This research investigates how industrial goods manufacturers sustain their competitive advantage in export markets, convincing buyers in a competitive data-rich business environment. The evidence has been taken from the RMG (readymade garment) industry, one of the largest manufacturing industries significantly attached to the export markets. Utilizing multi-phase research design, the study reveals that firms marketing analytics capability play a vital role in sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring the market, consequently leading to a sustained competitive advantage. The performance of sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring becomes higher for a firm when they adopt AI on the strength of the marketing analytics platform. These findings exhibit the latest avenue of exploration within marketing analytics and AI's academic research paradigm. Further, in practice, managers will be aware of the facts that create resilience in this specific industry context.
Keywords: Marketing analytics capability; AI adoption; Market sensing; Market seizing; Market reconfiguration; Manufacturing industry; B2B export market
rationale: The abstract discusses the role of marketing analytics and AI in sustaining competitive advantage, particularly in the context of the RMG industry. It emphasizes the importance of analyzing market conditions and leveraging data to enhance performance, which aligns closely with the definition of Thinking AI focused on market analysis and identifying competitive advantages.
resumo: A análise orientada por dados e a inteligência artificial (IA) tornaram-se aspectos cruciais na gestão de marketing industrial atual. Embora muitas empresas tenham adotado estratégias de análise e IA, os avanços acadêmicos correspondentes têm sido lentos. Esta pesquisa investiga como os fabricantes de bens industriais mantêm sua vantagem competitiva em mercados de exportação, convencendo compradores em um ambiente de negócios competitivo e rico em dados. As evidências foram coletadas da indústria de vestuário pronto (RMG), uma das maiores indústrias de manufatura intimamente ligada aos mercados de exportação. Utilizando um design de pesquisa em múltiplas fases, o estudo revela que a capacidade de análise de marketing das empresas desempenha um papel vital na percepção, apropriação e reconfiguração do mercado, levando, consequentemente, a uma vantagem competitiva sustentada. O desempenho na percepção, apropriação e reconfiguração aumenta para uma empresa quando ela adota IA com base na plataforma de análise de marketing. Esses achados mostram uma nova avenida de exploração dentro do paradigma de pesquisa acadêmica em análise de marketing e IA. Além disso, na prática, os gerentes estarão cientes dos fatores que criam resiliência nesse contexto específico da indústria.

Title: Machine learning and artificial intelligence use in marketing: a general taxonomy
Authors: De Mauro A.; Sestino A.; Bacconi A.
Abstract: The emergence of consumer-generated data and the growing availability of Machine Learning (ML) techniques are revolutionizing marketing practices. Marketers and researchers are far from having a thorough understanding of the broad range of opportunities ML applications offer in creating and maintaining a competitive business advantage. In this paper, we propose a taxonomy of ML use cases in marketing based on a systematic review of academic and business literature. We have identified 11 recurring use cases, organized in 4 homogeneous families which correspond to the fundamentals leverage areas of ML in marketing, namely: shopper fundamentals, consumption experience, decision making, and financial impact. We discuss the recurring patterns identified in the taxonomy and provide a conceptual framework for its interpretation and extension, highlighting practical implications for marketers and researchers. © The Author(s) 2022.
Keywords: Analytics; Artificial intelligence; Big Data; Machine learning; Marketing; Marketing analytics
rationale: The abstract discusses the use of Machine Learning (ML) in marketing, focusing on various applications that enhance decision making, analysis of consumption experiences, and financial impacts. The identification of use cases and their organization into families aligns with strategic analysis in marketing, which corresponds to the Thinking AI category.
resumo: A emergência de dados gerados por consumidores e a crescente disponibilidade de técnicas de Aprendizado de Máquina (ML) estão revolucionando as práticas de marketing. Os profissionais de marketing e pesquisadores ainda não compreendem completamente a ampla gama de oportunidades que as aplicações de ML oferecem para criar e manter uma vantagem competitiva nos negócios. Neste artigo, propomos uma taxonomia de casos de uso de ML em marketing com base em uma revisão sistemática da literatura acadêmica e empresarial. Identificamos 11 casos de uso recorrentes, organizados em 4 famílias homogêneas que correspondem às áreas fundamentais de alavancagem de ML em marketing: fundamentos do comprador, experiência de consumo, tomada de decisão e impacto financeiro. Discutimos os padrões recorrentes identificados na taxonomia e fornecemos um framework conceitual para sua interpretação e extensão, destacando implicações práticas para profissionais de marketing e pesquisadores.

Title: Does marketing analytics capability boost firms' competitive marketing performance in data-rich business environment?
Authors: Rahman M.S.; Hossain M.A.; Abdel Fattah F.A.M.
Abstract: Purpose: Few well-documented studies have explained the importance of researching firms' marketing analytics capability (FMAC). In spite of its significance, there is scant attention to conceptualising and empirically investigating FMAC and its consequences in a data-driven business context. Thus, this study aims to develop and test a conceptual model that relates FMAC and its repercussions in the data-rich business environment. Design/methodology/approach: This study analysed the data from 250 managers amongst large and medium-sized manufacturing and service-intensive firms. Furthermore, this research performed an empirical study by using operationalised questionnaire survey method to verify the hypotheses and reach its theoretical and managerial implications. Structural equation modelling with maximum-likelihood estimation method was applied to verify the validity of the proposed research model. Findings: Multivariate analysis results show that FMAC significantly influences firms' competitive marketing performance (FCMP) with the presence of holistic marketing decision-making (HMDM) as a mediator. Moreover, adoption of artificial intelligence (AAI) enhances the relationship of FMAC-HMDM and FMAC-FCMP linkages. Practical implications: This study analyses how FMAC can enhance FCMP and contributes to resource-based views and technological capability theories. From a managerial perspective, guidelines are provided for marketers to adopt advance technologies, such as AI, to optimise FMAC and HMDM to achieve competitive marketing performance. Originality/value: Believing that “how to be competitive in marketing performance under data-rich-environment”, this research is the first to use the data of a firm manager to facilitate the understanding of FMAC, which provides a new direction for improving marketing performance. In addition, HMDM and AAI are also proposed for firms to optimise FCMP. © 2021, Emerald Publishing Limited.

Utilizando um questionário operacionalizado, o estudo testou hipóteses e aplicou modelagem de equações estruturais para validar o modelo proposto. Os resultados mostram que a FMAC influencia significativamente o desempenho de marketing competitivo das empresas (FCMP), mediado pela tomada de decisão de marketing holística (HMDM). Além disso, a adoção de inteligência artificial (AAI) fortalece as relações entre FMAC-HMDM e FMAC-FCMP. As implicações práticas incluem diretrizes para que os profissionais de marketing adotem tecnologias avançadas, como IA, para otimizar FMAC e HMDM e, assim, melhorar o desempenho de marketing competitivo. Este estudo é pioneiro ao utilizar dados de gerentes para entender a FMAC, oferecendo uma nova direção para aprimorar o desempenho de marketing.

Title: Evaluating strategies for promoting retail mobile channel using a hidden Markov model
Authors: Chen J.; Rao V.R.
Abstract: With the proliferation of mobile communication technology, many firms, including retailers and consumer banks, are making efforts to develop mobile platforms to better engage with their customers and reduce operational costs. However, the cost advantage of these mobile technologies will not yield fruition unless the mobile channel accounts for a significant share of total transactions. In this article, we explore potential options for firms to promote usage of the mobile channel. To achieve this, we propose a hidden Markov model to both model customers’ decisions and assess different managerial strategies through simulations. While we apply our proposed model to data from a leading financial institution, our approach is equally applicable to other retail settings. The results show that customers’ choices of services and channels are sensitive to process time by type of channel. A 10% increase in process time through non-mobile channels leads to a nearly 14% increase in utilization of mobile banking channel. Therefore, retailing firms could potentially influence customers’ choice of different channels by changing channel-specific process times. Motivated by these findings, we present and compare performances across five different policies, in promoting the usage of mobile channel. Drawing on our simulation results, we also make personalized policy recommendations to firms facing different levels of financial constraints. For those with financial constraints, we recommend a policy of increasing process time for a selected subset of service requests through non-mobile channels. Firms not constrained by the resources might be better off improving process time with the mobile channel by targeting customers identified as having a better relationship with the firm. © 2022 New York University

No entanto, a vantagem de custo dessas tecnologias móveis não será aproveitada a menos que o canal móvel represente uma parte significativa das transações totais. Este artigo explora opções potenciais para as empresas promoverem o uso do canal móvel. Para isso, propomos um modelo oculto de Markov para modelar as decisões dos clientes e avaliar diferentes estratégias gerenciais por meio de simulações. Embora apliquemos nosso modelo a dados de uma instituição financeira líder, nossa abordagem é igualmente aplicável a outros contextos de varejo. Os resultados mostram que as escolhas dos clientes por serviços e canais são sensíveis ao tempo de processamento por tipo de canal. Um aumento de 10% no tempo de processamento em canais não móveis leva a um aumento de quase 14% na utilização do canal de banco móvel. Portanto, as empresas de varejo poderiam influenciar a escolha dos clientes por diferentes canais ao alterar os tempos de processamento específicos de cada canal. Motivados por essas descobertas, apresentamos e comparamos desempenhos em cinco políticas diferentes para promover o uso do canal móvel. Com base em nossos resultados de simulação, também fazemos recomendações de políticas personalizadas para empresas que enfrentam diferentes níveis de restrições financeiras. Para aquelas com restrições financeiras, recomendamos uma política de aumento do tempo de processamento para um subconjunto selecionado de solicitações de serviço em canais não móveis. Empresas que não estão limitadas por recursos podem se beneficiar mais ao melhorar o tempo de processamento no canal móvel, direcionando-se a clientes identificados como tendo um melhor relacionamento com a empresa.

Title: How has data-driven marketing evolved: Challenges and opportunities with emerging technologies
Authors: Rosário A.T.; Dias J.C.
Abstract: This paper explores data-driven marketing, its benefits, and challenges to provide insights and a framework for business leaders and marketers to leverage in their marketing efforts. Using a systematic literature review with bibliometric analysis, we examined a sample of 98 studies indexed in SCOPUS to identify research activity on this topic until May 2023. Data-driven marketing and communications have gained popularity as companies and marketers prioritize leveraging consumer and market data to strategize and make informed decisions. Adopting and integrating various technologies into the company's systems is crucial for companies aiming to achieve a sustainable competitive advantage. By analyzing and interpreting customer data, companies can implement customer-centered marketing initiatives that enhance their experience and satisfaction with the brand, thus strengthening company-customer relationships. However, data-driven marketing faces several challenges, including consumer privacy concerns, data poisoning, information quality issues, and the need for adequate organizational changes. © 2023

resumo: Este artigo explora o marketing orientado a dados, seus benefícios e desafios, fornecendo insights e um framework para líderes empresariais e profissionais de marketing. Utilizando uma revisão sistemática da literatura com análise bibliométrica, examinamos uma amostra de 98 estudos indexados no SCOPUS para identificar a atividade de pesquisa sobre este tema até maio de 2023. O marketing e as comunicações orientados a dados ganharam popularidade à medida que empresas e profissionais priorizam o uso de dados de consumidores e do mercado para formular estratégias e tomar decisões informadas. A adoção e a integração de várias tecnologias nos sistemas da empresa são cruciais para aquelas que buscam alcançar uma vantagem competitiva sustentável. Ao analisar e interpretar dados de clientes, as empresas podem implementar iniciativas de marketing centradas no cliente que aprimoram sua experiência e satisfação com a marca, fortalecendo assim as relações entre a empresa e o cliente. No entanto, o marketing orientado a dados enfrenta vários desafios, incluindo preocupações com a privacidade do consumidor, contaminação de dados, problemas de qualidade da informação e a necessidade de mudanças organizacionais adequadas. © 2023

Title: Using a data-driven marketing strategy on customer relationship management: an empirical case of urban coffee shops in Taiwan
Authors: Chiang W.-Y.
Abstract: Purpose: Nowadays, the agricultural business environment is expended to the whole world. Transaction records in point of sales and customer relationship management (CRM) systems can be large-scale data for long-established global chain businesses. Thus, the purpose of this paper is to using a proposed data mining approach to discover valuable markets/customers of urban coffee shop industry (retailer) in current environment of Taiwan, which can implement the industry's data-driven marketing strategy on a CRM system. Design/methodology/approach: In this research approach, Ward's method, C5.0 decision tree and a proposed model are applied for discovering valuable markets and mining useful customer rules. Findings: These found markets and discovered rules can be applied on marketing information or CRM system for identifying valuable customers and target markets. Originality/value: In this study, the CRM system can be the media for the data-driven marketing strategy in environment of Taiwan. The approach of this research can be applied on other businesses for their data-driven marketing strategies as well. © 2020, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Customer relationship management system; Customer value; Data mining; Marketing information system

This aligns with the 'Thinking AI' category, which emphasizes market analysis and targeting through the identification of valuable customers and markets. The use of decision trees and other analytical methods to derive insights for a data-driven marketing strategy further supports this classification.
resumo: O objetivo deste artigo é utilizar uma abordagem proposta de mineração de dados para descobrir mercados/clientes valiosos na indústria de cafeterias urbanas em Taiwan, permitindo a implementação de uma estratégia de marketing orientada por dados em um sistema de gerenciamento de relacionamento com o cliente (CRM). A pesquisa aplica o método de Ward, a árvore de decisão C5.0 e um modelo proposto para identificar mercados valiosos e extrair regras úteis sobre os clientes. Os mercados encontrados e as regras descobertas podem ser aplicados em informações de marketing ou no sistema CRM para identificar clientes valiosos e mercados-alvo. Este estudo destaca que o sistema CRM pode ser um meio para a estratégia de marketing orientada por dados no ambiente de Taiwan, e a abordagem pode ser aplicada em outros negócios para suas estratégias de marketing baseadas em dados.

Title: Fostering B2B sales with customer big data analytics
Authors: Hallikainen, H; Savimäki, E; Laukkanen, T
Abstract: This study focuses on the use of big data analytics in managing B2B customer relationships and examines the effects of big data analytics on customer relationship performance and sales growth using a multi-industry dataset from 417 B2B firms. The study also examines whether analytics culture within a firm moderates these effects. The study finds that the use of customer big data significantly fosters sales growth (i.e. monetary performance outcomes) and enhances the customer relationship performance (non-monetary performance outcomes). However, the latter effect is stronger for firms which have an analytics culture which supports marketing analytics, whereas the former effect remains unchanged regardless of the analytics culture. The study empirically confirms that customer big data analytics improves customer relationship performance and sales growth in B2B firms.
