O estudo também investiga se a cultura analítica dentro de uma empresa modera esses efeitos. Os resultados mostram que o uso de big data do cliente promove significativamente o crescimento das vendas (ou seja, resultados de desempenho monetário) e melhora o desempenho do relacionamento com o cliente (resultados de desempenho não monetário). No entanto, o efeito sobre o desempenho do relacionamento é mais forte em empresas que possuem uma cultura analítica que apoia a análise de marketing, enquanto o efeito sobre o crescimento das vendas permanece inalterado, independentemente da cultura analítica. O estudo confirma empiricamente que a análise de big data do cliente melhora o desempenho do relacionamento com o cliente e o crescimento das vendas em empresas B2B.

Title: Personalized digital marketing recommender engine
Authors: Behera, RK; Gunasekaran, A; Gupta, S; Kamboj, S; Bala, PK
Abstract: E-business leverages digital channels to scale its functions and services and operates by connecting and retaining customers using marketing initiatives. To increase the likelihood of a sale, the business must recommend additional items that the customers may be unaware of or may find appealing. Recommender Engine (RE) is considered to be the preferred solution in these cases for reasons that include delivering relevant items, hence improving cart value, and boosting customer engagement. The paper describes a model for delivering real-time, personalised marketing information concerning the recommended items for online and offline customers, using a blend of selling strategies: up-selling, cross-selling, best-in-class-selling, needs-satisfaction-selling and consultative-selling. The model further defines the e-marketplace by clustering items, customers and unique selling proposition (USP), and then gathering, storing, and processing transactional data, and displaying personalised marketing information to support the customer in their decision-making process, even when purchasing from large item spaces. An experimental study using a quantitative research methodology was conducted in a mid-size healthcare retailer, based out of India, to determine the tangible benefits. The model was tested with 100 online customers and, with the adoption of the proposed methodology, the results indicated growth in average monthly revenue (33.49%), Average Order Value (AOV) (32.79%) and Items per Order (IPO) (1.93%).
Keywords: Personalized digital marketing; Recommender engine; Customer relationship management
rationale: The abstract describes a model that utilizes a recommender engine to deliver personalized marketing information, which aligns closely with the focus on personalization and targeting in Thinking AI. The model aims to enhance customer engagement and improve sales metrics, indicating a strategic analysis of customer behavior and preferences. The experimental study also highlights the application of marketing analytics to achieve measurable growth, which further supports its classification under Thinking AI.
resumo: O e-business utiliza canais digitais para expandir suas funções e serviços, conectando e retendo clientes por meio de iniciativas de marketing. Para aumentar a probabilidade de venda, é essencial recomendar itens adicionais que os clientes possam desconhecer ou achar atraentes. O Recommender Engine (RE) é a solução preferida, pois entrega itens relevantes, melhorando o valor do carrinho e aumentando o engajamento do cliente. O artigo descreve um modelo para fornecer informações de marketing personalizadas em tempo real sobre itens recomendados para clientes online e offline, utilizando uma combinação de estratégias de venda: up-selling, cross-selling, best-in-class-selling, needs-satisfaction-selling e consultative-selling. O modelo também define o e-marketplace agrupando itens, clientes e proposta de venda única (USP), além de coletar, armazenar e processar dados transacionais, exibindo informações de marketing personalizadas para apoiar a tomada de decisão do cliente, mesmo em grandes espaços de itens. Um estudo experimental com metodologia de pesquisa quantitativa foi realizado em um varejista de saúde de médio porte na Índia para determinar os benefícios tangíveis. O modelo foi testado com 100 clientes online e, com a adoção da metodologia proposta, os resultados indicaram crescimento na receita média mensal (33,49%), no Valor Médio do Pedido (AOV) (32,79%) e nos Itens por Pedido (IPO) (1,93%).

Title: Ariika – a successful implementation of information and communication technology by Egyptian entrepreneurs
Authors: Azab N.; Mekkawy A.N.
Abstract: Subject area: This case shows an example of the opportunities opened by the internet that drove young entrepreneurs to start their business, in May 2011, as a premium beanbag supplier in Egypt. Study level/applicability: Undergraduate students studying management. Case overview: The case examines the use of information and communication technology (ICT) by young Egyptian entrepreneurs, and how technology could open for them a broad horizon for continuous development, creativity and innovation. It presents the experience of a group of four undergraduate students who established a virtual company producing and selling beanbags through their website. The main objective of the case is to highlight the business challenges faced by entrepreneurs and possible opportunities in emerging economies and the effective role of ICT in reacting to these business environment changes. The case also provides a strategic analysis of the various factors that may impact the organization and explains how technology can contribute to improving the company’s standing. Finally, recommendations are provided to serve as basis for any future strategic plans. Expected learning outcomes: This study highlights the value of ICT in general and the internet in particular in driving young entrepreneurs to start their own business. It also presents the best practices in conducting a successful online business, and approaches undertaken by internet entrepreneurs to address rising challenges. It understands the variety of tools that could be used to market business online. It indicates the role of information technology in supporting business strategies at any organizational stage to improve different processes, to assist in decision-making, and to create new customer-centric services and products. O principal objetivo do caso é destacar os desafios empresariais enfrentados pelos empreendedores e as oportunidades possíveis em economias emergentes, além do papel eficaz da TIC em responder a essas mudanças no ambiente de negócios. Os resultados esperados deste estudo destacam o valor da TIC em geral e da internet em particular na motivação de jovens empreendedores a iniciar seus próprios negócios. Também apresenta as melhores práticas para conduzir um negócio online de sucesso e as abordagens adotadas por empreendedores da internet para enfrentar desafios crescentes, além de compreender a variedade de ferramentas que podem ser utilizadas para comercializar negócios online. Indica o papel da tecnologia da informação no apoio a estratégias empresariais em qualquer estágio organizacional para melhorar diferentes processos, auxiliar na tomada de decisões e criar novos serviços e produtos centrados no cliente. Title: To establish online shoppers' markets and rules for dynamic CRM systems An empirical case study in Taiwan
Authors: Chiang, WY
Abstract: Purpose - The purpose of this paper is to establish customers' markets and rules of dynamic customer relationship management (CRM) systems for online retailers. Design/methodology/approach - This research proposes a procedure to discover customers' markets and rules, which adopts the recency, frequency, monetary value (RFM) variables, transaction records, and socioeconomic data of the online shoppers to be the research variables. The research methods aim at the supervised apriori algorithm, C5.0 decision tree algorithm, and RFM model. Findings - This research discovered eight RFM markets and six rules of online retailers. Practical implications - The proposed framework and research results can help retailer managers to retain and expand high value markets via their dynamic CRM and POS systems. Originality/value - This research uses data mining technologies to extract high value markets and rules for marketing plans. The research variables are easy to obtain via retailers' systems. The found customer values, RFM markets, shopping association rules, and marketing decision rules can be discovered via the framework of this research.
Keywords: Taiwan; Consumer behaviour; Customer relationship management; Internet; Apriori algorithm; C5.0 decision tree; RFM model; Customer values

Os métodos de pesquisa visam o algoritmo apriori supervisionado, o algoritmo de árvore de decisão C5.0 e o modelo RFM. Os resultados da pesquisa descobriram oito mercados RFM e seis regras para varejistas online. As implicações práticas sugerem que a estrutura proposta e os resultados da pesquisa podem ajudar os gerentes de varejo a reter e expandir mercados de alto valor por meio de seus sistemas dinâmicos de CRM e PDV. Os valores dos clientes encontrados, mercados RFM, regras de associação de compras e regras de decisão de marketing podem ser descobertos por meio da estrutura desta pesquisa.

Os métodos de pesquisa visam o algoritmo apriori supervisionado, o algoritmo de árvore de decisão C5.0 e o modelo RFM. A pesquisa descobriu oito mercados RFM e seis regras para varejistas online. As implicações práticas sugerem que a estrutura proposta e os resultados da pesquisa podem ajudar os gerentes de varejo a reter e expandir mercados de alto valor por meio de seus sistemas dinâmicos de CRM e PDV. Esta pesquisa utiliza tecnologias de mineração de dados para extrair mercados e regras de alto valor para planos de marketing. As variáveis de pesquisa são fáceis de obter através dos sistemas dos varejistas. Os valores dos clientes encontrados, os mercados RFM, as regras de associação de compras e as regras de decisão de marketing podem ser descobertos por meio da estrutura desta pesquisa.

Title: Marketing optimization in retail banking
Authors: Sundararajan R.; Bhaskar T.; Sarkar A.; Dasaratha S.; Bal D.; Marasanapalle J.K.; Zmudzka B.; Bak K.
Abstract: In this paper, we address the problem of making optimal product offers to customers of a retail bank by using techniques including Markov chains, genetic algorithms, mathematical programming, and design of experiments. Our challenges were large problem size, uncertainty about estimates of customer responses to product offers, and practical issues in training and implementation. The solution had an estimated financial impact of around $20 million; it also provided other intangible benefits, including structured decision making, the capability of performing what-if analysis, and portability to other markets and portfolios. © 2011 INFORMS.

The paper proposes a hierarchical reference model for support vector machine based classification within this discipline. Title: Knowledge management and data mining for marketing
Authors: Shaw M.J.; Subramaniam C.; Tan G.W.; Welge M.E.
Abstract: Due to the proliferation of information systems and technology, businesses increasingly have the capability to accumulate huge amounts of customer data in large databases. However, much of the useful marketing insights into customer characteristics and their purchase patterns are largely hidden and untapped. Current emphasis on customer relationship management makes the marketing function an ideal application area to greatly benefit from the use of data mining tools for decision support. A systematic methodology that uses data mining and knowledge management techniques is proposed to manage the marketing knowledge and support marketing decisions. This methodology can be the basis for enhancing customer relationship management. © 2001 Elsevier Science B.V.

Uma metodologia sistemática que utiliza técnicas de mineração de dados e gestão do conhecimento é proposta para gerenciar o conhecimento de marketing e apoiar decisões de marketing. Title: Identification of influencers - Measuring influence in customer networks
Authors: Kiss C.; Bichler M.
Abstract: Viral marketing refers to marketing techniques that use social networks to produce increases in brand awareness through self-replicating viral diffusion of messages, analogous to the spread of pathological and computer viruses. The idea has successfully been used by marketers to reach a large number of customers rapidly. If data about the customer network is available, centrality measures provide a structural measure that can be used in decision support systems to select influencers and spread viral marketing campaigns in a customer network. Usage stimulation and churn management are examples of DSS applications, where centrality of customers does play a role. The literature on network theory describes a large number of such centrality measures. A critical question is which of these measures is best to select an initial set of customers for a marketing campaign, in order to achieve a maximum dissemination of messages. In this paper, we present the results of computational experiments based on call data from a telecom company to compare different centrality measures for the diffusion of marketing messages. We found a significant lift when using central customers in message diffusion, but also found differences in the various centrality measures depending on the underlying network topology and diffusion process. © 2008 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.

resumo: O marketing viral refere-se a técnicas de marketing que utilizam redes sociais para aumentar a conscientização da marca por meio da difusão viral de mensagens, semelhante à propagação de vírus patológicos e de computador. Essa abordagem tem sido utilizada com sucesso por profissionais de marketing para alcançar um grande número de clientes rapidamente. Quando há dados sobre a rede de clientes, medidas de centralidade podem ser utilizadas em sistemas de suporte à decisão para selecionar influenciadores e disseminar campanhas de marketing viral. Estímulo ao uso e gerenciamento de churn são exemplos de aplicações de sistemas de suporte à decisão, onde a centralidade dos clientes desempenha um papel importante. A literatura sobre teoria de redes descreve várias medidas de centralidade. Uma questão crítica é qual dessas medidas é a melhor para selecionar um conjunto inicial de clientes para uma campanha de marketing, visando a máxima disseminação das mensagens. Neste artigo, apresentamos os resultados de experimentos computacionais baseados em dados de chamadas de uma empresa de telecomunicações para comparar diferentes medidas de centralidade na difusão de mensagens de marketing. Encontramos um aumento significativo ao usar clientes centrais na difusão de mensagens, mas também identificamos diferenças nas várias medidas de centralidade dependendo da topologia da rede subjacente e do processo de difusão. © 2008 Elsevier B.V. Title: Integrating the voice of customers through call center emails into a decision support system for churn prediction
Authors: Coussement K.; Van den Poel D.
Abstract: We studied the problem of optimizing the performance of a DSS for churn prediction. In particular, we investigated the beneficial effect of adding the voice of customers through call center emails - i.e. textual information - to a churn-prediction system that only uses traditional marketing information. We found that adding unstructured, textual information into a conventional churn-prediction model resulted in a significant increase in predictive performance. From a managerial point of view, this integrated framework helps marketing-decision makers to better identify customers most prone to switch. Consequently, their customer retention campaigns can be targeted more effectively because the prediction method is better at detecting those customers who are likely to leave. © 2008 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.
Keywords: Binary classification modeling; Call center email; Churn prediction; Customer relationship management (CRM); Data mining; Text mining; Voice of customers (VOC)

This aligns with the Thinking AI category as it involves market analysis and targeting, helping marketing-decision makers identify customers likely to switch. resumo: Estudamos o problema de otimizar o desempenho de um sistema de suporte à decisão (DSS) para previsão de churn. Em particular, investigamos o efeito benéfico de adicionar a voz dos clientes por meio de e-mails de call center - ou seja, informações textuais - a um sistema de previsão de churn que utiliza apenas informações de marketing tradicionais. Descobrimos que a adição de informações textuais não estruturadas a um modelo convencional de previsão de churn resultou em um aumento significativo no desempenho preditivo. Do ponto de vista gerencial, essa estrutura integrada ajuda os tomadores de decisão de marketing a identificar melhor os clientes mais propensos a mudar. Consequentemente, suas campanhas de retenção de clientes podem ser direcionadas de forma mais eficaz, pois o método de previsão é melhor em detectar aqueles clientes que provavelmente deixarão. © 2008 Elsevier B.V. Title: Customer targeting: A neural network approach guided by genetic algorithms
Authors: Kim Y.; Street W.N.; Russell G.J.; Menczer F.
Abstract: One of the key problems in database marketing is the identification and profiling of households that are most likely to be interested in a particular product or service. Principal component analysis (PCA) of customer background information followed by logistic regression analysis of response behavior is commonly used by database marketers. In this paper, we propose a new approach that uses artificial neural networks (ANNs) guided by genetic algorithms (GAs) to target households. We show that the resulting selection rule is more accurate and more parsimonious than the PCA/logit rule when the manager has a clear decision criterion. Under vague decision criteria, the new procedure loses its advantage in interpretability, but is still more accurate than PCA/logit in targeting households. ©2005 INFORMS.

A análise de componentes principais (PCA) das informações de fundo dos clientes, seguida pela análise de regressão logística do comportamento de resposta, é comumente utilizada por profissionais de marketing de banco de dados. Neste artigo, propomos uma nova abordagem que utiliza redes neurais artificiais (ANNs) guiadas por algoritmos genéticos (GAs) para direcionar lares. Mostramos que a regra de seleção resultante é mais precisa e mais econômica do que a regra PCA/logit quando o gerente possui um critério de decisão claro. Sob critérios de decisão vagos, o novo procedimento perde sua vantagem em interpretabilidade, mas ainda é mais preciso do que PCA/logit na segmentação de lares. ©2005 INFORMS.

Title: Fostering B2B sales with customer big data analytics
Authors: Hallikainen, H; Savimäki, E; Laukkanen, T
Abstract: This study focuses on the use of big data analytics in managing B2B customer relationships and examines the effects of big data analytics on customer relationship performance and sales growth using a multi-industry dataset from 417 B2B firms. The study also examines whether analytics culture within a firm moderates these effects. The study finds that the use of customer big data significantly fosters sales growth (i.e. monetary performance outcomes) and enhances the customer relationship performance (non-monetary performance outcomes). However, the latter effect is stronger for firms which have an analytics culture which supports marketing analytics, whereas the former effect remains unchanged regardless of the analytics culture. The study empirically confirms that customer big data analytics improves customer relationship performance and sales growth in B2B firms.

O estudo também investiga se a cultura analítica dentro de uma empresa modera esses efeitos. Os resultados mostram que o uso de big data do cliente promove significativamente o crescimento das vendas (ou seja, resultados de desempenho monetário) e melhora o desempenho do relacionamento com o cliente (resultados de desempenho não monetário). No entanto, o efeito sobre o desempenho do relacionamento é mais forte em empresas que possuem uma cultura analítica que apoia análises de marketing, enquanto o efeito sobre o crescimento das vendas permanece inalterado, independentemente da cultura analítica. O estudo confirma empiricamente que a análise de big data do cliente melhora o desempenho do relacionamento com o cliente e o crescimento das vendas em empresas B2B.

Title: Personalized digital marketing recommender engine
Authors: Behera, RK; Gunasekaran, A; Gupta, S; Kamboj, S; Bala, PK
Abstract: E-business leverages digital channels to scale its functions and services and operates by connecting and retaining customers using marketing initiatives. To increase the likelihood of a sale, the business must recommend additional items that the customers may be unaware of or may find appealing. Recommender Engine (RE) is considered to be the preferred solution in these cases for reasons that include delivering relevant items, hence improving cart value, and boosting customer engagement. The paper describes a model for delivering real-time, personalised marketing information concerning the recommended items for online and offline customers, using a blend of selling strategies: up-selling, cross-selling, best-in-class-selling, needs-satisfaction-selling and consultative-selling. The model further defines the e-marketplace by clustering items, customers and unique selling proposition (USP), and then gathering, storing, and processing transactional data, and displaying personalised marketing information to support the customer in their decision-making process, even when purchasing from large item spaces. An experimental study using a quantitative research methodology was conducted in a mid-size healthcare retailer, based out of India, to determine the tangible benefits. The model was tested with 100 online customers and, with the adoption of the proposed methodology, the results indicated growth in average monthly revenue (33.49%), Average Order Value (AOV) (32.79%) and Items per Order (IPO) (1.93%).
Keywords: Personalized digital marketing; Recommender engine; Customer relationship management
rationale: The abstract describes a model that utilizes a recommender engine to deliver personalized marketing information, which aligns closely with the focus on personalization and targeting in Thinking AI. The model aims to enhance customer engagement and improve sales metrics, indicating a strategic analysis of customer behavior and preferences. The experimental study also highlights the application of marketing analytics to achieve measurable growth, which further supports its classification under Thinking AI.
resumo: O e-business utiliza canais digitais para expandir suas funções e serviços, conectando e retendo clientes por meio de iniciativas de marketing. Para aumentar a probabilidade de venda, o negócio deve recomendar itens adicionais que os clientes podem não conhecer ou achar atraentes. O Recommender Engine (RE) é a solução preferida nesses casos, pois entrega itens relevantes, melhorando o valor do carrinho e aumentando o engajamento do cliente. O artigo descreve um modelo para fornecer informações de marketing personalizadas em tempo real sobre os itens recomendados para clientes online e offline, utilizando uma combinação de estratégias de venda: upselling, cross-selling, best-in-class-selling, needs-satisfaction-selling e consultative-selling. O modelo também define o e-marketplace agrupando itens, clientes e proposta de venda única (USP), além de coletar, armazenar e processar dados transacionais, exibindo informações de marketing personalizadas para apoiar a decisão do cliente, mesmo em grandes espaços de itens. Um estudo experimental com metodologia de pesquisa quantitativa foi realizado em um varejista de saúde de médio porte na Índia para determinar os benefícios tangíveis. O modelo foi testado com 100 clientes online e, com a adoção da metodologia proposta, os resultados indicaram um crescimento na receita média mensal (33,49%), no Valor Médio do Pedido (AOV) (32,79%) e nos Itens por Pedido (IPO) (1,93%).

Title: How has data-driven marketing evolved: Challenges and opportunities with emerging technologies
Authors: Rosário A.T.; Dias J.C.
Abstract: This paper explores data-driven marketing, its benefits, and challenges to provide insights and a framework for business leaders and marketers to leverage in their marketing efforts. Using a systematic literature review with bibliometric analysis, we examined a sample of 98 studies indexed in SCOPUS to identify research activity on this topic until May 2023. Data-driven marketing and communications have gained popularity as companies and marketers prioritize leveraging consumer and market data to strategize and make informed decisions. Adopting and integrating various technologies into the company's systems is crucial for companies aiming to achieve a sustainable competitive advantage. By analyzing and interpreting customer data, companies can implement customer-centered marketing initiatives that enhance their experience and satisfaction with the brand, thus strengthening company-customer relationships. However, data-driven marketing faces several challenges, including consumer privacy concerns, data poisoning, information quality issues, and the need for adequate organizational changes. © 2023

O marketing e as comunicações orientados a dados ganharam popularidade à medida que empresas e profissionais de marketing priorizam a utilização de dados de consumidores e de mercado para formular estratégias e tomar decisões informadas. A adoção e a integração de diversas tecnologias nos sistemas da empresa são cruciais para aquelas que buscam alcançar uma vantagem competitiva sustentável. Ao analisar e interpretar dados de clientes, as empresas podem implementar iniciativas de marketing centradas no cliente que aprimoram sua experiência e satisfação com a marca, fortalecendo assim as relações entre a empresa e o cliente. No entanto, o marketing orientado a dados enfrenta vários desafios, incluindo preocupações com a privacidade do consumidor, contaminação de dados, problemas de qualidade da informação e a necessidade de mudanças organizacionais adequadas. © 2023

Title: Marketing segmentation through machine learning models: An approach based on customer relationship management and customer profitability accounting
Authors: Florez-Lopez R.; Ramon-Jeronimo J.M.
Abstract: Customer relationship management (CRM) aims to build relations with the most profitable clients by performing customer segmentation and designing appropriate marketing tools. In addition, customer profitability accounting (CPA) recommends evaluating the CRM program through the combination of partial measures in a global costĝ€"benefit function. Several statistical techniques have been applied for market segmentations although the existence of large data sets reduces their effectiveness. As an alternative, decision trees are machine learning models that do not consider a priori hypotheses, achieve a high performance, and generate logical rules clearly understood by managers. In this article, a three-stage methodology is proposed that combines marketing feature selection, customer segmentation through univariate and oblique decision trees, and a new CPA function based on marketing, data warehousing, and opportunity costs linked to the analysis of different scenarios. This proposal is applied to a large insurance marketing data set for alternative cost and price conditions showing the superiority of univariate decision trees over statistical techniques. © 2009 Sage Publications.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence; Costĝ€"benefit analysis; Customer profitability accounting; Customer relationship management; Marketing

The emphasis on using decision trees for customer segmentation and the overall methodology for market analysis aligns closely with the 'Thinking AI' category, which focuses on market analysis and targeting.
resumo: A gestão de relacionamento com o cliente (CRM) visa construir relações com os clientes mais lucrativos por meio da segmentação de clientes e do design de ferramentas de marketing apropriadas. A contabilidade de lucratividade do cliente (CPA) recomenda avaliar o programa de CRM através da combinação de medidas parciais em uma função global de custo-benefício. Embora várias técnicas estatísticas tenham sido aplicadas para segmentação de mercado, a existência de grandes conjuntos de dados reduz sua eficácia. Como alternativa, árvores de decisão são modelos de aprendizado de máquina que não consideram hipóteses a priori, alcançam alto desempenho e geram regras lógicas facilmente compreendidas pelos gestores. Este artigo propõe uma metodologia em três etapas que combina seleção de características de marketing, segmentação de clientes por meio de árvores de decisão univariadas e oblíquas, e uma nova função CPA baseada em marketing, armazenamento de dados e custos de oportunidade vinculados à análise de diferentes cenários. Essa proposta é aplicada a um grande conjunto de dados de marketing de seguros para condições alternativas de custo e preço, mostrando a superioridade das árvores de decisão univariadas sobre técnicas estatísticas.

Title: To establish online shoppers' markets and rules for dynamic CRM systems An empirical case study in Taiwan
Authors: Chiang, WY
Abstract: Purpose - The purpose of this paper is to establish customers' markets and rules of dynamic customer relationship management (CRM) systems for online retailers. Design/methodology/approach - This research proposes a procedure to discover customers' markets and rules, which adopts the recency, frequency, monetary value (RFM) variables, transaction records, and socioeconomic data of the online shoppers to be the research variables. The research methods aim at the supervised apriori algorithm, C5.0 decision tree algorithm, and RFM model. Findings - This research discovered eight RFM markets and six rules of online retailers. Practical implications - The proposed framework and research results can help retailer managers to retain and expand high value markets via their dynamic CRM and POS systems. Originality/value - This research uses data mining technologies to extract high value markets and rules for marketing plans. The research variables are easy to obtain via retailers' systems. The found customer values, RFM markets, shopping association rules, and marketing decision rules can be discovered via the framework of this research.

resumo: O objetivo deste artigo é estabelecer os mercados de clientes e as regras dos sistemas dinâmicos de gerenciamento de relacionamento com o cliente (CRM) para varejistas online. A pesquisa propõe um procedimento para descobrir os mercados e regras dos clientes, adotando as variáveis de recência, frequência e valor monetário (RFM), registros de transações e dados socioeconômicos dos compradores online como variáveis de pesquisa. Os métodos de pesquisa visam o algoritmo apriori supervisionado, o algoritmo de árvore de decisão C5.0 e o modelo RFM. A pesquisa descobriu oito mercados RFM e seis regras para varejistas online. As implicações práticas sugerem que a estrutura proposta e os resultados da pesquisa podem ajudar os gerentes de varejo a reter e expandir mercados de alto valor por meio de seus sistemas dinâmicos de CRM e PDV. Este estudo utiliza tecnologias de mineração de dados para extrair mercados e regras de alto valor para planos de marketing, sendo que as variáveis de pesquisa são fáceis de obter pelos sistemas dos varejistas. Os valores dos clientes encontrados, os mercados RFM, as regras de associação de compras e as regras de decisão de marketing podem ser descobertos por meio da estrutura desta pesquisa.

Title: An integrated model for predicting consumer's intention to write online reviews
Authors: Dixit S.; Jyoti Badgaiyan A.; Khare A.
Abstract: For marketers, consumers’ increasing use of online reviews in arriving at purchase decisions is a double edged sword. On one hand, it presents opportunity for manufacturers and sellers to be highlighted for their good work, but at the same time, there remains a possibility of negative review impacting goodwill and reputation. Hence, it is important for managers to identify factors that impact consumers’ intentions to write online reviews. This research delves into this aspect by trying to identify the factors that impact reviews writing intentions of consumers for restaurants. The study extends the theory of planned behaviour with additions of variables such as ego involvement, taking vengeance and helping a restaurant. For this, 252 valid responses were obtained, and structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed model. Results indicate that perceived behavioural control, subjective norms, ego involvement and taking vengeance are significant predictors of intention to write online reviews for the restaurants. © 2017 Elsevier Ltd
Keywords: Consumer behaviour; E-WOM; Intentions to write online reviews; Theory of planned behaviour
keywords: ['online reviews', 'consumer intentions', 'ego involvement', 'helping a restaurant', 'taking vengeance']
rationale: The abstract discusses factors that influence consumers' intentions to write online reviews, which directly relates to understanding customer emotions and motivations. The inclusion of variables such as ego involvement and helping a restaurant indicates a focus on understanding emotional needs and relational aspects of consumer behavior, thus aligning with the Feeling AI category. Additionally, the study aims to understand and meet customer emotional needs regarding their review behaviors.
resumo: Para os profissionais de marketing, o crescente uso de avaliações online pelos consumidores na tomada de decisões de compra é uma faca de dois gumes. Por um lado, isso oferece oportunidades para que fabricantes e vendedores sejam destacados por seu bom trabalho, mas, ao mesmo tempo, existe a possibilidade de que avaliações negativas impactem a boa vontade e a reputação. Portanto, é importante que os gerentes identifiquem os fatores que influenciam a intenção dos consumidores de escrever avaliações online. Esta pesquisa investiga esse aspecto ao tentar identificar os fatores que impactam a intenção de escrever avaliações de consumidores para restaurantes. O estudo amplia a teoria do comportamento planejado com a adição de variáveis como envolvimento do ego, desejo de vingança e ajuda a um restaurante. Para isso, foram obtidas 252 respostas válidas, e a modelagem de equações estruturais foi utilizada para testar o modelo proposto. Os resultados indicam que o controle comportamental percebido, normas subjetivas, envolvimento do ego e desejo de vingança são preditores significativos da intenção de escrever avaliações online para restaurantes.

Title: A varietal-specific approach to investigate wine risk perception in South Africa: Recommendations for Chenin blanc
Authors: Van der Colff N.; Pentz C.; Nieuwoudt H.
Abstract: Purpose: This study aims to describe South African consumers’ wine risk perception on varietal level with recommendations for Chenin blanc. Design/methodology/approach: An exploratory mixed methods approach was followed where qualitative data were used to develop the questionnaire. Quantitative data were collected from 2,051 respondents using an online survey. ANOVA and Fischer least significance difference tests were used to indicate statistical significance. Findings: Significant perceived risks (PRs) associated with Chenin blanc across age and ethnic groups were functional, time and financial risks. Risk-reducing strategies (RRS) in the white wine category were favourite brands and a trusted store, while Sauvignon blanc was also described as an RRS. Recommended Chenin blanc RRS include tastings and events with food. Research limitations/implications: Measurement of PR remains challenging. This research approach can be reproduced and/or adapted to investigate other struggling varietals and/or regions-of-origin. The convenience sample limits generalisability. Practical implications: Segments were identified to develop new markets for Chenin blanc. RRS emphasise the importance of real sensory experience rather than media exposure to build knowledge and familiarity. Originality/value: This study is a pioneering endeavour in terms of using an exploratory mixed methods research approach to investigate and describe risk perception of a specific wine varietal. Recommendations, with implications for strategic marketing decisions, are made for South African Chenin blanc. © 2019, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Chenin blanc; Consumer behaviour; Consumer risk perception; Risk perception; South African white wine; Varietal perceived risk scale
rationale: The abstract discusses consumer risk perception concerning Chenin blanc, which relates to understanding customer needs and wants. It emphasizes the importance of sensory experiences and interaction with the product, aligning with the objectives of Feeling AI to develop customer understanding and emotional connections. Additionally, the research recommends strategies aimed at enhancing consumer experience, indicating a focus on relationalization. The findings also highlight the need to tailor marketing efforts based on emotional factors, further solidifying its placement in the Feeling AI category.
resumo: Este estudo tem como objetivo descrever a percepção de risco dos consumidores sul-africanos em relação ao vinho Chenin blanc em nível varietal. Foi adotada uma abordagem mista exploratória, utilizando dados qualitativos para desenvolver o questionário e coletando dados quantitativos de 2.051 respondentes por meio de uma pesquisa online. Os testes ANOVA e Fischer foram usados para indicar significância estatística. Os riscos percebidos significativos associados ao Chenin blanc, variando entre grupos etários e étnicos, foram riscos funcionais, de tempo e financeiros. As estratégias de redução de risco na categoria de vinhos brancos incluíram marcas favoritas e lojas de confiança, sendo o Sauvignon blanc também descrito como uma estratégia de redução de risco. As recomendações para o Chenin blanc incluem degustações e eventos com comida. As limitações da pesquisa incluem a dificuldade na medição da percepção de risco e a amostra de conveniência que limita a generalização. Implicações práticas foram identificadas para desenvolver novos mercados para o Chenin blanc, enfatizando a importância da experiência sensorial real em vez da exposição à mídia. Este estudo é pioneiro ao usar uma abordagem de pesquisa mista exploratória para investigar e descrever a percepção de risco de um varietal específico de vinho, com recomendações para decisões de marketing estratégico para o Chenin blanc sul-africano.

Title: Toward a model of sparkling wine purchasing preferences
Authors: Verdonk N.; Wilkinson J.; Culbert J.; Ristic R.; Pearce K.; Wilkinson K.
Abstract: Purpose: This paper aims to provide further insight into factors influencing Australian consumers’ purchasing preferences for sparkling wine, including champagne. Design/methodology/approach: Focus groups were conducted and thematic analysis was undertaken to identify factors influencing sparkling wine consumers’ purchasing preferences. Findings: Personal taste was found to influence choice of a sparkling wine rather than another type of beverage, and selection of a particular style and brand of sparkling wine. Country or region of origin was found to be important, often linked to the product being champagne. Brand image, reputation and symbolism were found to influence purchase decisions (sometimes linked to consumption occasion), especially for purchases of gifts. Advice, recommendations and expert reviews, and consumption occasion also were found to influence purchase decisions. Price was found to influence style and brand of sparkling wine purchased. A high price was found to be a barrier for some participants, while other participants were found to avoid sparkling wines priced below some particular level. Thematic analysis enabled development of a preliminary model of purchasing preferences. Research limitations/implications: Being exploratory in nature, findings cannot be generalised. Further studies are required to confirm the preliminary model and to evaluate the validity and significance of proposed relationships. Practical implications: Findings suggest a producer could benefit from marketing a range of sparkling wines to cater to different tastes, occasions and gift purchases. Findings also confirm the importance of marketers pursuing opportunities to obtain and promote favourable expert reviews for their sparkling wines, and of identifying and promoting regional distinctiveness. Originality/value: The first comprehensive model of sparkling wine consumers’ purchasing preferences has been developed. Empirical testing would enable refinement and enhance understanding. © 2017, © Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Australia; Consumer behaviour; Psychometric/qualitative; Survey research; Wines
keywords: ['personal taste', 'brand image', 'reputation', 'consumption occasion', 'gift purchases', 'expert reviews', 'customer preferences']
rationale: The abstract discusses various factors influencing purchasing preferences for sparkling wine, which includes understanding customer emotional needs and preferences such as personal taste, brand image, and the significance of the consumption occasion. These factors relate closely to customer understanding and positioning, which are key aspects of Feeling AI. The mention of gift purchases also ties into emotional engagement with customers. While there are elements that could relate to Mechanical or Thinking AI, the predominant focus on emotional and personal factors aligns it more closely with Feeling AI.
resumo: Este artigo tem como objetivo fornecer uma visão mais aprofundada sobre os fatores que influenciam as preferências de compra dos consumidores australianos de vinho espumante, incluindo champanhe. Grupos focais foram realizados e uma análise temática foi realizada para identificar os fatores que influenciam as preferências de compra dos consumidores de vinho espumante. Os resultados mostraram que o gosto pessoal influencia a escolha de um vinho espumante em vez de outra bebida, assim como a seleção de um estilo e marca específicos. O país ou região de origem foi considerado importante, frequentemente associado ao produto ser champanhe. A imagem da marca, a reputação e o simbolismo também influenciam as decisões de compra, especialmente em compras de presentes. Conselhos, recomendações e avaliações de especialistas, bem como a ocasião de consumo, também foram identificados como influências nas decisões de compra. O preço impacta o estilo e a marca do vinho espumante adquirido, com um preço elevado sendo uma barreira para alguns participantes, enquanto outros evitam vinhos espumantes com preços abaixo de um determinado nível. A análise temática possibilitou o desenvolvimento de um modelo preliminar de preferências de compra. Como limitações da pesquisa, os achados não podem ser generalizados, e mais estudos são necessários para confirmar o modelo preliminar e avaliar a validade e a significância das relações propostas. As implicações práticas sugerem que um produtor poderia se beneficiar ao comercializar uma variedade de vinhos espumantes para atender a diferentes gostos, ocasiões e compras de presentes. Os resultados também confirmam a importância de os profissionais de marketing buscarem oportunidades para obter e promover avaliações favoráveis de especialistas para seus vinhos espumantes, além de identificar e promover a distintividade regional. Um modelo abrangente das preferências de compra dos consumidores de vinho espumante foi desenvolvido, e testes empíricos poderiam aprimorar e aprofundar a compreensão.

Title: Attitude toward smoking: The effect of negative smoking-related pictures
Authors: Grigaliunaite V.; Pileliene L.
Abstract: Research background: Endeavouring to develop healthy societies is a primary goal in many countries. As smoking is a major problem of public health, lowering the extent of smoking is one of the conditions for developing a healthy society. Based on the research revealing that the pairing of the product with negative stimuli enhances the possibility of negative reaction to the product as negative stimulus transfers it's meaning to the product, tobacco packaging was labelled with negative smoking-related pictures illustrating the danger of smoking. Nevertheless, the extent of smoking is still large in many countries. Hence, the effect of negative smoking-related pictures has been the subject of intense debate within the scientific community. Purpose of the article: The aim of this research is to determine the effect of negative smoking-related pictures on the both implicit and explicit attitude toward smoking. Methods: For the purpose of determining the effect of negative smoking-related pictures on the both implicit and explicit attitude toward smoking, Implicit Association Test and questionnaire survey were provided. The questionnaire was elaborated based on the analysis and synthesis of scientific literature. Findings & Value added: The theoretical analysis substantiated the influence of attitude toward the product on consumer purchase decisions. Nevertheless, people do not always want to reveal their opinion, hence traditional marketing research methods for measuring explicit attitude are not sufficient as they are often not objective. Therefore, neuromarketing research methods complement traditional marketing research methods by providing more objectivity. Consequently, the Implicit Association Test and traditional questionnaire research are applied for the empirical research, revealing the effect of negative smokingrelated pictures on the both implicit and explicit attitude toward smoking. The recommendations for the usage of negative smoking-related pictures on purpose to influence attitude toward smoking and consumer purchase behaviour are substantiated. © 2017 Nicolaus Copernicus University. All rights reserved.
Keywords: Consumer behaviour; Explicit attitude; Mplicit attitude; Negative pictures; Smoking
keywords: ['negative stimuli', 'attitude', 'consumer purchase decisions', 'implicit and explicit attitude', 'emotional data']
rationale: The abstract discusses the impact of negative smoking-related pictures on attitudes toward smoking, which relates directly to understanding customer emotions and attitudes. The research aims to measure implicit and explicit attitudes, indicating a focus on emotional responses and customer understanding. Thus, it aligns with the objectives related to customer understanding and emotional needs, fitting well within the Feeling AI category.
resumo: O desenvolvimento de sociedades saudáveis é um objetivo primordial em muitos países, e a redução do tabagismo, um grande problema de saúde pública, é uma condição essencial para alcançar esse objetivo. A pesquisa indica que a associação de produtos com estímulos negativos pode aumentar a reação negativa ao produto, levando à utilização de imagens relacionadas ao perigo do tabagismo nas embalagens de tabaco. Apesar disso, o tabagismo ainda é prevalente em muitos lugares, gerando debates sobre a eficácia dessas imagens. Este estudo visa determinar o impacto dessas imagens negativas nas atitudes implícitas e explícitas em relação ao tabagismo, utilizando o Teste de Associação Implícita e questionários. A análise teórica confirma que a atitude em relação ao produto influencia as decisões de compra dos consumidores, mas métodos tradicionais de pesquisa de marketing podem não ser objetivos. Assim, métodos de neuromarketing complementam esses métodos tradicionais, proporcionando maior objetividade. A pesquisa empírica revela o efeito das imagens negativas sobre as atitudes em relação ao tabagismo e oferece recomendações para o uso dessas imagens a fim de influenciar atitudes e comportamentos de compra.

Title: Mobile shopping behaviour: Insights into attitudes, shopping process involvement and location
Authors: Holmes A.; Byrne A.; Rowley J.
Abstract: Purpose: Although there is evidence that adoption of mobile shopping has been slow, the increased functionality offered by smart phones offers significant potential for the development of marketing and retailing through the mobile channel. The purpose of this paper is to add to knowledge on consumer shopping behaviour through mobile devices by exploring attitudes to the use of mobiles in shopping, the use of mobile phones at different stages in the consumer decision-making process, the impact of involvement on the mobile consumer decision-making process and mobile shopping location. Design/methodology/approach: An online panel survey was conducted with a UK panel of nationally representative consumers. The survey collected data in respect of the following products that were ranked on level of involvement on the basis of the importance and effort consumers' associated with their purchase: bread (lowest), washing powder, DVD, footwear, phone and TV (highest). Findings: Use of mobiles for shopping is significant, but remains lower than use of computers in shopping. In general, respondents were more positive regarding their use of computer shopping than they were in relation to their use of a mobile. In using their mobile phone in shopping, respondents value its convenience and accessibility. There is higher use of the mobile phone in the information search and consideration of alternatives phases, than in the purchase transaction. The extent of use of mobile devices in the decision-making process is higher with higher involvement products, in relation to all stages in the decision-making process. The most frequent location for the use of their mobile in shopping is at home, which is consistent with the finding that the highest level of use of mobiles occurs in the information search and consideration of alternatives phases. Recommendations are offered for retailers and for further research. Originality/value: This is the first research to explore the use of mobile phones in different stages in the consumer-decision-making process across a number of product categories. © Emerald Group Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Consumer behaviour; Consumer decision making; Involvement; Mobile shopping; Smart phones
rationale: The abstract explores consumer attitudes and behaviors in mobile shopping, focusing on how emotional aspects like convenience and accessibility influence their decision-making process. It emphasizes understanding customer needs during different stages of shopping, aligning well with the objectives of Feeling AI, which aims to understand and meet customer emotional needs and wants.
resumo: O objetivo deste artigo é ampliar o conhecimento sobre o comportamento de compra dos consumidores por meio de dispositivos móveis, explorando atitudes em relação ao uso de celulares nas compras, a utilização de telefones móveis em diferentes etapas do processo de decisão do consumidor, o impacto do envolvimento no processo de decisão de compra móvel e a localização das compras móveis. Foi realizada uma pesquisa online com um painel representativo de consumidores do Reino Unido, coletando dados sobre produtos classificados por nível de envolvimento. Os resultados mostram que o uso de celulares para compras é significativo, mas ainda inferior ao uso de computadores. Os entrevistados demonstraram uma atitude mais positiva em relação às compras por computador do que por celular, valorizando a conveniência e acessibilidade dos dispositivos móveis. O uso do celular é mais frequente nas fases de busca de informações e consideração de alternativas do que na transação de compra. O uso de dispositivos móveis aumenta com produtos de maior envolvimento em todas as etapas do processo decisório, sendo que o local mais comum para o uso do celular nas compras é em casa. Recomendações são feitas para varejistas e para pesquisas futuras. Este é o primeiro estudo a explorar o uso de celulares em diferentes etapas do processo de decisão do consumidor em várias categorias de produtos.

Title: The effects of blogger recommendations on customers' online shopping intentions
Authors: Hsu C.-L.; Lin J.C.-C.; Chiang H.-S.
Abstract: Purpose: Blogging has become part of a consumer's decision making process when shopping online; however, the understanding of blog recommendation's effect on consumer purchase decision is still vague. The purpose of this study is to examine whether the blog reader's trusting belief in the blogger is significant in relation to the perceived usefulness of the blogger's recommendations; and how the blog reader's perceptions influence his/her attitude and purchasing behavior online. The moderating effect of blogger's reputation on readers' purchasing intentions is also tested. Design/methodology/approach: Based on various theories, a model was proposed in this study. A survey involving 327 blog readers as participants was analyzed in the empirical study to investigate whether the usefulness of bloggers' recommendations and trusting beliefs toward blogger had influence on consumers' attitudes and behavioral intentions toward online shopping. Findings: The results indicated that perceived usefulness of bloggers' recommendations and trust had significant influential effect on blog users' attitude towards and intention to shop online. Moreover, the findings showed that different determinants affected the users of perceived-high-reputation and perceived-low-reputation blogs. Originality/value: The findings suggest bloggers' electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) to be a promising marketing strategy for increasing sales. The marketers should provide free trial products and services to the perceived-high-reputation bloggers who, as valued opinion leaders, will influence and prompt others to shop online through a trusting effect. As for perceived-low-reputation bloggers, the marketing strategists should strive to emphasize the usefulness of products and services being marketed, so these perceived-low-reputation bloggers can focus more on describing the advantages and benefits of products or services discussed in their blogs. © Emerald Group Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Blogging; Blogs; Consumer behaviour; Electronic commerce; Online shopping; Recommendations; Reputation; Trust
rationale: The abstract focuses on the emotional and relational aspects of consumer behavior influenced by bloggers' recommendations. It highlights the importance of trust and perceived usefulness in shaping consumers' attitudes and purchasing decisions, which aligns with the objectives of Feeling AI to understand customer emotional needs and tailor experiences. The findings suggest a significant emotional engagement with the content provided by bloggers, particularly regarding their reputation, which further emphasizes the emotional connection in consumer decision-making.
resumo: O propósito deste estudo é examinar se a crença de confiança do leitor de blogs no blogueiro é significativa em relação à utilidade percebida das recomendações do blogueiro, e como as percepções do leitor influenciam sua atitude e comportamento de compra online. O efeito moderador da reputação do blogueiro nas intenções de compra dos leitores também foi testado. A pesquisa analisou 327 leitores de blogs para investigar se a utilidade das recomendações dos blogueiros e as crenças de confiança influenciam as atitudes e intenções comportamentais dos consumidores em relação às compras online. Os resultados indicaram que a utilidade percebida das recomendações dos blogueiros e a confiança tiveram um efeito significativo nas atitudes dos usuários de blogs em relação à compra online. Além disso, diferentes determinantes afetaram os usuários de blogs de alta e baixa reputação. As descobertas sugerem que o boca a boca eletrônico (eWOM) dos blogueiros é uma estratégia de marketing promissora para aumentar as vendas. Os profissionais de marketing devem fornecer produtos e serviços de teste gratuito para blogueiros de alta reputação, que, como líderes de opinião valorizados, influenciarão outros a comprar online por meio de um efeito de confiança. Para blogueiros de baixa reputação, os estrategistas de marketing devem enfatizar a utilidade dos produtos e serviços, permitindo que esses blogueiros se concentrem mais na descrição das vantagens e benefícios dos produtos discutidos em seus blogs.

Title: Homo economicus and social marketing: Questioning traditional models of behavior
Authors: Carvalho H.C.; Mazzon J.A.
Abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this paper is to bring forth the limitations of some important models of cognition and behavior adopted by social marketers and present important findings from recent lines of research that contribute to a fine-grained understanding of human behavior. Design/methodology/approach: This is a conceptual paper that presents a review of several theoretical approaches to human cognition and behavior and their implications regarding social marketing campaigns. Findings: It is concluded that the assumptions underlying traditional models of behavior need to be revised, especially the assumption that human beings are rational decision makers - the prototypical homo economicus. Behavioral science has revealed that people are far from being rational and are prone to be influenced by myriad factors, some deemed irrelevant under rational models. Social marketing interventions have greater probability of success when they rely on more realistic assumptions of human behavior. Research limitations/implications: Social marketing needs to embrace the contributions of the several disciplines and lines of research centered on the study of all facets of human behavior, such as behavioral economics and dual-system framework. Practical implications: The main implications are: the recommendation to assume people are running on their System 1 when they are in contact with social marketing campaigns, the need to consider the interplay of systems and selves over time, the recommended emphasis on place strategies, and the need to avoid cash incentives and silver bullets. Originality/value: The value of this paper is in contrasting the assumptions of traditional models of cognition and behavior widely used in social marketing with the evidence from several lines of research portraying influences in human behavior not accounted by those models. © Emerald Group Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Cognition; Consumer attitudes; Consumer behaviour; Social marketing; Social marketing theory; Theory of planned behaviour
rationale: The abstract discusses the limitations of traditional models of cognition and behavior in social marketing, emphasizing the importance of understanding human behavior beyond rational decision-making. This aligns with the Feeling AI category, as it focuses on customer understanding and emotional influences on decisions. The recommendation to consider emotional and psychological factors in social marketing campaigns further supports this classification.
resumo: O objetivo deste artigo é destacar as limitações de alguns modelos importantes de cognição e comportamento adotados por profissionais de marketing social e apresentar descobertas relevantes de pesquisas recentes que contribuem para uma compreensão mais detalhada do comportamento humano. Este é um artigo conceitual que revisa várias abordagens teóricas sobre cognição e comportamento humano e suas implicações para campanhas de marketing social. Conclui-se que as suposições subjacentes aos modelos tradicionais de comportamento precisam ser revisadas, especialmente a suposição de que os seres humanos são tomadores de decisão racionais - o protótipo do homo economicus. A ciência do comportamento revelou que as pessoas estão longe de ser racionais e são influenciadas por uma infinidade de fatores, alguns considerados irrelevantes sob modelos racionais. As intervenções de marketing social têm maior probabilidade de sucesso quando se baseiam em suposições mais realistas sobre o comportamento humano. O marketing social precisa abraçar as contribuições de várias disciplinas e linhas de pesquisa centradas no estudo de todas as facetas do comportamento humano, como a economia comportamental e o modelo de sistemas duais. As principais implicações práticas incluem a recomendação de considerar que as pessoas operam em seu Sistema 1 ao interagir com campanhas de marketing social, a necessidade de considerar a interação de sistemas e identidades ao longo do tempo, a ênfase em estratégias de local e a necessidade de evitar incentivos em dinheiro e soluções simplistas. O valor deste artigo reside em contrastar as suposições dos modelos tradicionais de cognição e comportamento amplamente utilizados no marketing social com evidências de várias linhas de pesquisa que retratam influências no comportamento humano não contabilizadas por esses modelos.

Title: How packaging affects the product preferences of children and the buyer behaviour of their parents in the food industry
Authors: Ogba I.E.; Johnson R.
Abstract: Purpose – Health is becoming an increasingly important issue in the UK as well as the rest of Europe. Emphasis on the importance of healthy eating is ongoing for many reasons, including the growing concern about childhood obesity resulting in the ban of advertising of unhealthy foods to children in the UK in April 2007. However, although legislation has been placed upon the advertising of unhealthy food products, no such restrictions have been placed on the packaging of children's foods despite the influence of packaging on consumer buyer decisions. This paper aims to investigate the effect of packaging on children's product preferences and its ability to influence parents' buyer decision in-store. Design/methodology/approach – The study was approached from the parents' rather than the children's perspective. A quantitative approach was adopted in data collection, using a 28 item Likert scaled questionnaire administered to 150 parents, with over 95 percent response rate. Findings – The study shows that packaging does affect the product preferences of children. Also, children are particularly interested in influencing the purchase of unhealthy foods. However, parents within the study claimed that they did not succumb to their children's requests for the purchase of unhealthy food, which contradicts evidence from previous findings. Research limitations/implications – The claim by parents that they did not succumb to their children's requests for unhealthy food contradicts findings from previous research. This therefore leads to a recommendation for further studies as social desirability bias may have influenced the outcomes of the findings. Practical implications – Findings from this study can be applied within the retail and service marketing sector to provide the practitioner with information relevant to decision making on children's influence on parents buyer behavior in-store. Outcomes of the study are also important when considering the future of children's food marketing and tackling the issue of childhood obesity. Originality/value – The paper demonstrates that there is a relationship between packaging and children product preferences and children's influence on parents' buyer decision in-store. © 2010, Emerald Group Publishing Limited
Keywords: Children (age groups); Consumer behaviour; Decision making; Food packaging; Parents; United Kingdom
rationale: The abstract discusses the influence of packaging on children's product preferences and how this affects parents' buying decisions. This ties to the understanding of customer emotions and the relational aspect of marketing, particularly the emotional influence that children have on their parents' purchasing behavior. The focus on emotional data and understanding customer needs aligns well with the Feeling AI category.
resumo: A saúde está se tornando uma questão cada vez mais importante no Reino Unido e na Europa, com ênfase na alimentação saudável devido à crescente preocupação com a obesidade infantil, resultando na proibição da publicidade de alimentos não saudáveis para crianças no Reino Unido em abril de 2007. No entanto, apesar da legislação sobre a publicidade de produtos alimentares não saudáveis, não há restrições semelhantes sobre a embalagem de alimentos para crianças, que influencia as decisões de compra dos consumidores. Este estudo investiga o efeito da embalagem nas preferências de produtos das crianças e sua capacidade de influenciar as decisões de compra dos pais nas lojas. A pesquisa foi realizada sob a perspectiva dos pais, utilizando um questionário de 28 itens em escala Likert aplicado a 150 pais, com uma taxa de resposta superior a 95%. Os resultados mostram que a embalagem afeta as preferências de produtos das crianças, que estão particularmente interessadas em influenciar a compra de alimentos não saudáveis. No entanto, os pais afirmaram que não cederam aos pedidos de seus filhos por alimentos não saudáveis, o que contradiz evidências de pesquisas anteriores. Essa contradição sugere a necessidade de novos estudos, pois o viés de desejabilidade social pode ter influenciado os resultados. As conclusões deste estudo podem ser aplicadas no setor de marketing de varejo e serviços, fornecendo informações relevantes para a tomada de decisões sobre a influência das crianças no comportamento de compra dos pais. Os resultados também são importantes ao considerar o futuro do marketing de alimentos para crianças e o combate à obesidade infantil. O artigo demonstra a relação entre embalagem e preferências de produtos das crianças, bem como a influência das crianças nas decisões de compra dos pais nas lojas.

Title: Anticipating a regrettable purchase: Implications of erroneous affective forecasting for marketing planning
Authors: Sevdalis N.; Kokkinaki F.; Harvey N.
Abstract: Purpose - The purpose of this paper is to present the concept of consumers' erroneous affective self-forecasts, and discuss the implications of such forecasts for consumer purchasing behaviour and marketing planning. Design/methodology/approach - First, the literature on inaction inertia - the lowering of the likelihood that a bargain will be taken once a better bargain has been missed - is reviewed. Second, the literature on affective self-forecasting is reviewed. Finally, the implications that the authors synthesis of the behavioural evidence carries for marketing are discussed. Findings - The in action inertia literature implicates the regret that consumers associate with purchasing a discounted item once they have missed a much larger discount on it as a major contributing factor to consumers' unwillingness to purchase the item on the second occasion. The literature on affective self-prediction suggests that regret (and other emotions) is systematically mispredicted. Research limitations/implications - The likely effect of erroneously anticipated regret in inaction inertia situations is depressed purchasing behaviour. The paper argues that because affective anticipations are typically erroneous, their impact on consumer decision-making processes cannot be deemed rational. It is proposed that marketing should intervene to either increase the accuracy of such anticipations, or to lead consumers to discount them. Practical implications - Price promotions can have negative side effects, such as those observed in inaction inertia circumstances. To some extent, these are driven by consumers anticipated regret (and possibly other relevant emotions). Marketing techniques can counteract the disproportionate impact of such emotions. Originality/value - The paper offers a synthesis of behavioural evidence on inaction inertia and affective self-forecasting - two quite separate literatures that have yet to be brought together in the present context. In addition, the paper outlines implications for marketing and suggests possible strategies to moderate the discussed effects.
Keywords: Advertising; Consumer behaviour; Decision making; Pricing; Sales forecasting
rationale: The abstract discusses how consumers' emotional responses, particularly feelings of regret and affective self-forecasting, impact their purchasing behavior. The findings indicate that these emotional anticipations can lead to inaction inertia, where consumers are less likely to purchase after missing a better deal. This aligns with the Feeling AI category, which focuses on understanding customer emotions and tailoring marketing strategies to address these emotional needs.
resumo: O objetivo deste artigo é apresentar o conceito de previsões afetivas errôneas dos consumidores e discutir as implicações dessas previsões para o comportamento de compra e o planejamento de marketing. O artigo revisa a literatura sobre inação inércia, que se refere à diminuição da probabilidade de um consumidor aproveitar uma oferta após perder uma oferta melhor, e a literatura sobre previsão afetiva. Os resultados indicam que o arrependimento associado à compra de um item com desconto, após perder um desconto maior, é um fator importante que contribui para a relutância dos consumidores em comprar o item novamente. Além disso, a literatura sugere que o arrependimento e outras emoções são sistematicamente mal previstos. As limitações da pesquisa indicam que o arrependimento antecipado incorretamente pode levar a um comportamento de compra deprimido. O artigo argumenta que, como as antecipações afetivas geralmente são errôneas, seu impacto nos processos de decisão do consumidor não pode ser considerado racional. Propõe-se que o marketing intervenha para aumentar a precisão dessas antecipações ou para levar os consumidores a desconsiderá-las. As promoções de preços podem ter efeitos colaterais negativos, impulsionados pelo arrependimento antecipado dos consumidores. Técnicas de marketing podem ajudar a contrabalançar o impacto desproporcional dessas emoções. O artigo oferece uma síntese das evidências comportamentais sobre inação inércia e previsão afetiva, duas literaturas distintas que ainda não foram integradas. Além disso, o artigo delineia implicações para o marketing e sugere estratégias possíveis para moderar os efeitos discutidos.

Title: The fallout from French nuclear testing in the South Pacific: A longitudinal study of consumer boycotts
Authors: Ettenson R.; Klein J.G.
Abstract: Purpose - The frequency and sophistication of consumer boycotts continue to increase from already high levels. Surprisingly, only limited research in marketing has investigated this topic. The purpose of this paper is to provide a strategic analysis of an actual consumer protest with implications for better managerial decisions. Design/methodology/approach - The animosity model of consumer purchase behavior was employed in two longitudinal studies to investigate an ongoing marketplace protest - Australian consumers' boycott of French products. Study 1 was carried out while France was engaged in nuclear testing in the South Pacific. Study 2 was carried out 1 year after the resolution of the conflict. Findings - Results from Study 1 show that Australian consumers' animosity toward France was negatively related to their willingness to purchase French products. Consistent with a key prediction from the animosity model, this effect was independent of evaluations of French product quality. The findings from Study 2 show that, a year after the cessation of nuclear testing, Australian consumers continue to have strong negative affect toward France, which in turn, had negative marketplace consequences for French products. Originality/value - While the results from Study 1 show that consumer anger over nuclear testing did not necessarily lead to the denigration of the quality of French goods, the second study indicates that, beyond the duration of the official protest, there may be repercussions for products associated with the offending party. Accordingly, managers should consider implementing communications programs which, over time, effectively reinforce the quality of their products in the minds of protesting consumers. © Emerald Group Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Brands; Consumer behaviour; International business
rationale: The abstract discusses consumer boycotts driven by emotional responses such as animosity and negative affect towards a country due to its actions. The findings emphasize the importance of understanding customer emotions and their impact on purchasing behavior, which aligns closely with the focus on customer understanding and emotional needs in the Feeling AI category.
resumo: O propósito deste artigo é fornecer uma análise estratégica de um protesto de consumidores, com implicações para decisões gerenciais. Utilizando o modelo de animosidade do comportamento de compra do consumidor, foram realizados dois estudos longitudinais para investigar o boicote de consumidores australianos a produtos franceses. O Estudo 1 foi realizado durante os testes nucleares da França no Pacífico Sul, e os resultados mostraram que a animosidade dos consumidores australianos em relação à França estava negativamente relacionada à disposição de comprar produtos franceses, independentemente da avaliação da qualidade desses produtos. O Estudo 2, realizado um ano após a resolução do conflito, revelou que os consumidores australianos ainda mantinham uma forte aversão à França, resultando em consequências negativas para os produtos franceses no mercado. Os resultados sugerem que, mesmo após o término do protesto oficial, pode haver repercussões para os produtos associados à parte ofensora, indicando que os gerentes devem considerar a implementação de programas de comunicação que reforcem a qualidade de seus produtos na mente dos consumidores em protesto ao longo do tempo.

Title: The effects of blogger recommendations on customers' online shopping intentions
Authors: Hsu C.-L.; Lin J.C.-C.; Chiang H.-S.
Abstract: Purpose: Blogging has become part of a consumer's decision making process when shopping online; however, the understanding of blog recommendation's effect on consumer purchase decision is still vague. The purpose of this study is to examine whether the blog reader's trusting belief in the blogger is significant in relation to the perceived usefulness of the blogger's recommendations; and how the blog reader's perceptions influence his/her attitude and purchasing behavior online. The moderating effect of blogger's reputation on readers' purchasing intentions is also tested. Design/methodology/approach: Based on various theories, a model was proposed in this study. A survey involving 327 blog readers as participants was analyzed in the empirical study to investigate whether the usefulness of bloggers' recommendations and trusting beliefs toward blogger had influence on consumers' attitudes and behavioral intentions toward online shopping. Findings: The results indicated that perceived usefulness of bloggers' recommendations and trust had significant influential effect on blog users' attitude towards and intention to shop online. Moreover, the findings showed that different determinants affected the users of perceived-high-reputation and perceived-low-reputation blogs. Originality/value: The findings suggest bloggers' electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) to be a promising marketing strategy for increasing sales. The marketers should provide free trial products and services to the perceived-high-reputation bloggers who, as valued opinion leaders, will influence and prompt others to shop online through a trusting effect. As for perceived-low-reputation bloggers, the marketing strategists should strive to emphasize the usefulness of products and services being marketed, so these perceived-low-reputation bloggers can focus more on describing the advantages and benefits of products or services discussed in their blogs. © Emerald Group Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Blogging; Blogs; Consumer behaviour; Electronic commerce; Online shopping; Recommendations; Reputation; Trust
rationale: The abstract focuses on the emotional and relational aspects of consumer behavior influenced by bloggers' recommendations. It highlights the importance of trust and perceived usefulness in shaping consumers' attitudes and purchasing decisions, which aligns with the objectives of Feeling AI to understand customer emotional needs and tailor experiences. The findings suggest a significant emotional engagement with the content provided by bloggers, particularly regarding their reputation, which further emphasizes the emotional connection in consumer decision-making.
resumo: O objetivo deste estudo é examinar a influência da crença de confiança do leitor de blogs no blogueiro em relação à utilidade percebida das recomendações do blogueiro e como essas percepções afetam a atitude e o comportamento de compra online. Também foi testado o efeito moderador da reputação do blogueiro nas intenções de compra dos leitores. A pesquisa analisou 327 leitores de blogs para investigar se a utilidade das recomendações dos blogueiros e as crenças de confiança influenciam as atitudes e intenções comportamentais dos consumidores em relação às compras online. Os resultados indicaram que a utilidade percebida das recomendações e a confiança tiveram um efeito significativo nas atitudes dos usuários de blogs em relação à compra online. Além disso, diferentes determinantes afetaram os usuários de blogs de alta e baixa reputação. As descobertas sugerem que o boca a boca eletrônico (eWOM) dos blogueiros é uma estratégia de marketing promissora para aumentar as vendas. Os profissionais de marketing devem fornecer produtos e serviços de teste gratuito para blogueiros de alta reputação, que, como líderes de opinião valorizados, influenciarão outros a comprar online. Para blogueiros de baixa reputação, os estrategistas de marketing devem enfatizar a utilidade dos produtos e serviços, permitindo que esses blogueiros se concentrem mais em descrever as vantagens e benefícios dos produtos discutidos em seus blogs.
