Title: Mobile shopping behaviour: Insights into attitudes, shopping process involvement and location
Authors: Holmes A.; Byrne A.; Rowley J.
Abstract: Purpose: Although there is evidence that adoption of mobile shopping has been slow, the increased functionality offered by smart phones offers significant potential for the development of marketing and retailing through the mobile channel. The purpose of this paper is to add to knowledge on consumer shopping behaviour through mobile devices by exploring attitudes to the use of mobiles in shopping, the use of mobile phones at different stages in the consumer decision-making process, the impact of involvement on the mobile consumer decision-making process and mobile shopping location. Design/methodology/approach: An online panel survey was conducted with a UK panel of nationally representative consumers. The survey collected data in respect of the following products that were ranked on level of involvement on the basis of the importance and effort consumers' associated with their purchase: bread (lowest), washing powder, DVD, footwear, phone and TV (highest). Findings: Use of mobiles for shopping is significant, but remains lower than use of computers in shopping. In general, respondents were more positive regarding their use of computer shopping than they were in relation to their use of a mobile. In using their mobile phone in shopping, respondents value its convenience and accessibility. There is higher use of the mobile phone in the information search and consideration of alternatives phases, than in the purchase transaction. The extent of use of mobile devices in the decision-making process is higher with higher involvement products, in relation to all stages in the decision-making process. The most frequent location for the use of their mobile in shopping is at home, which is consistent with the finding that the highest level of use of mobiles occurs in the information search and consideration of alternatives phases. Recommendations are offered for retailers and for further research. Originality/value: This is the first research to explore the use of mobile phones in different stages in the consumer-decision-making process across a number of product categories. © Emerald Group Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Consumer behaviour; Consumer decision making; Involvement; Mobile shopping; Smart phones
rationale: The abstract explores consumer attitudes and behaviors in mobile shopping, focusing on how emotional aspects like convenience and accessibility influence their decision-making process. It emphasizes understanding customer needs during different stages of shopping, aligning well with the objectives of Feeling AI, which aims to understand and meet customer emotional needs and wants.
resumo: O objetivo deste artigo é ampliar o conhecimento sobre o comportamento de compra dos consumidores por meio de dispositivos móveis, explorando atitudes em relação ao uso de celulares nas compras, a utilização de telefones móveis em diferentes etapas do processo de decisão do consumidor, o impacto do envolvimento no processo de decisão de compra móvel e a localização das compras móveis. Foi realizada uma pesquisa com um painel online de consumidores representativos do Reino Unido, coletando dados sobre produtos classificados por nível de envolvimento. Os resultados mostram que, embora o uso de celulares para compras seja significativo, ainda é inferior ao uso de computadores. Os entrevistados demonstraram uma atitude mais positiva em relação às compras por computador. A conveniência e acessibilidade dos celulares foram valorizadas, com maior uso durante a busca de informações e consideração de alternativas do que na transação de compra. O uso de dispositivos móveis é mais frequente em produtos de maior envolvimento em todas as etapas do processo decisório, sendo que a maioria das compras móveis ocorre em casa. Recomendações são oferecidas para varejistas e para pesquisas futuras. Este é o primeiro estudo a explorar o uso de celulares em diferentes etapas do processo de decisão do consumidor em várias categorias de produtos.

Title: An integrated model for predicting consumer's intention to write online reviews
Authors: Dixit S.; Jyoti Badgaiyan A.; Khare A.
Abstract: For marketers, consumers’ increasing use of online reviews in arriving at purchase decisions is a double edged sword. On one hand, it presents opportunity for manufacturers and sellers to be highlighted for their good work, but at the same time, there remains a possibility of negative review impacting goodwill and reputation. Hence, it is important for managers to identify factors that impact consumers’ intentions to write online reviews. This research delves into this aspect by trying to identify the factors that impact reviews writing intentions of consumers for restaurants. The study extends the theory of planned behaviour with additions of variables such as ego involvement, taking vengeance and helping a restaurant. For this, 252 valid responses were obtained, and structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed model. Results indicate that perceived behavioural control, subjective norms, ego involvement and taking vengeance are significant predictors of intention to write online reviews for the restaurants. © 2017 Elsevier Ltd
Keywords: Consumer behaviour; E-WOM; Intentions to write online reviews; Theory of planned behaviour
keywords: ['online reviews', 'consumer intentions', 'ego involvement', 'helping a restaurant', 'taking vengeance']
rationale: The abstract discusses factors that influence consumers' intentions to write online reviews, which directly relates to understanding customer emotions and motivations. The inclusion of variables such as ego involvement and helping a restaurant indicates a focus on understanding emotional needs and relational aspects of consumer behavior, thus aligning with the Feeling AI category. Additionally, the study aims to understand and meet customer emotional needs regarding their review behaviors.
resumo: Para os profissionais de marketing, o crescente uso de avaliações online pelos consumidores na tomada de decisões de compra é uma faca de dois gumes. Por um lado, isso oferece oportunidades para que fabricantes e vendedores sejam destacados por seu bom trabalho, mas, ao mesmo tempo, existe a possibilidade de que avaliações negativas impactem a boa vontade e a reputação. Portanto, é importante que os gerentes identifiquem os fatores que influenciam a intenção dos consumidores de escrever avaliações online. Esta pesquisa investiga esse aspecto ao tentar identificar os fatores que impactam a intenção de escrever avaliações de consumidores sobre restaurantes. O estudo amplia a teoria do comportamento planejado com a adição de variáveis como envolvimento do ego, desejo de vingança e ajuda a um restaurante. Para isso, foram obtidas 252 respostas válidas e a modelagem de equações estruturais foi utilizada para testar o modelo proposto. Os resultados indicam que o controle comportamental percebido, as normas subjetivas, o envolvimento do ego e o desejo de vingança são preditores significativos da intenção de escrever avaliações online sobre restaurantes.

Title: How packaging affects the product preferences of children and the buyer behaviour of their parents in the food industry
Authors: Ogba I.E.; Johnson R.
Abstract: Purpose – Health is becoming an increasingly important issue in the UK as well as the rest of Europe. Emphasis on the importance of healthy eating is ongoing for many reasons, including the growing concern about childhood obesity resulting in the ban of advertising of unhealthy foods to children in the UK in April 2007. However, although legislation has been placed upon the advertising of unhealthy food products, no such restrictions have been placed on the packaging of children's foods despite the influence of packaging on consumer buyer decisions. This paper aims to investigate the effect of packaging on children's product preferences and its ability to influence parents' buyer decision in-store. Design/methodology/approach – The study was approached from the parents' rather than the children's perspective. A quantitative approach was adopted in data collection, using a 28 item Likert scaled questionnaire administered to 150 parents, with over 95 percent response rate. Findings – The study shows that packaging does affect the product preferences of children. Also, children are particularly interested in influencing the purchase of unhealthy foods. However, parents within the study claimed that they did not succumb to their children's requests for the purchase of unhealthy food, which contradicts evidence from previous findings. Research limitations/implications – The claim by parents that they did not succumb to their children's requests for unhealthy food contradicts findings from previous research. This therefore leads to a recommendation for further studies as social desirability bias may have influenced the outcomes of the findings. Practical implications – Findings from this study can be applied within the retail and service marketing sector to provide the practitioner with information relevant to decision making on children's influence on parents buyer behavior in-store. Outcomes of the study are also important when considering the future of children's food marketing and tackling the issue of childhood obesity. Originality/value – The paper demonstrates that there is a relationship between packaging and children product preferences and children's influence on parents' buyer decision in-store. © 2010, Emerald Group Publishing Limited
Keywords: Children (age groups); Consumer behaviour; Decision making; Food packaging; Parents; United Kingdom
rationale: The abstract discusses the influence of packaging on children's product preferences and how this affects parents' buying decisions. This ties to the understanding of customer emotions and the relational aspect of marketing, particularly the emotional influence that children have on their parents' purchasing behavior. The focus on emotional data and understanding customer needs aligns well with the Feeling AI category.
resumo: A saúde está se tornando uma questão cada vez mais importante no Reino Unido e na Europa, com ênfase na alimentação saudável devido à crescente preocupação com a obesidade infantil. Em abril de 2007, foi proibida a publicidade de alimentos não saudáveis para crianças no Reino Unido, mas não há restrições sobre a embalagem de alimentos para crianças, que influencia as decisões de compra. Este estudo investigou o efeito da embalagem nas preferências de produtos das crianças e sua capacidade de influenciar as decisões de compra dos pais. A pesquisa foi realizada com 150 pais, utilizando um questionário de 28 itens em escala Likert, com uma taxa de resposta superior a 95%. Os resultados mostraram que a embalagem afeta as preferências das crianças, que estão particularmente interessadas em influenciar a compra de alimentos não saudáveis. No entanto, os pais afirmaram que não cederam aos pedidos dos filhos por esses produtos, o que contradiz pesquisas anteriores. As limitações da pesquisa sugerem a necessidade de mais estudos, pois o viés de desejabilidade social pode ter influenciado os resultados. As implicações práticas são relevantes para o setor de marketing de varejo e serviços, fornecendo informações sobre a influência das crianças no comportamento de compra dos pais. O estudo é importante para o futuro do marketing de alimentos para crianças e para enfrentar a obesidade infantil. O artigo demonstra a relação entre embalagem e preferências de produtos das crianças, bem como a influência delas nas decisões de compra dos pais.

Title: Toward a model of sparkling wine purchasing preferences
Authors: Verdonk N.; Wilkinson J.; Culbert J.; Ristic R.; Pearce K.; Wilkinson K.
Abstract: Purpose: This paper aims to provide further insight into factors influencing Australian consumers’ purchasing preferences for sparkling wine, including champagne. Design/methodology/approach: Focus groups were conducted and thematic analysis was undertaken to identify factors influencing sparkling wine consumers’ purchasing preferences. Findings: Personal taste was found to influence choice of a sparkling wine rather than another type of beverage, and selection of a particular style and brand of sparkling wine. Country or region of origin was found to be important, often linked to the product being champagne. Brand image, reputation and symbolism were found to influence purchase decisions (sometimes linked to consumption occasion), especially for purchases of gifts. Advice, recommendations and expert reviews, and consumption occasion also were found to influence purchase decisions. Price was found to influence style and brand of sparkling wine purchased. A high price was found to be a barrier for some participants, while other participants were found to avoid sparkling wines priced below some particular level. Thematic analysis enabled development of a preliminary model of purchasing preferences. Research limitations/implications: Being exploratory in nature, findings cannot be generalised. Further studies are required to confirm the preliminary model and to evaluate the validity and significance of proposed relationships. Practical implications: Findings suggest a producer could benefit from marketing a range of sparkling wines to cater to different tastes, occasions and gift purchases. Findings also confirm the importance of marketers pursuing opportunities to obtain and promote favourable expert reviews for their sparkling wines, and of identifying and promoting regional distinctiveness. Originality/value: The first comprehensive model of sparkling wine consumers’ purchasing preferences has been developed. Empirical testing would enable refinement and enhance understanding. © 2017, © Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Australia; Consumer behaviour; Psychometric/qualitative; Survey research; Wines
keywords: ['personal taste', 'brand image', 'reputation', 'consumption occasion', 'gift purchases', 'expert reviews', 'customer preferences']
rationale: The abstract discusses various factors influencing purchasing preferences for sparkling wine, which includes understanding customer emotional needs and preferences such as personal taste, brand image, and the significance of the consumption occasion. These factors relate closely to customer understanding and positioning, which are key aspects of Feeling AI. The mention of gift purchases also ties into emotional engagement with customers. While there are elements that could relate to Mechanical or Thinking AI, the predominant focus on emotional and personal factors aligns it more closely with Feeling AI.
resumo: Este artigo tem como objetivo fornecer uma visão mais aprofundada sobre os fatores que influenciam as preferências de compra dos consumidores australianos em relação ao vinho espumante, incluindo o champanhe. Foram realizados grupos focais e uma análise temática para identificar esses fatores. Os resultados mostraram que o gosto pessoal influencia a escolha de um vinho espumante em vez de outra bebida, assim como a seleção de um estilo e marca específicos. O país ou região de origem é considerado importante, frequentemente associado ao produto ser champanhe. A imagem da marca, a reputação e o simbolismo também influenciam as decisões de compra, especialmente em compras de presentes. Recomendações, análises de especialistas e a ocasião de consumo também afetam as decisões de compra. O preço influencia o estilo e a marca do vinho espumante adquirido, sendo um preço elevado uma barreira para alguns participantes, enquanto outros evitam vinhos espumantes com preços abaixo de um determinado nível. A análise temática possibilitou o desenvolvimento de um modelo preliminar de preferências de compra. As limitações da pesquisa indicam que os resultados não podem ser generalizados, sendo necessárias mais investigações para confirmar o modelo preliminar e avaliar a validade das relações propostas. As implicações práticas sugerem que os produtores poderiam se beneficiar ao comercializar uma variedade de vinhos espumantes para atender a diferentes gostos, ocasiões e compras de presentes. Além disso, confirmam a importância de os profissionais de marketing buscarem oportunidades para obter e promover análises favoráveis de especialistas para seus vinhos espumantes e identificar a singularidade regional. Este estudo desenvolveu o primeiro modelo abrangente das preferências de compra dos consumidores de vinho espumante, e testes empíricos poderiam aprimorar e aprofundar a compreensão.

Title: The impact of outcome, competency and affect on service referral
Authors: Johnson M.; Zinkhan G.M.; Ayala G.S.
Abstract: Proposes a model to explain consumers' willingness to recommend a service provider. The model considers four predictors of this phenomenon: affect, outcome, competency and courtesy. In a laboratory setting, subjects read and responded to a scenario describing a service encounter of a fictitious individual with a dry cleaner and/or an attorney. The subjects were later asked how likely they were to recommend this service provider to a friend experiencing a similar problem. Separate path analyses were performed to analyze each type of service encounter; and in both scenarios, outcome, competency, courtesy, joy and disgust were found to influence the likelihood that the consumer would recommend a particular service provider. The proposed model accounts for more than 72 percent of the variation in the subjects' decision to recommend. © 1998, MCB UP Limited
Keywords: Consumer behaviour; Marketing strategy; Recommendations; Service quality; Services marketing
rationale: The abstract discusses a model that explains consumers' willingness to recommend a service provider, focusing on emotional factors such as joy and disgust as well as other predictors like affect and courtesy. This aligns closely with the 'Feeling AI' category, which emphasizes understanding customer emotions and needs. The analysis of emotional responses and their influence on recommendations indicates a strong focus on customer understanding and relationalization.
resumo: O artigo propõe um modelo para explicar a disposição dos consumidores em recomendar um prestador de serviços. O modelo considera quatro preditores: afeto, resultado, competência e cortesia. Em um ambiente de laboratório, os participantes leram e responderam a um cenário que descrevia um encontro de serviço com um lavador a seco e/ou um advogado. Posteriormente, foram questionados sobre a probabilidade de recomendar esse prestador de serviços a um amigo enfrentando um problema semelhante. Análises de caminho separadas foram realizadas para cada tipo de encontro de serviço; em ambos os cenários, resultado, competência, cortesia, alegria e desgosto influenciaram a probabilidade de o consumidor recomendar um prestador específico. O modelo proposto explica mais de 72% da variação na decisão dos participantes de recomendar.

Title: Homo economicus and social marketing: Questioning traditional models of behavior
Authors: Carvalho H.C.; Mazzon J.A.
Abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this paper is to bring forth the limitations of some important models of cognition and behavior adopted by social marketers and present important findings from recent lines of research that contribute to a fine-grained understanding of human behavior. Design/methodology/approach: This is a conceptual paper that presents a review of several theoretical approaches to human cognition and behavior and their implications regarding social marketing campaigns. Findings: It is concluded that the assumptions underlying traditional models of behavior need to be revised, especially the assumption that human beings are rational decision makers - the prototypical homo economicus. Behavioral science has revealed that people are far from being rational and are prone to be influenced by myriad factors, some deemed irrelevant under rational models. Social marketing interventions have greater probability of success when they rely on more realistic assumptions of human behavior. Research limitations/implications: Social marketing needs to embrace the contributions of the several disciplines and lines of research centered on the study of all facets of human behavior, such as behavioral economics and dual-system framework. Practical implications: The main implications are: the recommendation to assume people are running on their System 1 when they are in contact with social marketing campaigns, the need to consider the interplay of systems and selves over time, the recommended emphasis on place strategies, and the need to avoid cash incentives and silver bullets. Originality/value: The value of this paper is in contrasting the assumptions of traditional models of cognition and behavior widely used in social marketing with the evidence from several lines of research portraying influences in human behavior not accounted by those models. © Emerald Group Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Cognition; Consumer attitudes; Consumer behaviour; Social marketing; Social marketing theory; Theory of planned behaviour

This aligns with the Feeling AI category, as it focuses on customer understanding and emotional influences on decisions. resumo: O objetivo deste artigo é destacar as limitações de alguns modelos importantes de cognição e comportamento adotados por profissionais de marketing social e apresentar descobertas relevantes de pesquisas recentes que contribuem para uma compreensão mais detalhada do comportamento humano. Este é um artigo conceitual que revisa várias abordagens teóricas sobre cognição e comportamento humano e suas implicações para campanhas de marketing social. Conclui-se que as suposições subjacentes aos modelos tradicionais de comportamento precisam ser revisadas, especialmente a suposição de que os seres humanos são tomadores de decisão racionais - o protótipo do homo economicus. A ciência comportamental revelou que as pessoas estão longe de ser racionais e são suscetíveis a serem influenciadas por uma infinidade de fatores, alguns considerados irrelevantes sob modelos racionais. Intervenções de marketing social têm maior probabilidade de sucesso quando se baseiam em suposições mais realistas sobre o comportamento humano. O marketing social precisa abraçar as contribuições de várias disciplinas e linhas de pesquisa centradas no estudo de todas as facetas do comportamento humano, como a economia comportamental e a estrutura de sistemas duais. As principais implicações práticas incluem a recomendação de assumir que as pessoas estão operando em seu Sistema 1 ao entrarem em contato com campanhas de marketing social, a necessidade de considerar a interação de sistemas e identidades ao longo do tempo, a ênfase recomendada em estratégias de local e a necessidade de evitar incentivos em dinheiro e soluções simplistas. O valor deste artigo reside em contrastar as suposições dos modelos tradicionais de cognição e comportamento amplamente utilizados no marketing social com as evidências de várias linhas de pesquisa que retratam influências no comportamento humano não contabilizadas por esses modelos.

Title: Attitude toward smoking: The effect of negative smoking-related pictures
Authors: Grigaliunaite V.; Pileliene L.
Abstract: Research background: Endeavouring to develop healthy societies is a primary goal in many countries. As smoking is a major problem of public health, lowering the extent of smoking is one of the conditions for developing a healthy society. Based on the research revealing that the pairing of the product with negative stimuli enhances the possibility of negative reaction to the product as negative stimulus transfers it's meaning to the product, tobacco packaging was labelled with negative smoking-related pictures illustrating the danger of smoking. Nevertheless, the extent of smoking is still large in many countries. Hence, the effect of negative smoking-related pictures has been the subject of intense debate within the scientific community. Purpose of the article: The aim of this research is to determine the effect of negative smoking-related pictures on the both implicit and explicit attitude toward smoking. Methods: For the purpose of determining the effect of negative smoking-related pictures on the both implicit and explicit attitude toward smoking, Implicit Association Test and questionnaire survey were provided. The questionnaire was elaborated based on the analysis and synthesis of scientific literature. Findings & Value added: The theoretical analysis substantiated the influence of attitude toward the product on consumer purchase decisions. Nevertheless, people do not always want to reveal their opinion, hence traditional marketing research methods for measuring explicit attitude are not sufficient as they are often not objective. Therefore, neuromarketing research methods complement traditional marketing research methods by providing more objectivity. Consequently, the Implicit Association Test and traditional questionnaire research are applied for the empirical research, revealing the effect of negative smokingrelated pictures on the both implicit and explicit attitude toward smoking. The recommendations for the usage of negative smoking-related pictures on purpose to influence attitude toward smoking and consumer purchase behaviour are substantiated. © 2017 Nicolaus Copernicus University. All rights reserved.

resumo: O desenvolvimento de sociedades saudáveis é um objetivo primordial em muitos países, e a redução do tabagismo é fundamental para alcançar esse objetivo. A pesquisa indica que a associação de produtos a estímulos negativos pode aumentar a reação negativa a esses produtos. Assim, embalagens de tabaco foram rotuladas com imagens que ilustram os perigos do fumo. Apesar disso, o tabagismo ainda é prevalente em muitos lugares, gerando debates sobre a eficácia dessas imagens. Este estudo visa determinar o impacto dessas imagens negativas nas atitudes implícitas e explícitas em relação ao tabagismo, utilizando o Teste de Associação Implícita e questionários. A análise teórica confirmou que a atitude em relação ao produto influencia as decisões de compra, mas métodos tradicionais de pesquisa de marketing podem não ser objetivos, pois as pessoas nem sempre revelam suas opiniões. Portanto, métodos de neuromarketing complementam as pesquisas tradicionais, proporcionando maior objetividade. O estudo empírico revelou o efeito das imagens negativas sobre as atitudes em relação ao fumo e recomenda o uso dessas imagens para influenciar comportamentos de compra.

Title: A varietal-specific approach to investigate wine risk perception in South Africa: Recommendations for Chenin blanc
Authors: Van der Colff N.; Pentz C.; Nieuwoudt H.
Abstract: Purpose: This study aims to describe South African consumers’ wine risk perception on varietal level with recommendations for Chenin blanc. Design/methodology/approach: An exploratory mixed methods approach was followed where qualitative data were used to develop the questionnaire. Quantitative data were collected from 2,051 respondents using an online survey. ANOVA and Fischer least significance difference tests were used to indicate statistical significance. Findings: Significant perceived risks (PRs) associated with Chenin blanc across age and ethnic groups were functional, time and financial risks. Risk-reducing strategies (RRS) in the white wine category were favourite brands and a trusted store, while Sauvignon blanc was also described as an RRS. Recommended Chenin blanc RRS include tastings and events with food. Research limitations/implications: Measurement of PR remains challenging. This research approach can be reproduced and/or adapted to investigate other struggling varietals and/or regions-of-origin. The convenience sample limits generalisability. Practical implications: Segments were identified to develop new markets for Chenin blanc. RRS emphasise the importance of real sensory experience rather than media exposure to build knowledge and familiarity. Originality/value: This study is a pioneering endeavour in terms of using an exploratory mixed methods research approach to investigate and describe risk perception of a specific wine varietal. Recommendations, with implications for strategic marketing decisions, are made for South African Chenin blanc. © 2019, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Chenin blanc; Consumer behaviour; Consumer risk perception; Risk perception; South African white wine; Varietal perceived risk scale

resumo: Este estudo tem como objetivo descrever a percepção de risco dos consumidores sul-africanos em relação ao vinho Chenin blanc em nível varietal. Foi adotada uma abordagem mista exploratória, utilizando dados qualitativos para desenvolver um questionário e coletando dados quantitativos de 2.051 respondentes por meio de uma pesquisa online. Os testes ANOVA e Fischer foram utilizados para indicar significância estatística. Os riscos percebidos significativos associados ao Chenin blanc, variando entre grupos etários e étnicos, foram riscos funcionais, de tempo e financeiros. As estratégias de redução de risco na categoria de vinhos brancos incluíram marcas favoritas e lojas confiáveis, sendo o Sauvignon blanc também descrito como uma estratégia de redução de risco. As recomendações para estratégias de redução de risco do Chenin blanc incluem degustações e eventos com comida. As limitações da pesquisa incluem a dificuldade na medição da percepção de risco e a amostra de conveniência, que limita a generalização dos resultados. Segmentos foram identificados para desenvolver novos mercados para o Chenin blanc, enfatizando a importância da experiência sensorial real em vez da exposição à mídia para construir conhecimento e familiaridade. Este estudo é pioneiro ao utilizar uma abordagem mista exploratória para investigar e descrever a percepção de risco de um varietal específico de vinho, apresentando recomendações com implicações para decisões de marketing estratégico para o Chenin blanc sul-africano.

Title: Navigating the Digital Transformation of Commercial Banks: Embracing Innovation in Customer Emotion Analysis
Authors: Sun, YY; Zhang, Q
Abstract: The rapid development of science has ushered the society into the era of the digital economy, profoundly altering the habits and behaviors of empowered digital citizens. This transformation is particularly evident in the financial sector, where Internet companies have spearheaded the growth of Internet finance, offering non-professional, highly autonomous, cost-effective, and accessible financial services. Traditional banks face stiff competition from internal and cross-border rivals, compelling them to embark on digital transformation journeys to stay relevant. This research paper delves into the critical relationship between technology forecasting and social change, exploring the impact of gender imbalances on FinTech innovation. It also examines innovative e-commerce marketing models driven by big data and artificial intelligence, catalyzing advancements in the financial field. The digitalization of banks encompasses multiple facets, including decision-making, ecosystem development, channel optimization, process enhancement, data center construction, and infrastructure fortification. Central to this transformation is the understanding of customer emotions, a task made more intelligent through natural language processing (NLP) technology. We employ NLP techniques to analyze customer voice data and discern emotional states, including one-hot vector representation and Word2Vector models, alongside Bi-LSTM and attention processes. This approach significantly enhances our ability to tailor policies and products in real time, ensuring a more personalized customer experience. Also, the paper emphasizes the importance of establishing robust data governance systems, innovating talent development mechanisms, controlling digital risks, and optimizing customer acquisition strategies in the digital transformation journey. It also addresses the changing landscape of e-commerce architecture, highlighting the significance of logistical expertise and security considerations in international Internet sales. This research advances our understanding of how commercial banks can leverage technology and innovation to serve the real economy effectively. It provides valuable insights into the analysis of customer emotions and offers practical recommendations for achieving a seamless digital transformation.

resumo: O rápido desenvolvimento da ciência trouxe a sociedade para a era da economia digital, alterando profundamente os hábitos e comportamentos dos cidadãos digitais empoderados. Essa transformação é particularmente evidente no setor financeiro, onde empresas da Internet lideraram o crescimento das finanças digitais, oferecendo serviços financeiros não profissionais, altamente autônomos, econômicos e acessíveis. Os bancos tradicionais enfrentam forte concorrência de rivais internos e transfronteiriços, obrigando-os a embarcar em jornadas de transformação digital para se manterem relevantes. Este artigo de pesquisa investiga a relação crítica entre previsão tecnológica e mudança social, explorando o impacto dos desequilíbrios de gênero na inovação em FinTech. Examina também modelos inovadores de marketing de e-commerce impulsionados por big data e inteligência artificial, catalisando avanços no campo financeiro. A digitalização dos bancos abrange múltiplas facetas, incluindo tomada de decisões, desenvolvimento de ecossistemas, otimização de canais, aprimoramento de processos, construção de centros de dados e fortalecimento de infraestrutura. Central a essa transformação está a compreensão das emoções dos clientes, tarefa aprimorada pela tecnologia de processamento de linguagem natural (NLP). Empregamos técnicas de NLP para analisar dados de voz dos clientes e discernir estados emocionais, incluindo representação de vetor one-hot e modelos Word2Vector, juntamente com processos Bi-LSTM e de atenção. Essa abordagem melhora significativamente nossa capacidade de adaptar políticas e produtos em tempo real, garantindo uma experiência mais personalizada ao cliente. O artigo também enfatiza a importância de estabelecer sistemas robustos de governança de dados, inovar mecanismos de desenvolvimento de talentos, controlar riscos digitais e otimizar estratégias de aquisição de clientes na jornada de transformação digital. Além disso, aborda o cenário em mudança da arquitetura de e-commerce, destacando a importância da expertise logística e considerações de segurança nas vendas internacionais pela Internet. Esta pesquisa avança nossa compreensão de como os bancos comerciais podem alavancar tecnologia e inovação para servir efetivamente a economia real, oferecendo insights valiosos sobre a análise das emoções dos clientes e recomendações práticas para alcançar uma transformação digital sem costura.

Title: Understanding Consumer Perceptions About Smartwatches: Feature Extraction and Opinion Mining Using Supervised Learning Algorithm
Authors: Manayath D.; Kaladharan S.; Soman N.V.; Vijayakumaran A.
Abstract: Against the backdrop of increasing smartwatch usage and the dynamic landscape of evolving features, a nuanced understanding of consumer opinions and preferences is vital for tailoring features and crafting effective marketing strategies. This study addresses this imperative by conducting a comprehensive analysis of customer reviews on smartwatches, aiming to determine the pivotal factors guiding consumer purchasing decisions. By employing word clouds to visually represent sentiments, the study uncovers notable trends. Positive reviews prominently highlight the term “quality”, suggesting a strong emphasis on product excellence. In contrast, negative reviews were characterized by the prevalence of the term “fake”, indicating concerns related to authenticity. Additionally, a comparative assessment of two machine learning algorithms, namely support vector machines and Naive Bayes, demonstrates that support vector machines exhibit superior accuracy in classification. These findings offer valuable insights for industry practitioners navigating the competitive landscape of the smartwatch market, providing actionable information for optimizing product features and refining marketing strategies to meet consumer expectations. © 2024 by the author(s). Além disso, uma comparação entre dois algoritmos de aprendizado de máquina, máquinas de vetor de suporte e Naive Bayes, mostrou que o primeiro apresenta maior precisão na classificação. Os resultados oferecem insights valiosos para profissionais da indústria, ajudando na otimização de recursos e estratégias de marketing para atender às expectativas dos consumidores.

Title: A Semantic-Context Embedding Enhanced Attention Fusion BiLSTM: Unraveling Multilingual Sentiments in Product Reviews with Advanced Deep Learning
Authors: Purohit A.; Patheja P.S.
Abstract: For natural language processing (NLP), sentiment analysis (SA) is crucial since it helps to understand users' feelings and opinions in a variety of contexts. Even though Deep Learning (DL) techniques are becoming more popular in SA, effective model optimization can be difficult because they frequently call for a great deal of hyperparameter tuning. However, because current models can't sufficiently capture the variety of review contexts, it introduces bias and inaccuracies, especially in product reviews. For Multilingual Sentiment Analysis (MSA) in product reviews, this research proposed a Semantic-Context Embedding Enhanced Attention Fusion BiLSTM (SCEEAF-BiLSTM). The proposed model combines Continuous Bag-of-Word (CBoW) and Skipgram techniques to extract semantic context after the preprocessing stages of tokenization, stop word removal, and case normalization. A novel Convolutional BiLSTM with Enhanced Attention (CoBLEA) architecture is introduced for multilingual sentiment prediction to extract comprehensive context representations. The model ultimately shows efficacy in dividing multilingual sentiments into positive, neutral, and negative states, providing a viable method for complex SA in several circumstances. The outcome signifies that the proposed approach obtains a high accuracy attained 0.987, precision attained 0.985, recall attained 0.978 and F1-Score attained 0.986 when compared with prior works. With practical applications in sentiment-driven platforms operating in multiple languages, the research presents a method for complex SA in e-commerce, social media, and customer feedback systems. It also emphasizes the significance of comprehending multilingual opinions for enhancing marketing strategies, driving business decisions, and improving customer satisfaction. © 2024 The Authors.
Keywords: Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM); Convolution neural network (CNN); Embedding; Sentiment analysis; tokenization

resumo: A análise de sentimentos (AS) é fundamental para o processamento de linguagem natural (PLN), pois ajuda a entender os sentimentos e opiniões dos usuários em diversos contextos. Embora as técnicas de Aprendizado Profundo (AP) estejam se tornando mais populares na AS, a otimização eficaz dos modelos pode ser desafiadora devido à necessidade de ajuste de muitos hiperparâmetros. Modelos atuais não conseguem capturar adequadamente a variedade de contextos de avaliação, introduzindo viés e imprecisões, especialmente em avaliações de produtos. Para a Análise de Sentimentos Multilíngue (ASM) em avaliações de produtos, esta pesquisa propôs um modelo chamado Semantic-Context Embedding Enhanced Attention Fusion BiLSTM (SCEEAF-BiLSTM). O modelo combina técnicas de Continuous Bag-of-Word (CBoW) e Skipgram para extrair contexto semântico após as etapas de pré-processamento, como tokenização, remoção de stop words e normalização de casos. Uma nova arquitetura chamada Convolutional BiLSTM with Enhanced Attention (CoBLEA) é introduzida para a previsão de sentimentos multilíngues, extraindo representações de contexto abrangentes. O modelo demonstrou eficácia em classificar sentimentos multilíngues em estados positivos, neutros e negativos, apresentando um método viável para AS complexa em várias circunstâncias. Os resultados indicam que a abordagem proposta alcançou alta precisão de 0,987, precisão de 0,985, recall de 0,978 e F1-Score de 0,986 em comparação com trabalhos anteriores. Com aplicações práticas em plataformas orientadas a sentimentos que operam em múltiplas línguas, a pesquisa apresenta um método para AS complexa em e-commerce, redes sociais e sistemas de feedback de clientes, enfatizando a importância de compreender opiniões multilíngues para aprimorar estratégias de marketing, impulsionar decisões de negócios e melhorar a satisfação do cliente.

Title: COVID-19 vaccine rejection causes based on Twitter people’s opinions analysis using deep learning
Authors: Alotaibi W.; Alomary F.; Mokni R.
Abstract: According to the World Health Organization, vaccine hesitancy was one of the ten major threats to global health in 2019, including the COVID-19 vaccine. The availability of vaccines does not always mean utilization. This is because, people have less confidence in vaccines, which resulted in vaccination hesitancy and developing global decline in vaccine intake and has caused viral disease outbreaks worldwide. Therefore, there is a need to understand people’s perceptions about the COVID-19 vaccine to help the manufacturing companies of the vaccine to improve their marketing strategy based on the rejection causes. In this paper, we used multi-class Sentiment Analysis to classify people’s opinions from extracted tweets about COVID-19 vaccines, using firstly different Machine Learning (ML) classifiers such as Logistic Regression (LR), Stochastic Gradient Descent, Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Tree (DT), Multinomial Naïve Bayes, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting and secondly various Deep Learning (DL) models such as Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Long Short Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), RNN-LSTM and RNN-GRU. Then, we investigated the analysis of the negative tweets to identify the causes of rejection using the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) technique. Finally, we classified these negative tweets according to the rejection causes for all the vaccines using the same selected ML and DL models. The result of SA showed that DT gives the best performance with an accuracy of 92.26% and for DL models, GRU achieved 96.83%. Then, we identified five causes: Lack of safety, Side effect, Production problem, Fake news and Misinformation, and Cost. Furthermore, for the classification of the negative tweets according to the identified rejection causes, the LR achieved the best result with an accuracy of 89.97%. For DL models, the LSTM model showed the best result with an accuracy of 91.66%. © 2023, The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Austria, part of Springer Nature.
Keywords: COVID-19 vaccines; Deep learning; GRU-LSTM; Latent Dirichlet allocation; Sentiment analysis; Vaccine rejection causes

resumo: De acordo com a Organização Mundial da Saúde, a hesitação em relação às vacinas foi uma das dez principais ameaças à saúde global em 2019, incluindo a vacina contra a COVID-19. A disponibilidade de vacinas não garante sua utilização, pois a falta de confiança nas vacinas resultou em hesitação vacinal e um declínio global na adesão à vacinação, causando surtos de doenças virais em todo o mundo. Portanto, é necessário entender as percepções das pessoas sobre a vacina contra a COVID-19 para ajudar as empresas fabricantes a melhorar suas estratégias de marketing com base nas causas de rejeição. Neste estudo, utilizamos Análise de Sentimento multiclasse para classificar as opiniões das pessoas a partir de tweets extraídos sobre as vacinas contra a COVID-19, empregando inicialmente diferentes classificadores de Aprendizado de Máquina (ML) como Regressão Logística, Gradiente Estocástico, Máquinas de Vetores de Suporte, K-Vizinhos Mais Próximos, Árvore de Decisão, Naïve Bayes Multinomial, Floresta Aleatória e Aumento de Gradiente, e em seguida, vários modelos de Aprendizado Profundo (DL) como Rede Neural Recorrente, Memória de Longo e Curto Prazo, Unidade Recorrente Gated, RNN-LSTM e RNN-GRU. Investigamos a análise dos tweets negativos para identificar as causas de rejeição utilizando a técnica de Alocação de Dirichlet Latente (LDA). Finalmente, classificamos esses tweets negativos de acordo com as causas de rejeição para todas as vacinas usando os mesmos modelos selecionados de ML e DL. O resultado da Análise de Sentimento mostrou que a Árvore de Decisão teve o melhor desempenho com uma precisão de 92,26%, e para os modelos de DL, o GRU alcançou 96,83%. Identificamos cinco causas: Falta de segurança, Efeitos colaterais, Problemas de produção, Fake news e Desinformação, e Custo. Além disso, para a classificação dos tweets negativos de acordo com as causas de rejeição identificadas, a Regressão Logística obteve o melhor resultado com uma precisão de 89,97%. Para os modelos de DL, o modelo LSTM apresentou o melhor resultado com uma precisão de 91,66%.

Title: Aspect based sentiment analysis and smart classification in uncertain feedback pool
Authors: Kumar V.V.; Raghunath K.M.K.; Muthukumaran V.; Joseph R.B.; Beschi I.S.; Uday A.K.
Abstract: The data used in the opinion can be either factual or subjective, or both. The subjective form includes a positive or negative view, whereas there are facts in the objective form. As the result of opinion mining, the subjectivity and objectivity of knowledge are described as created. The outcome may be either positive or negative or a combination of both. Machine learning helps the computer to behave without a specific task being specifically programmed. Many consumers will critically evaluate everything online, especially food and amenities in eateries, to show their modest viewpoint. These views are critical in the decision-making process, especially in an uncertain feedback pool. Manually evaluating and deriving genuine opinions from these evaluations is very tough despite the growing count of opinions that are accessible in every category. So, to solve this issue, an automated methodology is needed. Sentiment evaluations or opinion extraction are returned methodologies to evaluate and identify uncertain feedback subjects as either positive or negative in these reviews. Three different dimensions of recommender systems are present; document-based, sentence-based, and aspect-based. Report and statement-based opinion mining concentrates on the broader orientation of the review and does not identify more accurately the crucial aspects of all the extracted reviews. The subject of trend is thus view-based opinion mining, and the emphasis of this research is on the restaurant's feedback sector. Creative marketing strategies are planned using sentiment assessments and opinion mining. The sentiment classifications are managed through a smart method called Neuro-Fuzzy Sentiment Classification. It is an entirely automated method of sentiment estimation and prediction. It can be used to group textual data and then used to identify patterns about the contents of the textual information. The resultant data aids in creating autonomous systems that consider the input from customers and prepare restaurant strategies. © 2021, The Society for Reliability Engineering, Quality and Operations Management (SREQOM), India and The Division of Operation and Maintenance, Lulea University of Technology, Sweden.

resumo: Os dados utilizados nas opiniões podem ser factuais ou subjetivos, ou ambos. A forma subjetiva inclui uma visão positiva ou negativa, enquanto a forma objetiva contém fatos. A mineração de opiniões descreve a subjetividade e a objetividade do conhecimento como criadas. O resultado pode ser positivo, negativo ou uma combinação de ambos. O aprendizado de máquina ajuda os computadores a agir sem uma tarefa específica programada. Muitos consumidores avaliam criticamente tudo online, especialmente alimentos e serviços em restaurantes, para expressar sua opinião. Essas opiniões são cruciais no processo de tomada de decisão, especialmente em um ambiente de feedback incerto. Avaliar manualmente e extrair opiniões genuínas dessas avaliações é muito difícil, apesar do crescente número de opiniões disponíveis em cada categoria. Portanto, uma metodologia automatizada é necessária. Avaliações de sentimento ou extração de opiniões são metodologias utilizadas para avaliar e identificar temas de feedback incertos como positivos ou negativos. A mineração de opiniões baseada em relatórios e declarações concentra-se na orientação geral da avaliação e não identifica com precisão os aspectos cruciais de todas as avaliações extraídas. Title: A social CRM analytic framework for improving customer retention, acquisition, and conversion

Abstract: Social Customer Relationship Management (social CRM) has become one of the central points for many companies seeking to improve their customer experience. Nonetheless, the inclusion of social media data in CRM introduces new challenges, as it requires advanced analytical approaches to extract actionable insight from such a huge amount of data. Thus, in this paper, we propose a social CRM analytic framework, which includes various analytical approaches, aiming at improving customer retention, acquisition, and conversion. This framework has been tested on various datasets and extensively evaluated based on several performance metrics. The obtained results suggest that the proposed framework can effectively extract relevant information and support decision-making processes. From an academics perspective, the study contributes to an understanding of customers’ experiences throughout their engagement on social media and focuses on long-term relationships with customers. From a managerial perspective, companies should leverage the insight generated through every customer engagement on social media to drive effective marketing strategies. © 2021

Assim, este artigo propõe uma estrutura analítica de social CRM, que inclui várias abordagens analíticas, visando melhorar a retenção, aquisição e conversão de clientes. Title: Over a decade of social opinion mining: a systematic review
Authors: Cortis K.; Davis B.
Abstract: Social media popularity and importance is on the increase due to people using it for various types of social interaction across multiple channels. This systematic review focuses on the evolving research area of Social Opinion Mining, tasked with the identification of multiple opinion dimensions, such as subjectivity, sentiment polarity, emotion, affect, sarcasm and irony, from user-generated content represented across multiple social media platforms and in various media formats, like text, image, video and audio. Through Social Opinion Mining, natural language can be understood in terms of the different opinion dimensions, as expressed by humans. This contributes towards the evolution of Artificial Intelligence which in turn helps the advancement of several real-world use cases, such as customer service and decision making. A thorough systematic review was carried out on Social Opinion Mining research which totals 485 published studies and spans a period of twelve years between 2007 and 2018. The in-depth analysis focuses on the social media platforms, techniques, social datasets, language, modality, tools and technologies, and other aspects derived. Social Opinion Mining can be utilised in many application areas, ranging from marketing, advertising and sales for product/service management, and in multiple domains and industries, such as politics, technology, finance, healthcare, sports and government. The latest developments in Social Opinion Mining beyond 2018 are also presented together with future research directions, with the aim of leaving a wider academic and societal impact in several real-world applications. © 2021, The Author(s).

Através da Mineração de Opinião Social, a linguagem natural pode ser compreendida em termos das diferentes dimensões de opinião expressas pelos humanos, contribuindo para a evolução da Inteligência Artificial e ajudando no avanço de vários casos de uso no mundo real, como atendimento ao cliente e tomada de decisões. Title: Arabic language sentiment analysis via cross-language translation
Authors: Alsheref F.K.
Abstract: Social platforms on the web give us a huge amount of data like comments, messages, products' reviews and posts. Sentiment analysis on social users' data is a valuable analysis for automatically understanding people's opinions about products or some interesting topics, and this analysis provides valuable information for informed decision making in different domains. Arab web users number is about 200 million users; this huge number represents the strong impact on marketing which makes the sentiment analysis of Arabic language hot topic. This paper proposed an Arabic sentiment analysis model to increase the accuracy of Arabic sentiment analysis. It is based on a cross-language retrieval model. The proposed model was tested on a dataset extracted from twitter and manually sentimentally classified by experts, and it achieved 90.62% accuracy. Copyright © 2019 Inderscience Enterprises Ltd.
Keywords: Cross-language; Facebook; Information retrieval correlation coefficient; Sentiment analysis; Social network service; Text mining; The social network; Twitter
rationale: The abstract discusses sentiment analysis, which is directly related to understanding customer opinions and emotions regarding products. resumo: As plataformas sociais na web fornecem uma grande quantidade de dados, como comentários, mensagens, avaliações de produtos e postagens. A análise de sentimentos nos dados dos usuários sociais é uma análise valiosa para entender automaticamente as opiniões das pessoas sobre produtos ou tópicos de interesse, oferecendo informações importantes para a tomada de decisões informadas em diferentes áreas. O número de usuários da web árabe é de cerca de 200 milhões, o que representa um impacto significativo no marketing, tornando a análise de sentimentos da língua árabe um tópico relevante. Este artigo propôs um modelo de análise de sentimentos em árabe para aumentar a precisão dessa análise, baseado em um modelo de recuperação de linguagem cruzada. O modelo proposto foi testado em um conjunto de dados extraído do Twitter e classificado manualmente por especialistas, alcançando uma precisão de 90,62%. Title: Social media analytics: Extracting and visualizing Hilton hotel ratings and reviews from TripAdvisor
Authors: Chang Y.-C.; Ku C.-H.; Chen C.-H.
Abstract: Analyzing and extracting insights from user-generated data has become a topic of interest among businesses and research groups because such data contains valuable information, e.g., consumers’ opinions, ratings, and recommendations of products and services. However, the true value of social media data is rarely discovered due to overloaded information. Existing literature in analyzing online hotel reviews mainly focuses on a single data resource, lexicon, and analysis method and rarely provides marketing insights and decision-making information to improve business’ service and quality of products. We propose an integrated framework which includes a data crawler, data preprocessing, sentiment-sensitive tree construction, convolution tree kernel classification, aspect extraction and category detection, and visual analytics to gain insights into hotel ratings and reviews. The empirical findings show that our proposed approach outperforms baseline algorithms as well as well-known sentiment classification methods, and achieves high precision (0.95) and recall (0.96). The visual analytics results reveal that Business travelers tend to give lower ratings, while Couples tend to give higher ratings. In general, users tend to rate lowest in July and highest in December. The Business travelers more frequently use negative keywords, such as “rude,” “terrible,” “horrible,” “broken,” and “dirty,” to express their dissatisfied emotions toward their hotel stays in July. © 2017 Elsevier Ltd
Keywords: Google trends; Hospitality; Natural language processing; Sentiment analysis; Social media analytics; TripAdvisor; Visual analytics
rationale: The abstract focuses on analyzing user-generated data, particularly sentiments expressed in hotel reviews. It seeks to understand customer emotions and opinions, highlighting how different customer segments (e.g., Business travelers vs. Couples) express their satisfaction or dissatisfaction. This aligns with the 'Feeling AI' focus on customer understanding and emotional needs.
resumo: Analisar e extrair insights de dados gerados por usuários tornou-se um tema de interesse para empresas e grupos de pesquisa, pois esses dados contêm informações valiosas, como opiniões, avaliações e recomendações de produtos e serviços. No entanto, o verdadeiro valor dos dados das redes sociais raramente é descoberto devido à sobrecarga de informações. A literatura existente sobre a análise de avaliações de hotéis online foca principalmente em uma única fonte de dados, léxico e método de análise, raramente fornecendo insights de marketing e informações para a tomada de decisões que melhorem o serviço e a qualidade dos produtos das empresas. Propomos uma estrutura integrada que inclui um rastreador de dados, pré-processamento de dados, construção de árvore sensível ao sentimento, classificação de núcleo de árvore convolucional, extração de aspectos e detecção de categorias, além de análises visuais para obter insights sobre avaliações e classificações de hotéis. Os resultados empíricos mostram que nossa abordagem proposta supera algoritmos de referência, bem como métodos conhecidos de classificação de sentimentos, alcançando alta precisão (0,95) e recall (0,96). Os resultados das análises visuais revelam que viajantes a negócios tendem a dar classificações mais baixas, enquanto casais tendem a dar classificações mais altas. Em geral, os usuários tendem a avaliar mais baixo em julho e mais alto em dezembro. Os viajantes a negócios usam com mais frequência palavras-chave negativas, como "rude", "terrível", "horrível", "quebrado" e "sujo", para expressar suas emoções insatisfeitas em relação às suas estadias em hotéis em julho.

Title: A fuzzy-oriented sentic analysis to capture the human emotion in Web-based content
Authors: Loia V.; Senatore S.
Abstract: Capturing the sentiments and the emotional states enclosed in textual information is a critical task which embraces a wide range of web-oriented activities such as detecting the sentiments associated to the product reviews, developing marketing programs that would be attractive for users, enhancing customer service with respect to its expectation until to identifying new opportunities and financial market prediction, besides managing reputations. Opinions and the emotions that are embedded in them, play a key role in decision-making processes, with different effects depending on the negative or positive valence of the mood. When the choice depends on some important features (i.e., time, money, reliability/efficacy, etc.) and on other opinions (which come from previous experience), could be crucial to make the best decision. Inferring opinions and emotions enclosed in the written language is a complex task which cannot rely on body languages (posture, gestures, vocal inflections), rather than discovering concepts with an affective valence. The role of opinions extracted by the social content is crucial to support consumers' decision process; in addition, thanks opinions and emotions, it is possible to evidence improvements on existing decision supports and show how the opinion-mining techniques can be incorporated into these systems. This paper presents a tentative contribution that addresses this issue: it introduces a framework for extracting the emotions and the sentiments expressed in the textual data. The sentiments are expressed by a positive or negative polarity, the emotions are based on the Minsky's conception of emotions, that consists of four affective dimensions, each one with six levels of activations [1]. Sentiments and emotions are modeled as fuzzy sets; particularly, the intensity of the emotions has been tuned by fuzzy modifiers, which act on the linguistic patterns recognized in the sentences. The approach has been tested on some sets of documents categories, revealing interesting performance on the global framework processing. © 2013 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.
Keywords: Decision making system; Fuzzy modifiers; Linguistic patterns; Sentic computing; Sentiment analysis; WordNet
rationale: The abstract focuses on extracting sentiments and emotions from textual data, highlighting their critical role in understanding customer needs and influencing decision-making processes. This aligns with the objectives of 'Feeling AI,' which emphasizes customer understanding and emotional analytics. The emphasis on emotional data to support decision-making processes and improve marketing strategies further strengthens this classification.
resumo: Capturar os sentimentos e estados emocionais contidos nas informações textuais é uma tarefa crítica que abrange uma ampla gama de atividades voltadas para a web, como detectar os sentimentos associados a avaliações de produtos, desenvolver programas de marketing atraentes para os usuários, aprimorar o atendimento ao cliente em relação às suas expectativas, identificar novas oportunidades e prever o mercado financeiro, além de gerenciar reputações. As opiniões e emoções que estão embutidas nelas desempenham um papel fundamental nos processos de tomada de decisão, com efeitos diferentes dependendo da valência negativa ou positiva do humor. Quando a escolha depende de características importantes (como tempo, dinheiro, confiabilidade/eficácia, etc.) e de outras opiniões (que vêm de experiências anteriores), pode ser crucial para tomar a melhor decisão. Inferir opiniões e emoções contidas na linguagem escrita é uma tarefa complexa que não pode depender da linguagem corporal (postura, gestos, inflexões vocais), mas sim da descoberta de conceitos com uma valência afetiva. O papel das opiniões extraídas do conteúdo social é crucial para apoiar o processo de decisão dos consumidores; além disso, graças às opiniões e emoções, é possível evidenciar melhorias nos suportes de decisão existentes e mostrar como as técnicas de mineração de opinião podem ser incorporadas a esses sistemas. Este artigo apresenta uma contribuição tentativa que aborda essa questão: introduz um framework para extrair as emoções e os sentimentos expressos nos dados textuais. Os sentimentos são expressos por uma polaridade positiva ou negativa, as emoções são baseadas na concepção de emoções de Minsky, que consiste em quatro dimensões afetivas, cada uma com seis níveis de ativação. Sentimentos e emoções são modelados como conjuntos fuzzy; particularmente, a intensidade das emoções foi ajustada por modificadores fuzzy, que atuam nos padrões linguísticos reconhecidos nas frases. A abordagem foi testada em alguns conjuntos de categorias de documentos, revelando um desempenho interessante no processamento do framework global.

Title: A social CRM analytic framework for improving customer retention, acquisition, and conversion
Authors: Lamrhari S.; Ghazi H.E.; Oubrich M.; Faker A.E.
Abstract: Social Customer Relationship Management (social CRM) has become one of the central points for many companies seeking to improve their customer experience. It comprises a set of processes that allows decision-makers to analyze customer data, in order to launch an efficient, customer-centric, and cost-effective marketing strategy. Nonetheless, the inclusion of social media data in CRM introduces new challenges, as it requires advanced analytical approaches to extract actionable insight from such a huge amount of data. Thus, in this paper, we propose a social CRM analytic framework, which includes various analytical approaches, aiming at improving customer retention, acquisition, and conversion. This framework has been tested on various datasets and extensively evaluated based on several performance metrics. The obtained results suggest that the proposed framework can effectively extract relevant information and support decision-making processes. From an academics perspective, the study contributes to an understanding of customers’ experiences throughout their engagement on social media and focuses on long-term relationships with customers. From a managerial perspective, companies should leverage the insight generated through every customer engagement on social media to drive effective marketing strategies. © 2021
Keywords: Acquisition; Conversion; Customer retention; Customer satisfaction; Machine learning; Sentiment analysis; Social CRM; Social media
rationale: The abstract emphasizes the importance of understanding customer experiences and engagement on social media, which aligns with the focus on customer understanding and relationalization in Feeling AI. The proposed framework aims to improve customer retention and acquisition by leveraging insights from customer interactions, indicating an emotional and relational approach to marketing.
resumo: O gerenciamento de relacionamento com o cliente social (social CRM) tornou-se um ponto central para muitas empresas que buscam melhorar a experiência do cliente. Ele envolve um conjunto de processos que permite aos tomadores de decisão analisar dados dos clientes para lançar uma estratégia de marketing eficiente, centrada no cliente e econômica. No entanto, a inclusão de dados de mídias sociais no CRM traz novos desafios, exigindo abordagens analíticas avançadas para extrair insights acionáveis de grandes volumes de dados. Assim, este artigo propõe uma estrutura analítica de social CRM, que inclui várias abordagens analíticas, visando melhorar a retenção, aquisição e conversão de clientes. Essa estrutura foi testada em diversos conjuntos de dados e amplamente avaliada com base em várias métricas de desempenho. Os resultados obtidos sugerem que a estrutura proposta pode extrair informações relevantes e apoiar processos de tomada de decisão. Do ponto de vista acadêmico, o estudo contribui para a compreensão das experiências dos clientes durante seu engajamento nas mídias sociais e foca em relacionamentos de longo prazo com os clientes. Do ponto de vista gerencial, as empresas devem aproveitar os insights gerados em cada engajamento do cliente nas mídias sociais para impulsionar estratégias de marketing eficazes.

Title: Aspect based sentiment analysis and smart classification in uncertain feedback pool
Authors: Kumar V.V.; Raghunath K.M.K.; Muthukumaran V.; Joseph R.B.; Beschi I.S.; Uday A.K.
Abstract: The data used in the opinion can be either factual or subjective, or both. The subjective form includes a positive or negative view, whereas there are facts in the objective form. As the result of opinion mining, the subjectivity and objectivity of knowledge are described as created. The outcome may be either positive or negative or a combination of both. Machine learning helps the computer to behave without a specific task being specifically programmed. Many consumers will critically evaluate everything online, especially food and amenities in eateries, to show their modest viewpoint. These views are critical in the decision-making process, especially in an uncertain feedback pool. Manually evaluating and deriving genuine opinions from these evaluations is very tough despite the growing count of opinions that are accessible in every category. So, to solve this issue, an automated methodology is needed. Sentiment evaluations or opinion extraction are returned methodologies to evaluate and identify uncertain feedback subjects as either positive or negative in these reviews. Three different dimensions of recommender systems are present; document-based, sentence-based, and aspect-based. Report and statement-based opinion mining concentrates on the broader orientation of the review and does not identify more accurately the crucial aspects of all the extracted reviews. The subject of trend is thus view-based opinion mining, and the emphasis of this research is on the restaurant's feedback sector. Creative marketing strategies are planned using sentiment assessments and opinion mining. The sentiment classifications are managed through a smart method called Neuro-Fuzzy Sentiment Classification. It is an entirely automated method of sentiment estimation and prediction. It can be used to group textual data and then used to identify patterns about the contents of the textual information. The resultant data aids in creating autonomous systems that consider the input from customers and prepare restaurant strategies. © 2021, The Society for Reliability Engineering, Quality and Operations Management (SREQOM), India and The Division of Operation and Maintenance, Lulea University of Technology, Sweden.
Keywords: Accuracy; Aspect-based; Classification; Document-based; Machine learning; Opinion mining; Sentenced-based; Sentiment analysis; Uncertain feedback pool

rationale: The abstract discusses the use of sentiment analysis and opinion mining to understand customer feedback, particularly in the restaurant sector. It emphasizes the importance of understanding customer emotions and opinions, which aligns with the Feeling AI category. The methodologies mentioned aim to gauge customer sentiment and incorporate it into marketing strategies, indicating an understanding of customer emotional needs.
resumo: Os dados utilizados nas opiniões podem ser factuais, subjetivos ou ambos. A forma subjetiva inclui uma visão positiva ou negativa, enquanto a forma objetiva contém fatos. A mineração de opiniões descreve a subjetividade e objetividade do conhecimento como criadas, resultando em opiniões que podem ser positivas, negativas ou uma combinação de ambas. O aprendizado de máquina permite que os computadores atuem sem uma programação específica. Os consumidores avaliam criticamente tudo online, especialmente alimentos e serviços em restaurantes, o que é crucial no processo de tomada de decisão. Avaliar manualmente e extrair opiniões genuínas dessas avaliações é desafiador, exigindo uma metodologia automatizada. A extração de sentimentos ou opiniões é uma abordagem para avaliar e identificar feedback incerto como positivo ou negativo. Existem três dimensões de sistemas de recomendação: baseados em documentos, frases e aspectos. A mineração de opiniões baseada em relatórios e declarações foca na orientação geral da avaliação, sem identificar aspectos cruciais. A pesquisa se concentra na mineração de opiniões sobre feedback de restaurantes. Estratégias de marketing criativas são planejadas usando avaliações de sentimentos e mineração de opiniões, geridas por uma técnica chamada Classificação de Sentimentos Neuro-Fuzzy, que é totalmente automatizada. Essa técnica agrupa dados textuais e identifica padrões, ajudando a criar sistemas autônomos que consideram o feedback dos clientes e elaboram estratégias para restaurantes.

Title: COVID-19 vaccine rejection causes based on Twitter people’s opinions analysis using deep learning
Authors: Alotaibi W.; Alomary F.; Mokni R.
Abstract: According to the World Health Organization, vaccine hesitancy was one of the ten major threats to global health in 2019, including the COVID-19 vaccine. The availability of vaccines does not always mean utilization. This is because, people have less confidence in vaccines, which resulted in vaccination hesitancy and developing global decline in vaccine intake and has caused viral disease outbreaks worldwide. Therefore, there is a need to understand people’s perceptions about the COVID-19 vaccine to help the manufacturing companies of the vaccine to improve their marketing strategy based on the rejection causes. In this paper, we used multi-class Sentiment Analysis to classify people’s opinions from extracted tweets about COVID-19 vaccines, using firstly different Machine Learning (ML) classifiers such as Logistic Regression (LR), Stochastic Gradient Descent, Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Tree (DT), Multinomial Naïve Bayes, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting and secondly various Deep Learning (DL) models such as Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Long Short Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), RNN-LSTM and RNN-GRU. Then, we investigated the analysis of the negative tweets to identify the causes of rejection using the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) technique. Finally, we classified these negative tweets according to the rejection causes for all the vaccines using the same selected ML and DL models. The result of SA showed that DT gives the best performance with an accuracy of 92.26% and for DL models, GRU achieved 96.83%. Then, we identified five causes: Lack of safety, Side effect, Production problem, Fake news and Misinformation, and Cost. Furthermore, for the classification of the negative tweets according to the identified rejection causes, the LR achieved the best result with an accuracy of 89.97%. For DL models, the LSTM model showed the best result with an accuracy of 91.66%. © 2023, The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Austria, part of Springer Nature.
Keywords: COVID-19 vaccines; Deep learning; GRU-LSTM; Latent Dirichlet allocation; Sentiment analysis; Vaccine rejection causes
rationale: The abstract discusses understanding people's perceptions and emotions towards the COVID-19 vaccine, which aligns with the focus on customer understanding and using emotional data to comprehend existing and potential customer needs. The analysis of negative sentiments and identification of causes for vaccine hesitancy further emphasizes the emotional aspect of consumer behavior, linking it closely to the Feeling AI category.
resumo: De acordo com a Organização Mundial da Saúde, a hesitação em relação às vacinas foi uma das dez principais ameaças à saúde global em 2019, incluindo a vacina contra a COVID-19. A disponibilidade de vacinas não garante sua utilização, pois a falta de confiança nas vacinas resultou em hesitação vacinal e um declínio global na aceitação das vacinas, causando surtos de doenças virais em todo o mundo. Portanto, é necessário entender as percepções das pessoas sobre a vacina contra a COVID-19 para ajudar as empresas fabricantes a melhorar suas estratégias de marketing com base nas causas de rejeição. Neste estudo, utilizamos Análise de Sentimento multi-classe para classificar as opiniões das pessoas a partir de tweets extraídos sobre vacinas contra a COVID-19, empregando inicialmente diferentes classificadores de Aprendizado de Máquina (AM) como Regressão Logística, Gradiente Estocástico, Máquinas de Vetores de Suporte, K-Vizinhos Mais Próximos, Árvore de Decisão, Naïve Bayes Multinomial, Floresta Aleatória e Gradiente Boosting, e em seguida, vários modelos de Aprendizado Profundo (AP) como Rede Neural Recorrente, Memória de Longo e Curto Prazo, Unidade Recorrente Gated, RNN-LSTM e RNN-GRU. Investigamos a análise dos tweets negativos para identificar as causas de rejeição utilizando a técnica de Alocação de Dirichlet Latente (LDA). Finalmente, classificamos esses tweets negativos de acordo com as causas de rejeição para todas as vacinas usando os mesmos modelos selecionados de AM e AP. O resultado da Análise de Sentimento mostrou que a Árvore de Decisão apresentou o melhor desempenho com uma precisão de 92,26%, enquanto para os modelos de AP, o GRU alcançou 96,83%. Identificamos cinco causas: Falta de segurança, Efeitos colaterais, Problema de produção, Fake news e Desinformação, e Custo. Além disso, para a classificação dos tweets negativos de acordo com as causas de rejeição identificadas, a Regressão Logística obteve o melhor resultado com uma precisão de 89,97%. Para os modelos de AP, o modelo LSTM apresentou o melhor resultado com uma precisão de 91,66%.

Title: Understanding Consumer Perceptions About Smartwatches: Feature Extraction and Opinion Mining Using Supervised Learning Algorithm
Authors: Manayath D.; Kaladharan S.; Soman N.V.; Vijayakumaran A.
Abstract: Against the backdrop of increasing smartwatch usage and the dynamic landscape of evolving features, a nuanced understanding of consumer opinions and preferences is vital for tailoring features and crafting effective marketing strategies. This study addresses this imperative by conducting a comprehensive analysis of customer reviews on smartwatches, aiming to determine the pivotal factors guiding consumer purchasing decisions. By employing word clouds to visually represent sentiments, the study uncovers notable trends. Positive reviews prominently highlight the term “quality”, suggesting a strong emphasis on product excellence. In contrast, negative reviews were characterized by the prevalence of the term “fake”, indicating concerns related to authenticity. Additionally, a comparative assessment of two machine learning algorithms, namely support vector machines and Naive Bayes, demonstrates that support vector machines exhibit superior accuracy in classification. These findings offer valuable insights for industry practitioners navigating the competitive landscape of the smartwatch market, providing actionable information for optimizing product features and refining marketing strategies to meet consumer expectations. © 2024 by the author(s).
